title: Tack-Tile
name: Tack-Tile
one_line: Paid digital archive of 6,753 scanned paper ephemera, 1780-1980, with a no-AI pledge.

look.type: Uppercase Red Hat Mono 13px, wide-tracked, for all copy; giant wordmark in a variable dot typeface whose letters are built from overlapping black circles.
look.color: White ground, black ink, hairline black rules; one vermilion (#ce3d20) square as the only colour, plus near-black (#14161a) login buttons.
look.layout: Three-column strapline band between full-width rules, wordmark left, credits right; text accordions stacked below; footer in three columns; huge empty white below.
look.imagery: No images on the landing; the dot wordmark and a circular-text 'free sample' badge around a red square carry it.

behaviour: React SPA (the live page shows an empty shell); accordion questions open with arrows; log-in gate; mousemove and drag code hint at an interactive wordmark (unclear).
signature: Dotted wordmark: each letter is a loose scatter of black circles, like ink dabs, above rigid all-caps mono text.
why: One loose, tactile display face against a rigid mono grid separates the archive's subject (handmade, imperfect paper) from its apparatus (catalogued, exact), and the pledge in the strapline gives the site a stance.
steal: Pair one irregular display face with a strictly tracked mono caps text system, and put your stance ('made by humans, for humans') in a three-column band under the header.
moves: circular text badge around one red square

title: Tender Effect
name: Tender Effect
one_line: Weekly collective tarot reading read on a tiny phone screen floating over a full-bleed photo collage.

look.type: 11px monospace text on the phone's white screen with a blue link and red spellcheck squiggle; Libre Caslon Condensed declared elsewhere.
look.color: Violet, teal and near-black photo layers with a soft white vignette; acid-green buttons bottom-left; black phone shell.
look.layout: One small centred object (the phone) over a full-viewport collage; two buttons pinned bottom-left; nothing else on the page.
look.imagery: Layered, inverted botanical photographs blurred at the edges; a photo-real slide-out QWERTY phone cut-out.

behaviour: Weekly text scrolls inside the phone screen; custom image cursors and a float animation in CSS; RSS button pushes the readings to your phone; 10 KB total.
signature: Reading a tarot forecast on a nostalgic QWERTY slider phone, then offering the RSS feed 'on ur smartphone': the wink is the device mismatch.
why: A tiny text window inside a huge image makes the reading feel like a message received, not a page; the object frame supplies the tone, so the type can stay plain mono and the code tiny.
steal: Frame text inside a photographed or cut-out object (phone, card, receipt) on a full-bleed image ground, and keep the text itself plain monospace.
moves: text inside a cut-out phone screen

title: Trademarks & Symbols Vol. 2, Kuwayama: 1,504 Marks · symbools
name: symbools: Trademarks & Symbols Vol. 2, Kuwayama
one_line: All 1,504 marks from a 1973 trademark book, searchable by chapter, with counts, shuffle and a density toggle.

look.type: Newsreader (variable, light, high-contrast) for the 48px title, big numerals and search; Inter Tight for UI; tiny tracked caps for labels.
look.color: Warm paper #faf5f2 ground with ink #18190f; tiles #f2ebe6; one rose red (#e11d48) echoing the red book jacket; marks are pure black.
look.layout: Fixed left sidebar of 26 chapters with counts; right pane: rounded hero card with book cover and four stats, then search, then 7-column tile grid.
look.imagery: 1,504 black glyph-like marks on rounded tinted tiles, each numbered; the book's red jacket photo as the one colour image.

behaviour: Instant search with a '/' key hint, three grid densities, shuffle, chapter filtering; marks download as SVG/PNG. React SPA; CSS reduced-motion support.
signature: Hero card pairing the book's red jacket with four light-serif stats (1,504 marks, 725 designers, 1,142 companies, 30 countries) under tiny-caps captions.
why: The interface behaves like a well-made reference book: big light numerals, one accent taken from the object, chapter counts as wayfinding. Archive tools are added without competing with the marks.
steal: Take your single accent colour from the archived object itself (here the red book cover), let ink-on-paper neutrals carry everything else, and put counts beside every category.
moves: accent colour lifted from the archived book jacket
search field with '/' shortcut and density toggle

title: esoteric yellow pages - TUO TUO
name: esoteric yellow pages - TUO TUO
one_line: A tongue-in-cheek classified directory of tarot readers, astrologers and healers, laid out like a phone-book page.

look.imagery: Textured grey paper-photograph background and one gold line illustration of fanned pins above an open book; no other images.

why: Borrowing a trusted, boring format lets the humour and the community listing share one page; rules and a single serif keep it scannable, and the texture adds atmosphere.
steal: Pick a mundane print genre (yellow pages, classifieds, menu), reproduce its ruled-entry layout exactly, then let the content subvert it.

title: Tidelands 2100 | Homepage
name: Tidelands 2100
one_line: Landing for an immersive narrative world set in Potters Pond, Rhode Island, in 2100, with live tide and distance readouts.

look.type: Wordmark in a thin monoline custom face (~240px, peach) cropped at both edges; Space Mono caps at ~13px for readouts.
look.color: Deep navy-teal video ground, peach wordmark, acid-green (#aeff00) HUD text and outlines; difference blend elsewhere.

signature: A bottom-right HUD that reports the live tide state and your distance from Potters Pond, as if 2100 were already broadcasting.
why: Real-time data (UTC clock, tide, your distance) pulls speculative fiction into the present; oversized cropped type over video sets cinematic scale before any text must be read.
steal: Add a three-line monospace HUD in one neon colour to a video hero: live clock, one world-state value, and the visitor's distance from the place.
moves: live HUD: UTC clock, tide state, miles from place
wordmark cropped by the viewport edges
neon-green mono player pinned in a corner

title: Typedifferent - BD Ambient

name: FK Raster Grotesk | Florian Karsten Typefaces

steal: Make the first screen of a type page a single word at maximum width on a flat tinted ground, with the controls as small Helvetica text above.

variable-axis sliders (pixels, joints) in the tester
tiny Helvetica nav against huge type

title: Texturelib - free texture library
name: Texturelib - free texture library

name: The Work of Harald Peter Ström

name: Screen Slate

one violet for every non-content element

steal: Start an essay low on the first screen, leave the top two-thirds empty, and use only two type sizes: small bold caps for metadata, one large serif for the opening.

boxed corner nav with justified text breaking INF/O

title: FogCam archive and backup · every frame of the world’s oldest webcam · Fog-Bank
name: Fog-Bank: FogCam archive and backup
one_line: Archive and live viewer of every frame from FogCam, the world's oldest webcam (since 1994), as a forensic dashboard.

look.type: IBM Plex Mono at 10-12px for nearly all labels and readouts; Space Grotesk for nav and the big temperature; the camera's own red-orange timestamp.
look.color: Near-black navy panels; amber (#ffb454) for active state and charts, green (#57cc8a) for live, teal and coral as data hues.

look.imagery: The original FogCam frame with its burnt-in overlay; RGB histogram curves, amber bar charts, pixel-art moon with stars.

why: Obsessive specificity turns a low-res webcam into a place you can study; dense mono labels, one amber accent and consistent cards keep a dozen widgets legible, and the frame stays the hero.
steal: When archiving a stream, derive a few honest metrics per frame (motion, brightness, sharpness) and plot them beside the player as tiny labelled charts in one accent colour.
moves: per-frame forensic metrics beside the player
waveform-style scrub bar of frame sizes
weather and moon phase at the lens
keyboard shortcut legend under the player

look.color: White canvas, black photo frames and tags, translucent grey cones, pale blue-grey header band, one red FA logo square, tan and green key-word highlights.
look.layout: Near-blank map canvas in the capture: three framed photos placed around pins, text cards floating between, title and stepper pinned to the top.
look.imagery: Satellite and drone photographs in thick black frames, each linked to its map location by a translucent wedge.

behaviour: Step-through story: arrows and a '12 of 20' dropdown move between frames, each rearranging photos and text on a Mapbox base; today behind a Cloudflare 403.
signature: Translucent grey cones fan from a tiny lettered pin to a framed photograph, so every image is visibly anchored to a place.
why: Leader lines make evidence spatial: readers see where each image was taken and how views relate. Highlighted key words inside the text cards tie each claim to its image.
steal: Anchor each image to its subject with a thin translucent wedge or leader line and a letter, instead of a caption below.
moves: cone leaders from pin to photo
'n of N' stepper in the header

title: Trekker / Browser
name: Trekker / Browser (Occupant Fonts)
one_line: Type specimen for Dispatch 2 and Stainless 2: drag a central lens to reshape eight surrounding panels.

look.type: Stainless, a sans derived from the Dispatch slab, at 16-20px; labels wrapped in { curly braces }; asterisk-like dingbats on the spokes.
look.color: Slate blue-grey panels on a light grey ground; cream-white labels and hairlines; one pale grey lens rectangle.
look.layout: 3x3 grid of cells around a draggable centre lens with arrows at its corners; panel corners curve inward where they meet.
look.imagery: No images: rounded panels, a white disc, hairline spokes and small dingbats.

behaviour: A draggable lens ('drag me', blinking corner arrows) appears to drive the grid, cells reflowing around it; Perlin-noise script and designer-made sounds are loaded.
signature: A pale 'drag me' lens at the centre of slate panels whose corners curve inward where they meet.
why: The specimen is an instrument: the type is experienced by moving the page, not read about. Concave joins and hairline spokes give the panels a machined, plated look that suits an industrial slab.
steal: Replace the type-tester text field with one draggable control that visibly reshapes the whole layout; add sound and blinking arrows so people know to grab it.
moves: draggable lens as the only control

title: mallacht ár líne
name: mallacht ár líne
one_line: Ritual page: someone is thinking of you; a glass spiral; an 'ask the holy well' button.

look.type: Astloch, a quill-like display face, for the pale grey title (a 288px size exists in CSS); Times New Roman ~14px for the sentence.
look.color: Near-white with a faint mint wash at lower right; text in washed grey-green; sage-grey pill button with a white label.
look.layout: One centred column on a single screen: title, sentence, soft-edged round image, pill button, with generous empty ground.
look.imagery: A soft-focus photograph of a glass dish with a spiral, feathered into a circle so it dissolves into the page.

behaviour: Figma Sites build, JS-rendered, noindex. Page title now reads 'mallacht ár líne' versus 'na mallachtaí' in the capture; the button presumably draws an answer from the well.
signature: A one-line message that the visitor is being thought of turns an empty page into an act of care.
why: Low contrast, one object and one verb make the page an offering rather than a product. Fading type to near the ground colour pulls attention inward; the button is a ritual action, not navigation.
steal: Give a one-screen page one object and one ritual verb button ('ask...'), and fade all text to just above the ground colour.
moves: ritual verb as the only button

title: Bookmarklet
name: Bookmarklets (Poetic Web)
one_line: Bookmarklet showcase: nine drag-to-bookmark pills, each over a solid blue slab of its JavaScript, under an ASCII landscape title.

look.type: Book serif in blue: ~80px title, ~15px centred intro; code in 9-10px mono, white on blue; three serif nav words across the top.
look.color: One royal blue for type, pill outlines, ASCII art and code slabs, on pure white.
look.layout: Nav spread left, centre, right; title over ASCII art; intro; then a 3x3 grid of pill-over-slab cards.
look.imagery: ASCII-art skyline in blue monospace behind the title; the code slabs are the only other pictures.

behaviour: Drag each underlined pill to the bookmarks bar to install it; a converter and a tutorial are linked; the page now returns 404.
signature: The JavaScript itself sits in view, in solid blue rounded slabs under each outlined pill, so code is ornament as well as payload.
why: Showing the source makes the tool legible and teachable. One hue stops dense code reading as noise, and the pill outline marks what is draggable.
steal: Show the payload of every tool: put the code or recipe in a solid brand-colour block under its title, small mono, white on the brand hue.
moves: three-point nav spread across the top

title: Andrew Pierre Hart.com
name: Andrew Pierre Hart.com
one_line: Sound-painter's WordPress portfolio opening on a full-screen photo of a projected poem in a dark gallery.

look.type: Libre Franklin bold caps, widely tracked, for the title; 13px semibold nav; the projected poem is a mono face with some words enlarged.
look.color: Near-black greens and charcoals from the photo, a mint-white projection rectangle, white title, one blue current-page link.
look.layout: Theme hero: photo fills the first screen, avatar and caps title low left, a menu bar docked along the bottom, scroll arrow at right.
look.imagery: One dim gallery photograph: a pale block of projected text on a dark wall; tiny speaker photo beside the title.

behaviour: Standard WordPress theme: dropdown menu, scroll-down arrow, then galleries, video and five audio players; masonry and swiper scripts, RSS.
signature: The hero is documentation of the work itself, a projected poem about sound, so the template inherits the artist's subject.
why: A stock theme works when its one big slot holds a real piece of the practice. Darkness, low saturation and one pale rectangle make the artwork the only bright thing on screen.
steal: In a template with a full-screen header, fill it with a documentation photograph of the actual work and keep the title white, bold and small.

title: sophism
name: sophism
one_line: A founder-blogger's chaotic homepage: default Times, scrolling banner, multi-column jokes, coloured interest words and collapsible questions.

look.type: Browser-default Times at mixed sizes; scrolling banner ~20px; bold coloured serif interests ~25px; a monospace message box.
look.color: White page, default blue links, each interest phrase in its own flat colour (green, crimson, navy, purple); olive banner text, cyan name.
look.layout: Row of unequal columns (bio, links, photo, caps jokes, message box), then overlapping headings and a numbered list with disclosure triangles.
look.imagery: A few casual photos and screenshots; two triskelion glyph images in the banner; three canvas elements for effects.

behaviour: Scrolling letter-by-letter banner; 14 details toggles open each question; the textarea sends on Enter; canvas, WebGL shader and mouse scripts run.
signature: A homepage as stream of consciousness: unaligned columns, overlapping headings and a message box that sends on Enter.
why: With no design vocabulary beyond browser defaults, personality is left to the voice. Colour is used only to mark content, one hue per interest, never decoration.
steal: Use native details elements for lists of open questions, give each phrase one flat colour for emphasis, and let columns be uneven.

title: To be a Technologist is to be Human - Letters to a Young Technologist
name: Letters to a Young Technologist
one_line: Essay series with a sidebar of five letters and a large light-serif title over a wide reading column.

look.type: Book text serif ~15px at about 1.5 leading; display title ~48px light weight; sidebar numbered list in the same serif.
look.color: Off-white page, near-black text, indigo links; the current letter and its numeral in raspberry pink.
look.layout: Two columns: ~190px left rail with site title and numbered list; ~680px article column with the big title offset to the right.
look.imagery: None; type only.

behaviour: Static essay pages on GitHub Pages; the saved essay URL now returns a 404, so only the capture remains.
signature: The current letter is marked by turning its link and number pink, the only hot colour on the page.
why: Colour-coded location in a numbered contents list teaches order without icons. A book-size serif under a huge light title reads as printed essay, which signals slow reading.
steal: Put the table of contents in a left rail as a numbered list and recolour the current item; set body at 15px serif, 1.5 leading.

title: Dennis King - Láithreáin Ghaeilge
name: Dennis King - Láithreáin Ghaeilge
one_line: Irish-language links page on linen, with mint banner bars, a green pill, bold blue Verdana titles and indented descriptions.

look.type: Verdana 19px throughout; bold blue link titles over plain black descriptions; italic blue sign-off; tiny grey datestamp.
look.color: Linen ~#faf0e6 ground, mint ~#66dd99 bars, dark-green pill with yellow label, default-style blue links, green rules.
look.layout: Left-aligned list, each title above an indented line; a second list boxed between green rules; mint bar repeated top and bottom.
look.imagery: A tiny flag icon in the bar and a small arrow icon at top right; otherwise text only.

behaviour: Static 2008-era page, no JavaScript; link hover and focus styles; the old host now redirects to teanga.info.
signature: A mint home bar with a dark-green 'Donncha' pill, repeated at the top and the foot of an academic-server page.
why: Plain structure of bold link then one explanatory line scales to any language, and the coloured bars are the only branding. The hierarchy is honest: where it goes, what you get.
steal: List destinations as a bold link on one line with a single sentence beneath, and bracket the page with a coloured bar at top and bottom.

title: The Botanical Mind
name: The Botanical Mind
one_line: Camden Art Centre's online exhibition: a white title over a green-toned night photograph of a gnarled tree under stars.

look.type: Light grotesk in white: ~44px centred title, 3-line address top left at ~20px, 12px menu top right with underlined current page.
look.color: Duotone dark green and black photograph, white type; a coral #f0523d accent appears elsewhere in the CSS.
look.layout: Full-bleed hero photo, title centred just below middle, address and menu pinned to the top corners (Squarespace fluid layout).
look.imagery: Moonlit tree silhouette against a star field, tinted green; later sections carry commissions, podcasts and sacred-geometry art.

behaviour: Squarespace site with chapters, new commissions, podcasts and playlists; scroll animations, blend modes and clip-path effects in the CSS; 1.3 MB of CSS.
signature: One tinted night-sky photograph holds the whole home screen; the only other elements are an address block and a tiny menu.
why: A tonal photograph matched to the subject (trees as cosmic axis) sets mood faster than any layout; white light-weight type needs no box on a dark duotone.
steal: Tint one photograph to a single hue, run it full-bleed, centre a white light-weight title on it, and pin the address and menu to the corners in small type.
moves: address block used as the logo

title: After - Official Band Website
name: After - Official Band Website
one_line: Band site rebuilt as a 2000s media-player skin: lime blur-streak ground, album art, brushed-metal tour list and glass player.

look.type: Heavy geometric lowercase logotype ~80px; wide-set Aeonik nav in white; Aeonik Mono credit line; tiny caps in pill buttons; a pixel face is loaded.
look.color: Chartreuse-to-lime gradient with horizontal motion streaks and translucent white circles; glossy blue player, grey brushed-metal panel, magenta strip on the cover.
look.layout: Centred 800px stage: logo, album cover left with tour/news tabs right, full-width player bar, nav row, tiny credit; cart pill fixed bottom right.
look.imagery: Album art of a blurred train window with snowflake stickers; dot and circle patterns; glossy Spotify and Apple Music icons.

behaviour: Player UI with play, prev/next, scrub and volume; TOUR and NEWS tabs; ticket buttons; Next.js with drag and mouse scripts.
signature: Every control is a glossy hardware-style pill or key, from ticket buttons to transport, lit like Windows Media Player circa 2005.
why: Full commitment to one interface period, down to bevels and highlights, makes ordinary band content (dates, player, cart) feel like a found artefact; the skeuomorphism serves function, not decoration.
steal: Pick one period's interface idiom (a 2005 media player) and rebuild the real controls in it: bevelled pills, inset panels, glossy sliders, a streaked gradient ground.
moves: credit line for the site builder

title: Operate
name: Operate
one_line: Sales-CRM launch page drawn as a green technical document: a chaos-to-clarity dot field framed by brackets and a rotated spine.

look.type: Geist Mono ~12-14px for labels and brackets; Denim and Cinetype for headings; rotated spine text for Document A, date and name.
look.color: One hue: mid green paper with #117025 dark-green ink for every line, dot and label; a single violet 'We're Hiring' sticker.
look.layout: Square sheet framed by rounded bracket corners labelled Chaos (left) and Clarity (right); vertical dotted rules; spine strip at left; small card top right.
look.imagery: Generative scatter of circles, asterisks and suns on vertical dotted lines, disordered at left and aligned at right; paper grain.

behaviour: A pause button implies the field animates, circles drifting from scatter into rows; Next.js; today the copy and sections were rewritten but the green identity persists.
signature: The pitch is a diagram: scattered circles on dotted rules resolving from Chaos to Clarity inside a printed-document frame.
why: The whole argument is made as one drawing in one ink, so the page needs almost no copy. Document-sheet details (spine label, date stamp, brackets) turn a SaaS landing page into an artefact.
steal: Express the product's value as a single diagram in one ink colour, and frame it like a document sheet: spine label, date, bracketed axis labels.
moves: rotated spine strip with document number
round sticker as the call to action

title: RWO
name: Rietlanden Women's Office (RWO)
one_line: Feminist art office: scanned zine spreads tiled edge to edge, one flat green italic text box centred.

look.type: Times-style italic ~17px, centred, asterisk dividers between items; the scans carry book serifs, drop caps and wavy ornamental borders.
look.color: Cream and vermilion red from the scans, black ink; one flat saturated green box that clashes on purpose.
look.layout: 2x2 mosaic of full-width spread scans fills the screen; a ~400px square green box sits dead centre over the seams.
look.imagery: Photocopied feminist periodical spreads (Mukti, Triple Jeopardy): ornamental frames, a portrait, dense columns, in red and cream.

behaviour: Static single page, now answering 403 Forbidden; underlined italic links lead to publications, selected works and readings.
signature: A flat, unstyled-looking green rectangle of italic text dropped onto a wall of ornamented zine scans.
why: The raw box is a deliberate foil to the ornament beneath, enacting the 'ornamental' theme the text announces. Politics and address stay readable on a fully busy ground.
steal: Over a busy archival collage, place one solid-colour rectangle with centred text and asterisk dividers; the flatness keeps the text readable and the collage visible.

title: Commercial Type » Catalog
name: Commercial Type Catalog
one_line: Foundry catalogue: each family is a full-width row set in its own face, plus filter chips and pinned test strip.

look.type: Styrene UI for chrome at ~13px; family names at ~90px in their own faces; grey 12px centred blurbs; root font size set in vw units.
look.color: White ground, black hairlines; nav as black keycap chips with white text; filter chips pale blue #e2f2ff; black cart button.
look.layout: Two-row header (nav chips, filter chips), then stacked bordered rows: style count and icons on top, giant name, blurb below.
look.imagery: None; the type specimens are the images.

behaviour: Filter by category, optical size, weight, effect, OpenType and language; pin families to a test strip; a 'Type it...' field retypes every specimen; ~1,900 buttons.
signature: The family name set at hero size in its own face fills each row, so browsing the catalogue is already reading specimens.
why: Specimen-as-label removes the gap between description and evidence; hairline rows give rhythm; filters by optical size and weight speak a type designer's vocabulary rather than a shop's.
steal: In a catalogue, render each item's name in the item itself at hero size on a hairline-ruled row; keep filters in a quiet tinted chip bar above.
moves: name set in its own typeface

title: CSS Layout Generator
name: CSS Layout Generator
one_line: CSS Grid and Flexbox generator whose home is a gallery of pictogram cards, one per layout template.

look.type: Inter 13.8px throughout; bold section label; rotated 'Grid' and 'Flexbox' side labels; uppercase 'ABOUT' at top right.
look.color: Warm greige #ecebdf ground, charcoal #333 pictograms and text, taupe-grey card borders; brick red #bc3b38 is in the CSS but unseen here.
look.layout: Header rule, then rows of equal rounded cards (six per row) in two groups, each card a pictogram above its name; hairline between groups.
look.imagery: Flat charcoal block pictograms drawn as the layout they name: holy grail, sidebar, rows, 12-span grid.

behaviour: Pick a template, then edit a visual grid or flex layout and copy the code; Next.js with drag and keyboard handling; plausible analytics.
signature: Layout presets are shown as tiny solid-block diagrams of themselves, so the menu doubles as documentation.
why: A chooser made of pictograms is faster than names; consistent charcoal-on-greige keeps a dozen diagrams comparable. The tool starts from outcomes (shapes), not CSS vocabulary.
steal: For any tool with presets, show each preset as a solid-block pictogram in a bordered card with a one-line name beneath, on a warm neutral ground.
moves: rotated group labels in the margin

title: Gesture Systems®
name: Gesture Systems
one_line: Design studio index: one 12px type size, lime chips, and varied-size project tiles of 3D and motion work.

look.type: TWK Continental at one size, 12px: bold caps captions with smaller bold discipline tags; the studio blurb runs the full width.
look.color: White page, black text, acid lime #b4ee00 for the studio chip and New tags, grey #e4e4e4 menu chips; the projects supply all other colour.
look.layout: Tiles of mixed widths and heights on a loose grid, captions left-aligned beneath; four across on the first row, three on the second.
look.imagery: Blurred gradient placeholders resolving to 3D renders and motion: a pink gel blob, pixel cursor icons, chrome shards on black.

behaviour: 16 muted looping videos autoplay in tiles; hover states; Nuxt/Vue with drag, mouse and scroll listeners; blurred previews while media loads.
signature: A single 12px size for everything, with lime chips as the only interface colour, so the work is the loudest thing.
why: Constraint as system: one size and one accent leave nothing competing with the renders. Mixed tile sizes give rhythm without needing headings or dividers.
steal: Set all UI text at one small size, use one accent for labels (New, menu chip), and size project tiles variably so layout carries the hierarchy.

title: Radio Gardening Summer School
name: Radio Gardening Summer School
one_line: Are.na-fed internet radio for a summer school: three blurred round 'Listen in' stations above a pill-block schedule timeline.

look.type: IBM Plex Mono 12-16px throughout; title in a thin, wobbly handwritten-italic caps face in brown, stacked on three lines.
look.color: Sage ground (~#c5d1c5), brown ink, butter-yellow (~#fbee83) for buttons and the live programme block, pale-yellow outlines, blue slider thumbs.
look.layout: Title top left, pill links top right; three circles evenly spaced mid-screen; schedule strip with day label and ticker pinned to the bottom.
look.imagery: Three blur-filtered circular photographs (hands, tote-bag print, walkie-talkie) acting as channel covers.

behaviour: Three audio streams with play buttons and volume sliders; schedule pulled from Are.na with a 'now' marker; announcement ticker; cursor-follow and drag scripts.
signature: A schedule drawn as outlined pill blocks on a time axis, the current programme filled butter-yellow, with a red 'now' line.
why: Time becomes shape: block length equals show length, one filled block equals now. Soft blur and warm sage make a live service feel like a garden rather than a dashboard.
steal: Draw a schedule as outlined pill blocks on a time axis, fill only the live one in the accent colour, and add a red 'now' hairline.

title: Concrete Form
name: Concrete Form
one_line: A form poem (The HTML Review): its lines are spread across hundreds of form controls, opening on an ASCII envelope.

look.type: Times New Roman ~12-14px for the instruction line and poem fragments; dashed ASCII lines in light grey draw the envelope.
look.color: White with black and mid-grey text; colour appears only through the form's own colour-picker and file inputs.
look.layout: Centred object: a ~420px ASCII envelope under one instruction line; later screens break the poem into word-sized pieces interleaved with inputs.
look.imagery: ASCII line-art envelope; later a photo-upload field and a colour field; 24 images and one audio track in the markup.

behaviour: Arrow buttons page through 100+ sections; real controls (radio, checkbox, range, colour, file, time) are answered to continue; uses location, clock and localStorage for 'save progress'.
signature: A poem whose stanzas are form fields: asking whether you are human or want to save progress becomes radio buttons you must answer.
why: The medium's bureaucratic grammar (forms, consent, submit)…'s subject, so the interface is the meaning. Default controls, styled by nothing, stay cold and exact.
steal: Use native form controls as literary or structural material: let readers answer radios and sliders to advance, and leave the controls unstyled.
moves: questions that need answers to continue
reader's time and place pulled in

title: Century-Scale Storage
name: Century-Scale Storage
one_line: Long essay on storing data for 100 years, with eight p5 sketches (punch cards, vases, discs) and a decay overlay.

look.type: Newsreader serif throughout: light ~38px hero question, tiny chapter nav; pixel-font numerals 7 to 1 down the centre.
look.color: Near-black with a fine dot-matrix texture and white type; the sticky chapter nav uses an exclusion blend so it inverts over any section.
look.layout: Hero splits the question: top-left clause, bottom-right clause, pixel number line down the middle; essay sections follow below.
look.imagery: Generative p5 canvases per storage medium: number line, vase grid, face grid, magnetic core, punch card, conveyor, disk, Rosetta.

behaviour: Scroll-driven chapters with a sticky exclusion-blend nav; a fixed full-viewport decay canvas overlays the page; eight p5 sketches run inside the text.
signature: A 16,000-word essay interrupted by small generative machines, each one a storage medium you can watch fail or persist.
why: Each argument gets its own demonstration, so the essay is both read and run. A black ground, one serif and bitmap digits make the century time scale visible from the first screen.
steal: For long-form, embed one purpose-built sketch per section, keep one serif and a sticky blend-mode nav, and open with a typographic hero staging the central question.

title: url.town
name: url.town
one_line: A hand-built web directory presented as a town: default HTML, a population counter, categories as three-column link lists.

look.type: Times New Roman at 1.2em; bold underlined category headings; comma-separated subcategory links; emoji in the 'Latest addition' legend.
look.color: Default white page, black text and #0000ee blue underlined links; dotted black box edge; orange cones in the construction GIF.
look.layout: Centred header (barricade GIF, title, nav, search), a rule, then a three-column grid of categories with centred text.
look.imagery: A 3D-rendered 'under construction' barricade GIF with cones and a beacon, straight from the 1990s.

behaviour: Search, random link, stats, login and submissions; the headline population grows as members add sites (466 in the capture, 974 now).
signature: The page title is the live head-count: 'Welcome to url.town, population N'.
why: A civic metaphor gives a dull link list a voice and a growth stat; default HTML styling suits link-heavy content and loads instantly, so the community's contributions are the design.
steal: Give a directory a place-name and a headline number, show the latest addition in a dotted-border legend box, and leave links in default blue.
moves: latest addition in a legend box

title: jon photographs.
name: jon photographs.
one_line: Photographer's index in one signal green on white: three header items and a three-column project table, no images.

look.type: Neue Haas-style grotesk (Diatype stack) ~16px bold; PROJECT, TYPE, DATE column heads in caps; links with hairline underlines.
look.color: Pure white with every glyph in #14d206 signal green; nothing else.
look.layout: Header trio across the top (bio, email, 'work.'); table mid-screen with right-aligned project names meeting left-aligned type and date columns.
look.imagery: None on the landing screen; photographs live behind each project link.

behaviour: Cargo site; each project row opens an image set; scroll listener present; otherwise static.
signature: A whole site in one flat green: the right-aligned project column forms a ragged spine down the middle of the page.
why: One saturated hue is a complete identity for a photographer because it will not compete with the photographs behind the links; a table scans for type and year faster than a thumbnail grid.
steal: Open a photography site with a text table (project, type, year) in one saturated colour, and let images appear only after a click.
moves: header trio of bio, email, work

title: May 25th, 2025
name: May 25th, 2025
one_line: One photograph of a May 2025 wall calendar, overlaid with blended leaf-shadow video and ambient music.

look.type: No interface type; only the calendar's own printed 'MAY 2025' and tiny weekday headers inside the photograph.
look.color: Khaki-greige #d6d1bf ground; shadow video blended with colour-burn and multiply; warm brown photo tones.
look.layout: Full-viewport single photograph: a small spiral calendar hung at top centre, the rest an empty wall of shadow.
look.imagery: Photo of a wall calendar showing two cowboy-hatted men embracing; dappled foliage-shadow video laid over the whole screen.

behaviour: Calendar photo has a pointer cursor (likely starts sound); a muted shadow video is layered twice with multiply and colour-burn blends; autoplay audio element; SvelteKit with Tailwind.
signature: A video of moving leaf shadows is blended over a photograph of a calendar, as if sunlight were crossing the real wall.
why: The date is the work, so the page is one object and one atmosphere. Blend modes fuse video and photo into a single light, which makes the calendar feel physically present.
steal: Layer a looping shadow or light video over a still photo using mix-blend-mode multiply and color-burn so a flat image acquires a time of day.

title: all form forms time / falls on the body
name: all form forms time / falls on the body
one_line: A divinatory Are.na mood tracker: a calendar of every day of a year, each cell coloured by what you saved.

look.type: Times New Roman, tiny: one italic disclosure label bottom right; the rest of the interface is the grid itself.
look.color: Lilac-to-periwinkle ramp (#e5e5f7 to #837bed, ink #1d1549) named thaw/frost/freeze, written with OKLCH relative colours and a display-p3 fallback.
look.layout: Full-viewport grid of square day cells, about 19 across and down, 1px light gutters; a small details panel fixed bottom right.
look.imagery: No images: each cell fills like a bar with vertical gradients per saved block, darker where more was added.

behaviour: Reads any Are.na channel through the API, finds dates in block titles and text, layers years, toggles types/years legend, zoom, animation and erase; source on GitHub.
signature: Every day of a year as one lilac square, filled by how much you saved that day, with years stacked for comparison.
why: One hue, one unit and a tiny control panel turn a data feed into a reflective instrument; the dedication and 'divinatory' framing make a tracker poetic rather than clinical.
steal: Visualise personal data as a plain grid of equal cells in one hue ramp with a small collapsible control panel, and name palette variables after the metaphor.
moves: palette variables named thaw and frost
controls tucked in a details panel
Are.na channel as the data source

title: S A L L Y T H U R E R
name: Sally Thurer (old site)
one_line: Designer's old portfolio: four checkbox nav items, a bio paragraph, and a pile of overlapping image cut-outs.

look.type: Fugue geometric sans ~25px bio in black with blue underlined links; caps nav ~20px beside hand-ticked checkbox icons.
look.color: White page, black text, link blue; all colour comes from pasted posters, 3D renders and a lime slime logo.
look.layout: Centred nav row on top; bio in a left column; images stack down and across over the text, rotated and shadowed like a desk pile.
look.imagery: Magazine cover, posters, 3D bodies, a bulldog in sunglasses, a winged TV on a thread, browser-window screenshots, GIFs.

behaviour: Nav items are checkboxes (Work and About ticked in the capture) that appear to toggle sections; jQuery drag and mouse scripts; five GIFs; a winged-TV toy on a thread.
signature: Navigation as checkboxes: ticking Work and About together lays the image pile over the bio text.
why: Toggles make navigation additive, not exclusive, so layers can overlap; soft drop shadows keep each cut-out legible in the pile. The designer's maximalism is the portfolio.
steal: Make nav items real checkboxes that show or hide layers so visitors can stack sections, and give every pasted image a soft drop shadow so overlaps stay readable.

title: Devouring Details
name: Devouring Details
one_line: Interaction-design reference manual (20 chapters then, 23 now) sold from a white sheet with an orange ruler.

look.type: Custom 'dd'grotesk ~18px at 1.75 leading, stacked…'REGISTER NOW' tag; tiny serif labels on the dial.
look.color: Pale grey page, white sheet, black text, one orange (#ff5a00) for logo dot, hairline and tag; grey dial.
look.layout: 800px white sheet on grey: logo dot left, nav list right, two-column intro text, rounded demo panel; ruler ticks in the left margin.

why: Instrument-like chrome (ruler, hairline, dial) shows the author's craft in the container before any chapter. One orange accent and generous leading let the motion demos carry the page.
steal: Prove craft in the chrome: add a measurement ruler and one accent hairline, set body at 18px with 1.75 leading, and let short muted videos do the demonstrating.

one_line: A research dictionary whose home is one flowing sentence of terms, each with thumbnail and count, sorted by weight.

look.type: Aileron (a Helvetica-like grotesk) ~26px for terms with grey superscript counts; unreferenced terms in lighter grey.
look.color: Black on white with a hairline header; weight shown by grey tone: black terms with images, mid-grey for unlinked terms.
look.layout: Terms wrap inline like a paragraph with 24px thumbnails before each; three full-width collapsible rows (Search, Rhizome, Timeline) below.
look.imagery: Tiny thumbnails (book covers, film stills, portraits) inline before terms, acting as icons for concepts.

behaviour: jQuery site; click a term to see its sources; Search, Rhizome and Timeline panels fold open from ruled rows; keyboard shortcuts present.
signature: A tag cloud rewritten as prose: terms ordered by count, each with a thumbnail and tiny superscript, inline like words in a sentence.
why: Sorting by weight and showing counts as superscripts gives the research agenda at a glance without charts; keeping terms inline preserves reading rhythm and lets images work as punctuation.
steal: Render an index as a paragraph: sort by frequency, add superscript counts and tiny thumbnails inline, and grey out unlinked terms.
moves: tag cloud as running text sorted by weight

title: Meditation Journal Entries (Chronological) | Jhana8
name: Meditation Journal Entries - Jhana8
one_line: A meditation teacher's chronological journal index: WordPress page with leaf logo, green links and decades of dated entries.

look.type: System sans (DejaVu/Verdana-like) 16px body; light ~34px page title; green underlined links; headings in the same face at 26-30px.
look.color: White page, dark grey text, one leaf green for links, search button and logo.
look.layout: Centred ~880px column: heading block, centred nav, search, then h2/h3 sections with bullet lists of dated entry links.
look.imagery: A leaf logo; no photos in view; the page is text and links.

behaviour: WordPress with search form, RSS and expandable index sections; each entry links to its own journal post; an 'Abhinna' index sits alongside.
signature: A 25-year private practice kept as a dated, linkable list of first-person entries, each with a plain one-line summary.
why: The one-sentence annotation after each link (what happened, when) makes a long diary navigable, and the plain template stays out of the way of the testimony.
steal: Index a long diary as era headings with bullets: link title, dash, date and a one-sentence summary of the oddest thing in the entry.

title: Source Type: Index
name: Source Type: Index
one_line: A type foundry's alphabetical index of references: Times-set entries mixing essays, images and jokes, plus a Clippy cookie banner.

look.type: Huge light Times-style 'Index' ~90px; entries in letterspaced Times New Roman 15px; A-Z sans letters in a rounded black pill.
look.color: Off-white (#f5f5f5) with black type and black pills; the only colour is a yellow Windows-95 dialog and the images.
look.layout: Three-column free flow of entries at unequal heights: apple silhouette, essay paragraphs, map images; A-Z pill nav at top; big title above.
look.imagery: A black apple silhouette (Enzo Mari), brick-pattern pixel art, a grainy satellite image; a hand-drawn line mark top left.

behaviour: Vue + GSAP + Three.js site; letters filter the index; the cookie banner is a Windows 95 dialog with Clippy; 3.1MB payload with 3D and sound libraries.
signature: The cookie notice is a Windows 95 dialog spoken by Clippy: 'Welcome to Source Type! Accept cookies?…'.
why: A calm, letterspaced Times ground lets wildly mixed entries (an apple, a river, an acronym) sit as equals, and one comic intrusion shows the foundry's humour without disturbing it.
steal: Replace the cookie banner with a period-UI joke in your brand's tone, and keep the rest of the page quiet so the gag has room.
moves: Times with open letterspacing as house voice
entries mixing image, essay and definition at equal weight

title: Color of the Pandemic | Broadcast
name: Color of the Pandemic - Pioneer Works Broadcast
one_line: An arts-publication feature: ten artists name their pandemic colour on Pantone-style chips inside a rounded black panel.

look.type: Heavy tight display title ~64px; Times subtitle ~24px; bold Helvetica-style labels with HEX codes on chips; spaced-caps 'COMPILATION'.
look.color: Page tinted pale aqua per article; black panel; ten swatches (cardboard, ultraviolet, teal, green screen, yolk...).
look.layout: Thin masthead and ruled sub-nav, centred headline, a 5x2 chip grid inside a 28px-radius black card, black pill ticker pinned at the bottom.
look.imagery: Paper-textured colour chips shaped like Pantone cards: swatch above, white label below with name, contributor and hex.

behaviour: Next.js; per-article background colour and display face by CSS variables; a looping ticker pill 'Print Issue 02: Now Available' pinned at the bottom can be closed.
signature: Pantone's chip format as the editorial…' colours of the pandemic, each with a name and hex code.
why: Borrowing a familiar object (the colour chip) makes a list of personal answers instantly legible and comparable; the page changes colour per story, so the publication feels curated, not templated.
steal: Make each article's page colour and headline typeface variables, and borrow a familiar printed object (chip, label, ticket) as the unit for list content.
moves: per-article background colour and display face
rounded black panel framing the set
ticker pill with a close box

title: Nokia Design Archive
name: Nokia Design Archive
one_line: A browsable archive of Nokia's design process as a network of 722 entries, with a timeline view and topic filters.

look.type: Monospace 11-13px for all UI; heavy extended grotesk for the title; node labels tinted by topic.
look.color: Near-black UI; topics coded orange, red, blue and teal; a lime (#c5ee44) Accept pill and indigo (#5252ff) selected state.
look.layout: Left control rail (view type, keyword search, topic radios, date histogram) and a full-height network canvas running past the right edge.
look.imagery: Grey dots joined by faint links, coloured hub labels; the capture is dimmed by an onboarding modal.

behaviour: D3 force graph on canvas with zoom +/-, drag and hover; Network/Timeline switch; histogram range slider filters 1992-2014; 7-step welcome tour; cookie bar.
signature: Archive as galaxy: 722 documents float as a dot network whose hubs are design topics, filterable by a date histogram.
why: The first view already shows the archive's shape and scale, and a persistent filter rail lets people carve it down; the dark mono UI keeps colour for data only.
steal: Give a large archive a network or timeline view as its front door, colour-code topics, and add a short onboarding tour of five to seven steps.
moves: numbered onboarding tour in a modal

title: Roc Camera
name: Roc Camera
one_line: Product page for a camera that certifies real photos: white single-screen hero, isometric line-drawn camera, dot-matrix italic type, lime accent.

look.type: Dot-matrix italic display (Mono45 Headline) for title, button and footer; Frutiger Light tagline ~20px; italic serif FAUST mark.
look.color: White ground, black line art, one acid lime (#b0cf00) for 'Roc' and the PREORDER outline, one red shutter button.
look.layout: Centred stack on a single screen (title, camera, tagline, button), footer links in two corners, a 7-dot pager at the right edge.
look.imagery: Isometric outline drawing of the camera with a single red button; later sections use product renders and photos.

behaviour: Astro + Alpine; scroll-snapped sections with a right-edge dot pager; dialog for pre-order; variable-font weights; reduced-motion respected.
signature: A viewfinder-LCD dot-matrix italic for the product name, paired with a thin outline drawing, so type and object share one language.
why: Using the one red element (the shutter button) against a white, lime and black page makes the camera the focal point; hardware-like type tells the story before any copy is read.
steal: Set the product name and buttons in a typeface that echoes the product's own display, limit the palette to white, black and one acid accent, and use red once.
moves: single red shutter button as the only red
right-edge dot pager with scroll snap

title: Design for the Time Being
name: Design for the Time Being
one_line: Design-essay series: contents list one word per line in a narrow serif column; empty blue-grey field; a single black dot.

look.type: HK Serif ~16px, italic for credits, wrapped one word per line in a ~90px column; Common Sans for notes.
look.color: Flat blue-grey (#cfd6de) ground, black type; the About overlay inverts to black with blue-grey text; one black dot.
look.layout: A 90px text column hugging the left edge and a vast empty field; the black dot floats at the right edge as the sole control.
look.imagery: None on the first screen; essay pages hold 30em-wide images.

signature: A table of contents narrowed until it becomes a poem: Design / and / Design Designs, one word per line.
why: Radical emptiness and a deliberately narrow column turn titles into rhythm and give each essay a blank field to arrive in; the single dot is the whole interface.
steal: Constrain a contents list to a 90px column so titles break one word per line, and leave the rest of the screen empty.
moves: contents column forced to one word per line
one black dot as the only control
About as an inverted full-screen overlay

title: Mira Joyce
name: Mira Joyce
one_line: A writer's one-column page (Jan 2025): name,…'Open World' line.

look.type: Helvetica 14px at tight leading, all lowercase, hard line breaks, one italic indented quotation; name set at the same size.
look.color: Pure white and black; today's version adds five Apple system colours (red, yellow, green, blue, purple), likely for hover.
look.layout: A ~230px text column hugging the left edge; the remaining 75% of the viewport is blank; date and poem stack below a dash divider.
look.imagery: None; it is a poem.

behaviour: Static in the capture; today's page is 4KB with a spaced-letter 'Open W o r l d' line, star and pencil glyphs and coloured hover states.
signature: A bio that admits 'i don't know what my email is either', then a lowercase poem in a thin left column.
why: Zero ornament makes the writing the interface; the narrow column and hard line breaks make the poem's lineation visible; empty space on the right reads as quiet.
steal: Publish writing as plain text in a 230px column at the left edge with hard line breaks, and leave the rest of the viewport empty.

title: Grid – Thinking With Type
name: Grid - Thinking With Type
one_line: Companion site to a typography book: black masthead, serif lesson on grids, double-ruled contents box, red-annotated diagrams.

look.type: Bold italic serif title ~48px and bold 32px section head; 11px book serif body at generous leading; red italic captions; white serif masthead.
look.color: White page, black masthead and type; red for diagram annotations and captions; beige figure panels with a pale yellow plate.
look.layout: Full-width black bar, ~375px reading column at left, a 650px figure panel below and a double-bordered contents box floated right.
look.imagery: Diagrams in the book's idiom: golden-section rectangles, red construction lines, a pale yellow page plate, red italic captions.

behaviour: Static site with nav (Letter | Text | Grid | Extras) and search; this URL returns 404 today, so the capture is the only evidence.
signature: A hatched double rule under the title and a double-bordered contents box carry the printed book's furniture onto the web.
why: A teaching site that looks like the book it supports reinforces the lessons: ratios drawn in the same red-annotated style as print make the diagrams the content.
steal: When a site supports a book, reuse its diagram style, caption colour and rule styles so readers cannot tell where print ends and screen begins.
moves: red annotation colour on diagrams and captions

title: Stochaster
name: Stochaster - Dotraster
one_line: A French halftone-software site: grotesk nav, a three-column description row, a perspective-tilted stack of app windows as hero.

why: Letting the real app UI and its output fill two-thirds of the screen sells the tool better than description; small grotesk text rows keep information dense but tidy.
steal: Show the actual interface in perspective, cropped by the viewport edges with the output visible inside it, above a three-column description row.

title: Unlife
name: Unlife

look.layout: Centred ~700px column: masthead left, contact lines and circular emblem right, hairline, bracketed nav, then four lists of bracketed timestamps and titles.
look.imagery: A circular glyph emblem in magenta; film stills and GIFs inside posts; no photography on the index.

behaviour: Neocities HTML with details/summary folds for sections; 62 list items stamped like org-mode ([2024-04-30 Tue 20:41]); GPG and fediverse contact in the header.
signature: A blackletter masthead above a terminal-style log, every post stamped like an Emacs org-mode timestamp.
why: Two typographic extremes (medieval blackletter, 1970s terminal) in one hue combine subculture and tool-use signals; the list format makes a large archive scannable by date.
steal: Pair a heavy blackletter masthead with a terminal face for the list, keep everything in one hot hue on near-black, and stamp entries with exact times.
moves: org-mode timestamps as the post index

title: Creating A Pencil Effect In SVG | CSS-Tricks
name: Creating a Pencil Effect in SVG - CSS-Tricks

look.layout: Black top bar, tall dark hero with title and byline, white card (8px radius) with a ~480px text column and a full-width embed.
look.imagery: Greyscale fantasy-map hillshade as header texture, matched to the article's subject; pencil-textured SVG demo in the embed.

signature: The header image is a dim fantasy map matched to the article's subject, then the page drops straight into a live demo.
why: Tutorial pages work when the demo sits between short paragraphs of context; a subject-specific dark header and generous line height make long reading easy.

title: Making Space for a Handmade Web | Figma Blog
name: Making Space for a Handmade Web - Figma Blog

look.color: Butter yellow (#f2ee93) ground with black type; illustration in tomato red, sky blue, pink, olive and violet.

steal: Give each long read its own saturated page colour and one grain-textured illustration with a small in-joke from the subject matter.

mono caps for date and tags

title: First-ever compendium of indigenous technologies provides a powerful toolkit for climate-resilient design - Harvard Graduate...
name: Compendium of indigenous technologies - Harvard GSD

signature: The headline's last line overlaps the photo's top edge, tying type and image into one object.
why: A single bold overlap is the only gesture on an otherwise austere page, so it reads as confident editorial design; the picture does the emotional work.

title: WADA SANZO | DICTIONARY OF COLOR COMBINATIONS

swatch / list / JSON API as views

letterspaced caps nav (with a zero in S0CIAL)

mix-blend-mode text over a white shape
konami easter egg that inflates the type

title: Wishing Well by Eyes8atelier

signature: The page's own colours are sampled from the game's posterised palette, so the store page already feels like the game.
why: Restricting both screenshots and page chrome to the same warm colours makes the game's mood legible before anyone plays; the gentle copy (slow and peaceful) matches the palette.
steal: On a platform page, set the theme colours (background, column, buttons, text) from the work's own palette and quantise screenshots to match.

title: Thick Press - A Publishing Practice

one_line: A publisher's home as a wall of book photographs, each on its own saturated colour tile, with sentence-style navigation.

signature: Navigation is written as verbs - 'is about', 'is out and about', 'is connecting' - on hairline-ruled rows at the foot.
why: Giving each book its own flat colour field turns a catalogue into a colour chart you scan by hue; the sentence nav gives the press a voice with no extra copy.
steal: Give every product a flat tile in a colour pulled from it, tile edge to edge, and write footer navigation as short verb phrases.
moves: nav written as 'is about / is connecting'
logo wrapped by syllable in a narrow rail

title: APOD.LI
name: APOD.LI

why: Extreme scale contrast (110px against 10px) with an identical card structure makes thousands of records loud and scannable at once; form-style filter boxes signal a database honestly.
steal: Set a one-line title at viewport width, then pack records into bordered grey cards: 24px caps title, bold author, 10px metadata columns.

title: Mainframe
name: Mainframe
one_line: A 'generative computing' environment: the capture shows a loader inside a grey bevelled device frame at 5%.

look.type: Tiny 11px Helvetica-like UI text ('Status / Loading... / 5%'); later versions declare Geist Mono and a Timeless serif and sans.
look.color: Warm stone-grey bezel around a pale putty screen; black progress-bar outline; no accent.
look.layout: A full-viewport bevelled frame like a monitor with a rounded inset screen; status block top-left; a small port icon bottom centre.

behaviour: Next.js app embedding an iframe; the loader mimics an old-OS status bar; mainfra.me now redirects to mainframe.app and the live page shows only a JS shell.
signature: Even the loading state is staged: a physical bezel, an OS-style status line and a 5% bar make a website feel like a device.
why: Skeuomorphic framing signals 'this is a computer' before any content exists; the quiet beige and tiny type keep the focus on the screen's future content.
steal: Wrap a web app in a drawn device bezel and design the loading screen as an old OS status panel, in 11px type and one progress bar.
moves: tiny type on a pale screen

title: Whispers
name: Whispers
one_line: A chain of fifty interlinked artworks by fifty contributors, shown as a closed ring around a centred statement.

look.type: Nanum Myeongjo serif 20px, centred, 'Whispers' in italic; credits at 10px; 'More info' in italic; nothing else is text.
look.color: Warm light grey (#f4f3f3) ground; colour comes only from the fifty artworks; no accent.
look.layout: Fifty ~65px thumbnails fixed on a circle, each rotated to the tangent; statement in the empty middle; credits at the foot.

signature: The chain is drawn as a closed ring, so a game of telephone reads as a loop you can enter at any work.
why: The layout is the concept: sequence, equality of size and connection are visible at once; the empty centre holds the explanation, and zooming is the only interaction needed.
steal: When content is a sequence or loop, draw it as a ring of identical thumbnails around the statement; let a click move one image to the centre.
moves: ring of fifty thumbnails rotated to the tangent
click zooms an image to the middle with caption
identical thumbnail size so artworks compete equally

title: Hobonichi Techo - Dear Dicery - Hobonichi Techo Official Website

why: A strict three-colour palette (yellow, blue, black) and condensed type give the toy a recognisable identity; physical, overlapping objects make a prompt generator feel like play.

title: Spoon museum exhibits

title: In Search of Organic Software

why: The essay argues for organic, slow software and the page behaves that way: warm, hand-drawn, slightly off-grid, with a margin date that reads like a diary entry.

title: Holy Site

title: LAN Party House

title: Hyper Tensions Mindful Liberation

title: Did you know that a wave is a dynamic system in catastrophe?

one_line: A text about waves that scrolls forever: the page clones itself, so the end loops back to the start.

look.type: Sub-Marine, a hair-thin monoline custom face at 39px with 2px tracking; Sub-Marine Pictographs at 234px turns A, B, C into pixel pictograms.
look.color: Black on white, yellow (#ff0) text selection, pure blue (#00f) links without underline; no other colour.

signature: A scroll that never ends, so an essay about waves behaves like one: each paragraph arrives alone, rises, passes and returns.
why: Form enacts content: the loop is the wave, the huge gaps are the troughs, and a pictograph font gives each lettered section an image without any image files.
steal: Clone your content section once and jump scroll position when you reach the clone: an endless loop in ten lines, with giant white gaps for pacing.

why: Using the most overlooked pixels in the browser as a canvas, and the voice of instructions (steps, footnotes) to play it straight, gives a tiny idea full commitment.
steal: Pick a forgotten browser surface (favicon, tab title, status bar) and write a deadpan step-by-step guide to decorating it.

why: Status rides on the cheapest visual variables (colour, strikethrough) so a list of 150 towns scans at a glance and weighs 10KB.

why: The name is acted out: repetition in the title, a circling hoop, radio-button circles in the nav. A heavy subject (waste) lands softly through characters and flat colour.

signature: Navigation as a plant: seven section names hang from one root word on straight hairline branches.
why: The tree matches the foundation's subject (seeds, heritage, residencies) as well as acting as the menu, so structure and meaning are one drawing; flat green keeps it legible.
steal: Draw your sitemap as a literal diagram of what you do (tree, river, wheel) on a flat colour field, with labels at the line ends.

title: How often should you blog?
name: pcalv.es blog
one_line: A short post about blogging in an airy serif column; today the site is monospace on cream with dark mode.

look.type: Capture: bold geometric sans title ~32px, italic old-style date, Garamond-like body ~22px at line-height near 2; now Space Mono throughout.
look.color: Capture: lavender-grey page, near-black text, violet links and nav; now cream #faf8f1, or #201e26 in dark mode.
look.layout: Single left-aligned column about 780px wide; nav (notes, now, books, links, rss) right-aligned beside a small hand icon as logo.
look.imagery: None beyond a small line-drawn two-finger hand logo in the corner.

behaviour: Static; footnote links; RSS; CSS variables with prefers-color-scheme dark mode; fluid clamp() root size; a small clock script.
signature: Very generous line-height (about 2) and short paragraphs make the text feel like a letter, with violet links as the only colour.
why: Reading comfort is the whole design: a measure of about 70 characters, large type, loose leading, one accent for links. The post's argument (a small personal web) is matched by the form.
steal: Set blog text at ~22px with line-height near 2, a 65-70 character measure and one accent colour for links; keep nav on the logo row.

title: Frogs: Frog Facts, Myths & More | Exploratorium
name: Exploratorium Frogs
one_line: The Exploratorium's 1999 online frog exhibition, preserved as-is: table layout, GIF headings, khaki ground, cattail border.

look.type: Browser-default Arial/Helvetica at 11px; section headings are green GIF lettering; hand-lettered orange frogs logotype.
look.color: Khaki-sage ground (about #cccc99); terracotta-orange links; black body text; green headings; photographs supply the saturated frog colours.
look.layout: Centred 440px table: narrow text column at left, four image-plus-heading sections alternating sides at right, a cattail strip on the edge.
look.imagery: Cut-out frog photographs and a pen-drawn cattail; 27 GIFs in all; a sponsor logo strip at the foot.

behaviour: Static tables and GIFs with no CSS or JS; a banner says the exhibition ran Feb 1999 to Feb 2000 and the pages stay online.
signature: A 1999 museum exhibit kept alive untouched: each section is a frog photo beside a GIF-lettered heading, laid out in a table.
why: Because nothing was redesigned it still works: tiny files, text that reflows, an honest ran-from-through notice. Preservation is a design decision.
steal: Keep retired exhibitions online with a dated banner stating when they ran, and leave the original layout untouched.

title: this website is a door
name: doors to doors
one_line: Starfield page of navy rectangle doors down the scroll, each an open-door link into a portal.

look.type: Bold-italic Times title with a white glow; italic Times captions; open door in a Courier-like mono; all browser defaults.
look.color: Black tiled starfield with white, blue and red sparkles; midnight-blue (#191970-ish) doors with grey bevel borders; white glowing text.
look.layout: Intro text top-left; tall 200x390 doors placed at irregular x positions down a long scroll.
look.imagery: Tiling pixel starfield; flat blue door rectangles; one ghost emoji; nothing else.

behaviour: Each door links to another page or site on a trickster web server; the Glitch project is gone (410), so the doors no longer open.
signature: The page is a hallway: door-shaped rectangles you walk past down the scroll, each labelled only open door.
why: A plain literal metaphor, committed: one shape (the door) repeated, one verb (open), a starfield that says somewhere else. Curiosity does the work.
steal: Make links into one repeated object (a door) at its natural proportions, scatter them along the scroll, and label each with a single verb.
moves: trickster server premise in one line

title: Our Field Recordings
name: Our Field Recordings
one_line: Audio-collecting project with spaced-mono nav and a monospaced field guide over a blurred deep-blue storm photograph.

look.type: Source Code Pro monospace ~14px body, letter-spaced mono caps nav, a light condensed caps title (Abel-like) at ~28px.
look.color: Full-bleed indigo-to-black photograph with orange-pink glints; white and pale-blue type; one tan-and-black vintage print as the light object.
look.layout: Nav splits around a centred waveform logo; one 380px text column over the photo; further sections are Squarespace pages.
look.imagery: A blurred storm-light wave photograph as ground; a square vintage BE A TRANSFORMER mandala print as the lead image.

behaviour: Squarespace with pages for Splash, Welcome, Look, Microdoses, Moon-dial and Apothecary; the copy reads as instructions for recording; RSS.
signature: An instruction-poem as the front page: how to record your field, in typewriter-grade mono over a storm-lit photograph.
why: Copy, stormy ground and monospace voice all say capture the moment; a waveform glyph as logo is a literal mark of the subject.
steal: Put a long, instructive poem at the front of your site in monospace over a full-bleed photo; make the logo a literal waveform of your subject.

title: Mending Gallery — Repair Shop
name: Repair Shop Mending Gallery
one_line: Gallery of visible mends: darned socks, patched sweaters and embroidered sleeves in a plain four-column photo grid.

look.type: Monument Grotesk bold ~36px title, Diatype light ~22px intro, hairline hamburger; no other text on the page.
look.color: White page; the photos carry everything: red darning on black knit, yellow patch on olive wool, blue and red thread on cream.
look.layout: Left-aligned title and one-line description over a four-column grid; images centred in equal cells at native proportions.
look.imagery: Flat-lay and worn-on photos of clothing; the bright repair stitching is the focal point of each.

behaviour: Cargo site; a hamburger opens navigation; rotate and keyframe rules suggest small image motion (unclear); the viewport meta blocks zoom.
signature: The grid shows repair as ornament: each photo is chosen so the mend, not the garment, is the brightest thing.
why: A neutral frame lets contrast thread read as decoration; the words incomplete gallery set an unfinished, ongoing tone that welcomes new entries.
steal: Title a collection as incomplete, and photograph each object so its fix is the visual focus; use plain white so flaws read as ornament.

title: secret
name: secret (tiana.computer)
one_line: A poem hidden behind 36 slate-purple tiles over a looping video; each hover removes a tile and reveals one word.

look.type: Italic browser-default serif; every word is invisible (alpha 0) until hover, then white, centred in its tile.
look.color: Flat slate-violet #5b5886 tiles on ivory; the video's greens, browns and sky blue show only in 4px seams and revealed holes.
look.layout: Full-viewport 6-column CSS grid of 36 identical tiles with 2px margins; one word per tile, in reading order.
look.imagery: Muted looping phone-camera video fixed behind everything, visible through the tile gaps and hovered tiles.

behaviour: Pure CSS: on hover a tile goes transparent and its white word fades in over 0.5s; the poem can only be read by sweeping the cursor.
signature: Reading is uncovering: drag the cursor across a wall of tiles and the poem and the footage appear together, word by word.
why: The mechanism enacts the poem (when you disappear): tiles vanish under your hand, so touching and reading are one gesture. No JavaScript, 36 divs.
steal: Hide each word of a short text in its own tile above a video; use a 0.5s hover transition to make the tile transparent and reveal word and footage.

title: Scroll, Skim, Stare - Orit Gat
name: Orit Gat: Scroll, Skim, Stare
one_line: A critic's essay on artists' websites, set on their own Cargo site: year list at left, one narrow text column.

look.type: Tiny neutral sans (Helvetica Neue / Lucida-style, ~11-12px) for everything; bold numerals as section heads; grey navigation; no display type.
look.color: White page, black text, mid-grey (#999) navigation and years; no accent at all.
look.layout: Fixed left list (About, Selected, then years 2024 to 2012), centred 440px essay column, up, close and down arrows at top right.
look.imagery: None: an essay with no examples, as it says itself; a Running on Cargo credit bottom-right.

behaviour: Cargo page navigation (up, close, down arrows). The saved URL now returns a styled 404 File not found.
signature: A tiny-type essay page whose own template (left list, centred column) is the example of the uniformity it questions.
why: Strict plainness gives long reading a calm measure and a year index for orientation; the template's anonymity is the essay's evidence.
steal: For an essay-first site, fix a narrow text column in the middle, a grey index of years or sections at left, and drop all decoration.

title: a website could be
name: a website could be
one_line: Connect-the-dots sentence maker: click noun, verb and adjective dots, draw a path, and build your own definition of a website.

look.type: PicNic, a wobbly marker display face, at 160px for the title with green and grey stacked shadows; Meta-Old-French at 80px for the story.
look.color: Light grey #e3e0e0 ground, mid-grey dots and type; one green (#5db76f) for the selected dot and drawn lines.
look.layout: Two columns, 45 and 55 percent: left a 15-by-13 grid of numbered dots, right the giant title and growing sentence; legend bottom-left.
look.imagery: Dots as encoding: square is noun, solid circle verb, hollow circle adjective; 1px green leader lines join the chosen ones.

behaviour: Clicking a dot extends a 1px green line (LeaderLine) from the last, appears to add its word to the story, pulses the start dot, shows typing dots.
signature: Grammar as a game board: three dot shapes encode parts of speech, and the path you draw becomes the sentence.
why: The interface makes the idea physical: composing is travelling, shapes are parts of speech, and grey plus one green keeps focus on your path and the words.
steal: Encode a data type in a glyph shape (square, disc, ring), let the user draw a path through them, and use one accent for the chosen route.
moves: dot shapes encode parts of speech
oversized wobbly title with layered shadows

title: Rotating Sandwiches – that's it
name: Rotating Sandwiches
one_line: A blog that is a single column of 67 rotating sandwich GIFs on white, under a lowercase title.

look.type: DM Sans regular ~38px lowercase title, italic 13px email line; no other text on the page.
look.color: White ground fading to pale blue at the top; food colour (toast, herbs, foil) is the only colour.
look.layout: One centred column: cut-out sandwiches about 200px apart on white, with title and email left-aligned above.
look.imagery: Background-removed sandwiches, each a looping spin GIF: a slaw melt, a banh mi, a foil-wrapped burrito.

behaviour: WordPress.com theme; 67 GIFs stacked down one scroll; comment and subscribe footer left as the host provides it.
signature: The title is the content: sandwiches that rotate, stacked, nothing else; even the tab title says that's it.
why: A single joke executed at full commitment with 67 assets in one format: consistent cut-out, scale and spacing turn repetition into rhythm.
steal: Pick one absurd object, shoot 60 of them in one format with the background removed, and stack them in a single column with no captions.

title: Our Networks
name: Our Networks
one_line: A conference site written as terminal output: tree-diagram nav in box-drawing characters, plotter-style headline and ASCII-art illustration.

look.type: Monospace throughout: Hershey Futural plotter-font headline ~36px, small mono body ~14px, underlined links, box-drawing characters as interface.
look.color: Beige paper (#f5f5dc), black text, one red #ff4433 X in the ASCII laptop; nothing else.
look.layout: A 480px left-aligned column: logo glyph, tree menu, event title and date, ASCII picture, then paragraphs.
look.imagery: ASCII drawing of clouds and a laptop reading NETWORK IS OPTIONAL; a small blocky pixel-glyph logo.

behaviour: Light static page (39KB): the menu is a pre-formatted tree with real links; 2022 is struck out and replaced by 2047; small clock and random scripts.
signature: The sitemap printed like a tree command: box-drawing lines make navigation, theme and joke at once.
why: Every layer says own your network: text-mode type, ASCII art, tiny page weight. The metaphor goes all the way down, so nothing feels decorative.
steal: Choose one computing metaphor (terminal, tree, man page) and apply it to nav, headings, illustration and page weight; draw pictures in text characters.
moves: ASCII illustration with one red X
future-year joke in the archive list

title: Come, Pray the Rosary | Pray with Others Worldwide
name: Come, Pray the Rosary
one_line: A black splash gate: glowing script title beside a silver rosary photo, a chrome ENTER button, a tiny credit line.

look.color: Pure black; white and silver only; the button is a bevelled #ededed-to-#d8d8d8 gradient.
look.layout: Centred stack: title and photo side by side, credit line, ENTER button, two links; everything above the fold, empty black below.
look.imagery: One photo of a silver rosary on black lace, its edges faded into the black page.

signature: A 3KB splash that does one thing: black ground, a glowing script title, a silver rosary and a chunky chrome ENTER.
why: Total commitment to one atmosphere (candle-black, silver, script) with a single obvious action; the bevelled button reads as an object you press.
steal: Keep the gate page tiny: one image faded into the background, one glowing title, one big bevelled button as the only action.

title: bratgen | Brat Generator
name: Brat Generator
one_line: Meme tool: type any word and it renders in the Charli XCX brat album-cover style on acid green.

look.type: Blurred black lowercase brat in a narrow Arial-like grotesk at ~90px; every control in unstyled Times 14px.
look.color: Flat acid lime (#8acf00) field, black text; a white pill input; nothing else.
look.layout: The word dead centre of a full-viewport field; a pill input and legal links stacked at the bottom.
look.imagery: None; the low-resolution blur on the type is the image.

behaviour: Type into the pill and the centre word updates; a note says take a screenshot to save, so there is no export step. Today returns 403.
signature: A cultural moment reduced to two decisions: one lime, one deliberately blurry Arial; the generator is just a text field.
why: Fidelity to a few recognisable parameters (lime, lowercase, blur) matters more than interface polish: unstyled Times controls do not hurt because the output is exact.
steal: For a meme tool, nail the one recognisable look (colour plus type treatment) in the output, leave the controls plain, and ask for screenshots instead of building export.
moves: one flat colour plus one face as a brand
take a screenshot instead of export

title: ritual of forgetting
name: ritual of forgetting (clique books)
