look.type: Typewriter-mono lowercase captions at ~11px (low bit, as i sit, in thrall) centred at the top and bottom of the page.
look.color: Sage-khaki ground with a faint dotted tile; near-black ink silhouettes; one pale misty photo square.
look.layout: One 250px object dead centre in a 1000px field, captions marooned top and bottom; huge empty margins.
look.imagery: Silhouette cut-outs (bar, ring, wheat sprig, mushrooms, a stooped figure) cluster around a bleached photo of branches and light.

behaviour: Unclear: probably a click-through digital edition. The saved URL returns 404; the Are.na note points to the EDITION-1 path.
signature: Scale as mood: an image the size of a postage stamp floating in sage space, labelled with two lowercase lines.
why: Emptiness slows the viewer: the small object demands attention, the typewriter captions read like marginalia, and the matte green makes it feel printed.
steal: Show the work at about a quarter of the field, centred, with two tiny lowercase captions at top and bottom; let the margin be the design.

title: Bindery.js · Intro
name: Bindery.js
one_line: Docs site for a book-typesetting JS library, itself typeset like a book: serif with indented paragraphs, outlined buttons.

look.type: Transitional serif ~22px with real first-line indents and no paragraph gaps; Input Mono and a system sans ~14px for buttons.
look.color: Black on white; links underlined; buttons are 1px black outlines with 6px radius; no accent colour.
look.layout: 700px column with a book-icon logo and serif nav at left and a Make book button at right; a large empty area below the text.
look.imagery: None on the intro; a small open-book line icon is the logo; a dot marks the current nav item.

behaviour: Static docs; scroll listener only. An italic notice says Bindery is no longer in development and points to Paged.js, WeasyPrint and PrinceXML.
signature: Typeset like the product: indent-not-space paragraphs and an em-dash divider carry the library's book logic onto the web.
why: A tool for books proves itself by borrowing book conventions in plain CSS; restraint (one serif, one rule, tiny buttons) is credible for a typography tool.
steal: Use first-line indents with zero paragraph spacing and an em-dash break for long running text; style buttons as 1px outlines.

title: Alt Text Selfies | Splash
name: Alt Text Selfies
one_line: Disability-led portrait project: pale yellow splash with two outlined boxes, enter with sound or without.

look.type: Century Expanded, a wide text serif: caps title ~18px, sentence-case labels ~24px centred inside the boxes.
look.color: Flat pale yellow (#feffbb), black hairlines and black asterisk ornaments; nothing else.
look.layout: Two 255px outlined boxes side by side in the centre; title at the top; five small asterisks scattered near the corners.
look.imagery: Hand-drawn eight-point asterisks; no photos on the splash.

behaviour: A choice gate: Enter with sound or without; a Vue app with drag, mouse and random handlers likely moves the ornaments; entries are text self-portraits.
signature: The first decision is access itself: two equal boxes, sound or no sound, before any content appears.
why: Access is part of the design language from the first screen; a legible wide serif, large hit areas and one calm colour keep the entry quiet and unmistakable.
steal: Open with two equally weighted outlined choices (with sound / without sound) in large type; let people set the mode before the content.

title: Demo Festival
name: Demo Festival
one_line: NEW INC's art-and-tech festival site (2024 edition): DEMO 2024 spelled in blocky letters that fill a grid of square tiles.

look.type: Neographik, a blocky rounded-corner display face: each letter fills a square cell, O as a square with a round hole; Akkurat for text.
look.color: 2024: pale grey ground (about #ebebe8), warm taupe letters and hairlines; the current 2026 edition flips to black with Akkurat and yellow #ffbb00.
look.layout: A 4-by-4 square module grid: outlined empty cells with circles above and below; the two middle rows are DEMO and 2024 in letter cells.

behaviour: The 2024 splash appears static; today's Nuxt site adds autoplay muted video, Swiper carousels, drag, search and a festival map.
signature: Empty grid cells are the same size as the letters, so the brand reads as a system: outlined squares are blank type.
why: Lettering and ornament share one module, so any message can be spelled, padded or animated in the same grid; two flat tints are enough.
steal: Draw your wordmark so every letter fits one square module, fill unused modules with outlined placeholder cells, and reuse the grid across the site.
moves: O as square with circular hole

title: Home | Varyer
name: Varyer

look.type: GT Alpina variable serif (plus condensed) up to 252px for headlines; Roobert for nav and tags; fluid sizing across 61 distinct sizes.
look.color: Warm off-white #fcfbf7, ink #161616; rainbow risograph gradient on yellow, coral #ff656e and periwinkle #9896ff accents.
look.layout: Hairline-ruled masthead (date left, logo centre, time and weather right), nav, filter pills, then bento tiles clipped to arches and circles.
look.imagery: Risograph-grain skull-and-dagger arch, woodcut figure, hand-drawn sketches, vinyl-style circle badge, photo stills; every image clipped to a shape.

behaviour: GSAP ScrollTrigger and Isotope masonry; local time and temperature in the header; autoplaying muted video tiles; drag carousels; category pills filter content.
signature: Content tiles cut to different silhouettes (arch, circle, rounded card) so a feed reads like a shelf of objects, with the weather in the masthead.
why: A shared set of shapes and one warm ground unify very different content (poster, spreadsheet, record, sketch); masthead facts make the site feel published today.
steal: Clip every feed item to one of three silhouettes (arch, circle, card) on a warm off-white ground and add a masthead strip with date and weather.
moves: masthead with live time and weather

title: broider
name: Broider
one_line: Pixel-draw tool for 9-patch CSS borders: paint nine cells, copy the generated border-image CSS, submit to a gallery.

look.type: Tiny 10px monospace with a soft text shadow; pixel numerals for the border width; bracketed links like [click to copy].
look.color: Antique-white #faebd7 page; lavender-grey #6b7593 grid lines; black pixels; a black preview square.
look.layout: Centred 3-by-3 editor at top, explanation and code box beneath, preview square at right, name field and submit last.
look.imagery: Pixel-art tool icons (pen, eraser, mirror, undo) inside the middle cell; the artwork is whatever you draw.

behaviour: Canvas drawing in nine cells with mirror and undo; live preview via border-image; outputs a data-URI CSS rule to copy; gallery submission.
signature: The editor is a 9-patch: the toolbar lives in the empty centre cell, so the tool is drawn inside its own output.
why: Output as interface: you see the exact thing you will ship (border CSS), the controls tuck into otherwise unused space, and copy-paste is the only export.
steal: Put the tool palette inside the empty centre of the thing being edited, show a live preview at real size, and offer one click-to-copy output.

title: home - poetic computer
name: poetic computer

look.type: Fluxisch / Phililita: a bold wobbly slab-italic display at 72px, set slightly rotated; nav in Luxi Mono underlined caps.
look.color: White ground, black ink; any colour comes from the scanned notes (green headings, yellow highlights, red markers).

signature: Research shown as evidence: the home page is a desk of the actual notes, diagrams and annotations, not a description of them.
why: Showing raw artefacts at real size proves a process-led project and invites browsing; the wobbly title ties handwriting to the code-poetry theme.
steal: Replace a hero image with a messy pile of your real working artefacts: scans, diagrams, screenshots, overlapped, with 1px borders and slight rotations.
moves: artefacts at real scale with borders

title: LEAVING RECORDS | ARTISTS
name: Leaving Records

why: Overlap shows relationships a list cannot; hairline outlines keep the page open, and the stark white ground leaves room for artist imagery to be the colour.
steal: Show a roster as overlapping outlined circles with names inside, and let collaboration entries visibly overlap the solo entries they share artists with.

title: Library - Handmade Web
name: Handmade Web library

look.type: Not Courier Sans (a light mono) ~13px for nearly everything; olive-brown #5d4e31 ink; Selectric typewriter face declared for accents.
look.color: Day: lime #d6e1a1, olive ink, burnt-orange #b65320 links. Night: slate #4e4e5c, lavender text, sage-teal links; red-orange square sun.
look.layout: 200px fixed sidebar menu with three theme swatches; main area is two columns of bordered tables: header row, then author | title | pdf rows.
look.imagery: No photographs; a tiny tree icon, asterisk ornaments, and a 50px square sun blended over the page in overlay mode.

behaviour: After idle time the page cross-fades over 30 seconds into night, the sun square sinks and a moon square rises; at real night it switches instantly.
signature: A screensaver as sunset: when idle, a square sun sinks off the page and a smaller moon rises as colours fade to night.
why: Two systems make a bibliography charming: strict tables for utility, a slow time-of-day mood for delight. Colour tokens as CSS variables make the shift trivial.
steal: Define day and night palettes as CSS variables, then on idle animate between them over 30 seconds with an expo ease while a square sun sets.

title: onoffon radio

signature: A pink, softly rounded pull-quote sets the tone: this is a home-cooked meal, not an enterprise guide.
why: Documentation written like a letter: short paragraphs, a stated intention and permission to be imperfect; typography stays quiet so the voice does the persuading.

title: Gridder – Modular Grid Generator

why: Controls are large numbers you edit directly; each parameter pairs an icon with a value, so the panel reads as a legible equation of the page.

title: Julia Kim Smith
name: Julia Kim Smith

behaviour: jQuery; animated tab title; drag and random handlers likely rearrange or preview cells; 14 media queries reflow the grid.
signature: A spreadsheet of deadpan project names: AdWords, baltimore actually, miss dmz, each in an identical cell.
why: Equal cells and plain titles flatten very different projects (net art, prints, performance) into a dry catalogue, which makes the weirdness of each title land harder.
steal: Make your portfolio index a hairline table of titles only, alphabetical, centred in equal cells; let strong titles do the selling.

title: esoteric.codes
name: esoteric.codes
one_line: Esolang blog: mint-circle ASCII logo, email bar, and a three-column magazine grid of code-art images and mono titles.

look.type: Inconsolata monospace for the caps site name and ~20px post titles; Montserrat tagline; Open Sans ~13px excerpts.
look.color: Light-grey header, white grid with #ddd rules, mint-green blocks and logo; images are black-and-white code art.
look.layout: Banner with follow icons and a subscribe form over a hairline; three columns of variable-height posts separated by vertical rules.
look.imagery: High-contrast esolang artefacts: ORCA tile art, a hard-drive nebula, a terminal poem, wire graphs, seven-segment glyphs.

behaviour: Static blog with Bootstrap-era styling; 86 article blocks under Latest, Interviews, Posts and Projects; email signup; no scripts beyond analytics.
signature: An ASCII-art mint circle as logo and a mint rectangle as section marker: one colour tying a black-and-white image set together.
why: The subject (esoteric languages) is visual, so the layout steps aside and lets black-and-white code artefacts form the texture; one mint accent organises the sections.
steal: Pick one accent colour and use it only for the logo and section markers; let high-contrast black-and-white images carry the page.
moves: ASCII logo in a colour disc

title: ui.land
name: ui.land

look.type: Inter-style sans: 48px tight-tracked two-tone headline (black, then grey), 16px names, 12-13px grey metadata.
look.color: Warm off-white with a 12-step grey ramp; near-black text; no accent colour visible; icons in the resource list are the only colour.
look.layout: Two columns: interview list left (role, name, line, Read Interview arrow), bordered cards right (newsletter, resources) with 12px radius.
look.imagery: Tiny app icons in the resource list (Diagram, Sonner, React, an avatar); no photographs.

behaviour: Next.js; keydown and localStorage handlers, fade keyframes, a small email form; focus-visible and reduced-motion rules are present.
signature: A two-tone headline whose second line dims to grey, then a list that ranks by greys alone.
why: Hierarchy comes from three greys and weight alone, so scanning six interviews takes no effort; side cards keep secondary tasks out of the way.
steal: Build hierarchy from a grey ramp: role in light grey, name in medium-weight black, description in mid-grey, action in bold with an arrow.

title: Bookshelf Town
name: Bookshelf Town
one_line: Social reading site whose home is one paper book: ASCII bookshelf cover, Open a book, bookmark-style tabs.

look.type: Selectric typewriter-serif Open a book ~22px in rust; monospace 11-12px tabs and ASCII drawing in tan.
look.color: Three inks only: cream #f4e7d4 paper, rust spine and title, tan ASCII art and tab outlines.
look.layout: One 300x430 book dead centre; Login ribbon, Create Account box and dotted About, New Features, Bulletin Board tabs poke from its edge.

behaviour: Login and links hang off the book as tabs; Open a book presumably leads to the shelf; localStorage and a random pick are used by the scripts.
signature: The login UI is bookmarks: a ribbon-notched tab for Login and dotted index tabs that stick out of the closed book.
why: The brand is one physical metaphor in three inks, so the call to action (open a book) is the product, and secondary links become obvious as physical tabs.
steal: Replace the hero with one object that is the product (a closed book), and hang the nav off its edge as tabs and ribbons.

title: The Wanderverse Project
name: The Wanderverse Project
one_line: Collaborative poetry game at MIT's library: flourished title, PLAY and…'s ornaments scattered like confetti.

signature: Printer's ornaments as weather: pilcrows, daggers and manicules drift across a cold-blue page like confetti.
why: Typographic marks are both decoration and the poem's raw material; sparse tints and a narrow central column keep the buttons unmissable among the scatter.
steal: Use a font's dingbats (pilcrow, section sign, dagger, manicule) as scattered ornaments in three or four tints at random sizes instead of illustrations.

title: Catalogue

look.color: Light grey #f2f2f2 page, black UI, mid-grey captions; indigo #5f5dff is held back for interaction states; photos sit on neutral grey.

signature: Handsets at consistent scale on neutral grey, so the grid itself shows how phones shrank, swelled and folded over four decades.
why: A museum catalogue needs equal treatment: same grey, same cut-out, same caption format let design diversity be the subject; filters are plain words, not icons.
steal: For a collection, cut out each object on one neutral ground at consistent scale, caption as Brand - Model, and filter with four plain dropdowns.

title: Archive

signature: A file-browser layout for an art practice: three panes, neon-green nav tiles, each project tagged by discipline and an oval year chip.
why: Dense metadata (year chip, category tags) makes a body of work scannable like a database, while neon green gives the nav a position without touching the artwork.
steal: Give a portfolio a persistent index column with year chips and discipline tags and a large stage beside it; colour only the nav.

why: One 3D form replaces grid and nav; type is nearly absent, so thumbnails of real devices act as proof. Hands free? signals this studio also builds technical demos.

why: Interaction that demonstrates the product: you compare two faces by moving a lens, so size, colour and weight are tested by hand, not read in a table.
steal: Make the specimen one draggable object with labelled corners; show the typeface through the movable window and name each mode in {curly braces}.

title: Quantum Natives

why: The map is catalogue and genre mood (ambient, game-like, mysterious) in one form; unexplored fog creates the pull a list never does.
steal: Use a pan-and-zoom map engine for a non-geographic archive: cover it in fog, place releases as markers, and tuck news into a slide-down tab.

slide-down legend tab with blog feed

name: Loaders.css
one_line: A specimen sheet of pure-CSS loading animations: white shapes in a four-column grid on coral red.

look.type: Untitled Sans: bold 45px 'Loaders' plus light '.css', 17px white tagline; no other text on the page.

look.layout: Title left and outlined 'View on Github' button right; below, a rigid four-column grid with each loader centred in an invisible cell.

behaviour: Every cell loops its own CSS animation (spin, bounce, pulse, scale, 3D flip via perspective); zero JavaScript, 43 KB page.
signature: A whole page that is nothing but small motions on one ground, so you compare them like paint swatches.
why: A component library's best demo is the components themselves. One ground colour and identical cell size remove everything except the motion, so timing and shape differences become the content.
steal: When showing a set of moving things, put each in an identical cell on one flat colour with no labels; let the motion be the only variable.

title: Museo

why: Black ground makes any artwork look lit, and the interface keeps to one input so the museums' images supply the whole palette. A credit line and curly quotes give it a human voice.

title: NJ Roseti
name: NJ Roseti

title: us

title: Document
name: event.preventDefault()
one_line: A 2019 design thesis about website design, laid out as scroll-synced columns: contents strip, text sheet, footnotes with GIFs.

look.type: Times New Roman ~24px: centred title with italic subtitle; contents labels in small grey Arial ~12px; tiny footnote type in the aside.
look.color: Off-white #f8f8f8 page, white centre sheet, grey hairline boxes, black text at 84% opacity; no accent colour.

signature: The table of contents is a scroll-synced strip whose boxes are sized to their chapters, a minimap of the whole argument.
why: A long argument gets a spatial map, so you always see where you are in the whole text. Footnotes in their own lane keep the central column unbroken and give the GIFs a home.
steal: For long-form pieces, build the contents as a second scroll lane synced to the text, with box heights matching section lengths, and put footnotes in a third lane.
moves: Times New Roman as a stance
thesis presented as its own demo

title: Homegrown National Parks

why: One mascot with a clear role (signs of life) warms up a dense choropleth. A single green ramp is intuitive for ecology, and yellow glow dots mark activity without extra legends.
steal: Put one illustrated creature on a data map, tie the colour ramp to the subject (olive to deep green), and limit the stat card to three icons with numbers.

title: Fuse.kiwi - Interesting Internet

signature: A ball pit that is the dataset and the filter in one playable object: toss the balls, then browse the same sites as cards.
why: The directory appears twice at two scales: an undifferentiated mass you can play with, then named cards. The toy invites play before browsing and lets you feel how many entries exist.
steal: Give a directory a playful overview (balls, dots, tiles) above the list, where every mark is a real entry and the filter controls float inside the toy.

flag plus mono category label on each card
paste-link submit box in the corner

title: the html review 03

look.layout: Contents as a radial wheel of names around 'ISSUE 03'; pieces step diagonally down the…'s angle, fading as they leave.

why: Navigation, contents and layout are one gesture: a single geometric rule (twenty stations on a circle) generates everything, so a long issue feels like an object you rotate rather than a list you scroll.
steal: Place each section by polar coordinates in CSS custom properties (--x, --y, --rotate-inner) on a big circle, then rotate the container from scroll position.

twenty stations placed by computed polar coordinates
boxed, rotated titles with red bylines
pieces fade as they leave the focus path
