title: Bureau Cool
name: Bureau Cool
one_line: Studio homepage whose hero is a thin 3D ring carrying recent-visitor dots labelled by country and time.

look.type: Heavy monospace caps (Arial Monospaced Bold ~50px) for the pitch; a light Century Schoolbook Mono for the name; 9-11px mono labels.
look.color: Flat light grey #dedede ground, black type, mid-grey timestamps; the ring is pale metal grey. Fully monochrome.
look.layout: Name and three-line pitch top-left, two outlined pill links beneath, a ~500px ring centred, 'RECENT TRAFFIC' label at the left edge.
look.imagery: A glossy thin torus rendered in WebGL with tiny spheres for visitors; no photography on the first screen.

behaviour: A WebGL canvas places one sphere per recent visit with country code and 'ONLINE' or '6MIN AGO'; SvelteKit app; selected work follows (Nike, Nosaj Thing, pgLang).
signature: The homepage shows who is looking right now: dots for visitors by country and minutes ago, floating on a delicate ring.
why: Live data about the site's own audience makes a studio site feel occupied and shows real-time skill without a slogan. Mono caps keep the tone technical and calm.
steal: Show a tiny live readout of your own site (visitors by country, last updated) as the hero object, set in 10px mono caps, instead of a slogan image.
moves: monospace caps as the only voice

title: Studium Generale | Take a Walk on the Wild Side | GRA + Rietveld Uncut
name: Take a Walk on the Wild Side (Rietveld)
one_line: A Rietveld Academie programme site: a full-screen landscape collage of sliced, glitched photos under a stepped nav.

look.type: Sneak, a light-and-medium grotesk, at 17px on 22px lines; every label sits on a white chip; the current page is bold.
look.color: Meadow greens, sky blue, rock violet and tree-trunk brown from the photographs; chips are white, empty ground #eee.
look.layout: Header nav in 10%-wide cells staggered on three rows (offsets 0, 22, 44px) over a full-bleed field assembled from rectangular tiles.
look.imagery: Landscape photography (meadow, granite mountain, motorway aerial) plus cut-out tree trunks, tiled and smeared into horizontal streaks.

behaviour: Vue app; a 4px full-height black line tracks the mouse as the cursor; mousemove, drag and random code suggest the collage is reshuffled live.
signature: A cursor drawn as a full-height vertical line, over a landscape built from mismatched tiles and tree trunks like a half-loaded image.
why: The title is enacted: nature appears assembled, artificial and slightly broken. White label chips keep the staggered nav legible over very busy imagery.
steal: When nav must sit on a busy image, give every label its own solid white chip and stagger labels across three baselines so they never collide.

title: ophelia do you listen to lana del rey?
name: ophelia do you listen to lana del rey?
one_line: A fairycore collage page: a Max/MSP patch down the left edge among archived GeoCities nature GIFs placed by percentage.

look.type: No visible type: the only text is the tab title, which scrolls like a marquee; the Max patch labels live inside an image.
look.color: White page; all colour comes from GIFs: turquoise pond, pink glitter wings, red roses, leaf green, navy music notes.
look.layout: 85 absolutely positioned images placed by left/top/bottom percentages and vw widths; the patch runs down the left, pond and crystal ball sit lower right.
look.imagery: Old-web GIFs hot-linked from Wayback Machine GeoCities snapshots: waterfalls, fairies, frogs, notes, roses, plus a Max/MSP patch.

behaviour: A fairy PNG replaces the cursor; the document title rotates one character every 450ms; most images are pulled live from archive.org.
signature: A Max/MSP sound patch (metro, counter, cycle~ into a speaker) beside glitter fairy GIFs, as if synthesis and fairycore shared one canvas.
why: Two vernaculars (audio-programming patch and 2000s fan-page clip-art) share a page without comment; the juxtaposition is the idea. Hot-linking the archive makes the page depend on the web's memory.
steal: Collage by percentage: place each found image with left/bottom percentages and a vw width on blank white, and let the tab title scroll as a marquee.
moves: GIFs hot-linked from the Wayback Machine
tab title scrolls like a marquee
audio-patch diagram as a decorative rail

title: Karl-Luis Vossbeck
name: Karl-Luis Vossbeck
one_line: A painter's site that shows each canvas as a polygon shard on near-white, with the caption peeking out from behind.

look.type: Default sans-serif ~16px; the only text is the artist's name (centred, blend-difference) and a centred caption with title, year and size.
look.color: Near-white #f7f7f7 ground; colour comes only from the paintings (pink scrawl, black field, green); the name inverts through a difference blend.
look.layout: Masonry of 33vw and 66vw cells; each image is clipped to a thin shard, leaving most of every cell empty.
look.imagery: Gestural abstract paintings (pink marks, a black field with white ticks) clipped to triangles so only fragments show.

behaviour: jQuery and Masonry; lazyload swaps 20px placeholders for 1200px images; a 'fixed' class expands an image to the full viewport; the name overlay morphs via clip-path.
signature: Paintings clipped into sharp polygon shards so you see fragments first, with the caption half-hidden behind the cut-away corner.
why: Withholding makes you act: you must click to see the whole painting. A CSS-only shard is cheap and sharp, and it echoes the violent marks in the paintings.
steal: Show artwork as clip-path polygons first and expand to the full image on click; put the caption behind the image (z-index -1) so it shows only through the cut.
moves: caption behind the image, revealed by the cut
ASCII-art portrait hidden in the HTML comment

title: Claudia Maté
name: Claudia Mate
one_line: An artist portfolio dressed as a Finder window: grouped sidebar plus an icon grid of captioned thumbnails (now blank).

look.type: System UI sans ~11px: grey caps section headers (WORKS, LINKS), blue selected row, tiny captions under thumbnails.
look.color: Pale blue-grey translucent sidebar, white content area, one blue selection highlight; thumbnails bring saturated CGI colour.
look.layout: A ~115px sidebar of grouped links; an 8-column icon grid of ~80px thumbnails, each with a tiny file-type icon and a one-line caption.
look.imagery: 3D avatars, CGI, video stills and site screenshots with soft shadows; one cell is a 'Loading, Please wait' spinner.

behaviour: Sidebar groups (Featured, Projects, Collab, Websites) presumably filter the grid like Finder; a Facebook Like button sits bottom-left. Today the domain serves a black 'Red Page'.
signature: The portfolio is a file browser: works are 'files'with type icons, and one cell…'Loading, Please wait' spinner.
why: An operating-system metaphor is instantly legible, gives free structure (sidebar groups, captions) and suits a net artist whose subject is screen culture. A dense icon grid shows breadth at a glance.
steal: Dress an index as a file browser: grouped sidebar, 80px icon grid, one-line captions with file-type icons; include one joke cell such as a loading spinner.

title: There Are No Weeds – Bog
name: Bog: There Are No Weeds
one_line: An online magazine whose essays each get their own scene: faded bog photograph, nettle engraving, one narrow serif column.

look.type: Times-like serif ~17px in a ~240px column with indented poem lines; credit in neon-green system sans bottom-left; Brandon Grotesque elsewhere.
look.color: Bog photograph bleached to ~15% strength, black ink engraving, one neon-green credit line, a tiny red-gold medieval figure top-right.
look.layout: Text column on the right third, 'Fig.1' engraving with caption mid-left, round grey medallion top-left (likely the menu), small illustration top-right.
look.imagery: Washed-out landscape photograph, botanical line engraving of nettles, a coin-like medallion, a lute-playing figure illustration.

behaviour: WordPress with Bootstrap, canvas 2D and mousemove code; five looping audio elements and 200+ keyframes across the issue; a Snipcart shop.
signature: The landscape photo is bleached until it acts as paper, with a 'Fig.1' nettle engraving set beside the text like a field-guide plate.
why: Each article is art-directed to its subject, so reading about nettles feels like standing in the bog. A narrow measure and big margins keep long essays comfortable.
steal: For an essay, bleach a subject photograph to about 15% strength as the page, keep text to a 240px serif column, and add one captioned plate ('Fig.1').
moves: credit in one off-palette neon colour

title: Pete Deevakul
name: Pete Deevakul
one_line: A Cargo photography portfolio: a four-column grid of uniform tall stills on grey, with blue one-word navigation.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Medium ~28px for the name and links; blue underlined links; '888' numerals and an O-ring logo are the only ornaments.
look.color: Light grey #dedede ground, pure blue links, gold '888' numerals; the photographs carry sky blue, signal red and pink.
look.layout: Four-item header (888, ring logo, name, info), then four columns of identical 4:5 images with narrow gutters; 'Index' and 'Next' float over the last tile.
look.imagery: Still lifes (red dice and ice, beans on graph paper, a bird, a rose in a hand) in saturated colour.

behaviour: Cargo grid: clicking an image opens its project; the 'Index / Next' control floats over the last tile; a '(site buildout ongoing)' note sits under info.
signature: A rose, a dice-and-ice cube and a bird share one crop and gutter, so very different subjects read as one voice.
why: A rigid grid and a single link colour put all the personality in the photographs; a uniform crop turns a varied practice into a recognisable set.
steal: Crop every image to one ratio, set the gutter at about 10px, and use exactly one link colour; let subject and colour supply all the variety.

title: Tooooools.app
name: Tooooools.app
one_line: Free browser image-effects tool (stippling, dithering, ASCII, CRT) whose hero is a live black-and-white effect on a photo.

look.type: JetBrains Mono 14px for everything; a chunky bubble-mono wordmark 'Tooooools' ~100px in charcoal #333; 12px mono pitch.
look.color: Warm paper #f9f8f5 with charcoal #333; the preview is pure black and white; one grey button; no accent colour.
look.layout: Centred stack: wordmark, two-line pitch, boxed 'Get started', then a wide preview frame; below, mono effect lists (/Effects, /animate) in columns.
look.imagery: A live effect preview: black vertical bars with stepped edges forming a figure; effects run on your own image.

behaviour: Upload, pick an effect (stippling, dots, dithering, bevel, cellular automata, CRT, ASCII), adjust, export, all in the browser with p5; Enter starts; an animate mode exists.
signature: The wordmark stretches its o's ('Tooooools') in a chunky bubble-mono, and…'s own output, not a screenshot.
why: A live, striking effect on load proves the tool in one second. One mono family with dotted rules gives a coherent, tool-like voice without chrome.
steal: Make the hero the product's real output on a sample…'/Effects', '/animate') over 1px dotted rules.

name: irony machine: rose
one_line: A pink page with twelve draggable GIF roses and one request: 'i'm tired. please decorate this page yourself.'

look.type: Times New Roman 20px in dark red, lowercase sentence; list items bold; everything boxed in a double-rule frame; nothing else.
look.color: Flat pink (--pink, ~#ffa8bb) with dark-red text and a red double border; the GIF roses add deep red and leaf green.
look.layout: Roses stacked in a column down the left edge; one ~310px double-bordered message box dead-centre; the rest of the pink is empty.
look.imagery: Twelve 90s embroidered-rose GIFs (buds, stems, garlands) in a vertical tray; no other pictures.

behaviour: Drag any rose onto the pink and drop it; click the message to dismiss it and a textarea lets you write your own text; jQuery drag.
signature: The designer hands the page over: 'i'm tired. please decorate this page yourself.' is both the brief and the toolbox.
why: A site that admits tiredness gives visitors a job, and decorating is pleasurable, so the visitor completes the design. One mechanic plus one honest sentence is the whole piece.
steal: Replace a finished layout with a toolbox: a tray of 10-15 draggable assets, a blank field and one honest sentence telling the visitor what to do.

title: More Love
name: More Love
one_line: A quiet display of affection: a field of red hearts, a camera prompt and three steps for sending love.

look.type: Arial Narrow 8-12px in red; caps nav (REFRESH, HOW TO LOVE); the 'MORE LOVE' logotype sets each letter in its own outlined pink circle.
look.color: Exactly two colours: heart red #f73131 and blush #ffd8d6, on white; a red hairline under the header.
look.layout: Thin header (refresh, logotype, how-to), then a vertical split: left half a lattice of thousands of tiny hearts, right half empty white.
look.imagery: Tiny heart glyphs on a regular lattice; letters in circles; no photos until the camera starts.

behaviour: Asks for camera access (p5, jQuery); steps: think of someone, make a heart over your head, hover, send an 'i<3u'; Refresh resets; best on desktop.
signature: The instructions read as a ritual ('think of someone you hold dear') and the whole site obeys a strict two-colour rule.
why: A tight constraint (two colours, one glyph, one narrow face) makes tenderness legible; gesture instructions turn the visitor's body into the interface, which is the affection.
steal: Limit a piece to two colours and one repeated glyph, then write the instructions as numbered gestures with circled digits that the visitor must perform.
moves: camera permission asked politely up front

title: Junior GD
name: Junior GD
one_line: A graphic-design course site: ASCII-art garden, syllabus text and a black rail of student site thumbnails, in three columns.

look.type: FK Grotesk family at ~14px: mono for ASCII art and schedules, neue for syllabus text; tight caps mono header nav.
look.color: Vertical gradient from pink-violet to mint green across two columns; black third column; black text; green #00c55d links.
look.layout: Three hairline-separated columns: ASCII art and presentation times, project syllabus with workshop link lists, a black rail of student thumbnails.
look.imagery: ASCII flowers and figures credited to Joan G. Stark; tiny screenshot thumbnails of student sites tagged OPEN LINK.

behaviour: Hand-built on Cargo, Glitch and GitHub Pages: schedule links to Glitch workshops, an Are.na-linked rail, masonry and glitch scripts, about 1,300 elements.
signature: An ASCII-art 'Junior Garden' (flowers, a figure saying thank you) lives inside the schedule, beside student presentation times.
why: The course site practises its own assignment: an archive-style website fed by collected links, so teaching and demonstration are one artefact. Gradient and mono keep it friendly but technical.
steal: Build a class site as a three-column sheet: ASCII banner and schedule, assignment text, and a rail of student work thumbnails; make the site practise the course.
moves: ASCII art as mascot and divider
syllabus, schedule and student work in one view

title: Muumuu House
name: Muumuu House
one_line: Indie literary press site built like a 2000s Word-exported page: 69pt Helvetica title, three links, dated news list.

look.type: Helvetica at default sizes; 'MUUMUU HOUSE' in caps at 69pt, centred; news lines ~13px with each date on its own line.
look.color: No colour declared: black on white, browser-default blue links, visited links forced to blue so nothing looks 'used'.
look.layout: A 780px centred table: title, 770px rules, 'ABOUT | BOOKS | STORE', then a 200px NEWS column beside a long list of about 400 links.
look.imagery: Essentially none: one tiny image; everything else is text links.

behaviour: Static legacy markup (body vlink, Mso classes, align=center); news items link to X, YouTube and venue sites; screenshot is a Chrome DNS error, so this is read from the HTML.
signature: A 69pt all-caps title and 400 plain links in a Word-era table: the press's seriousness is carried by refusing to style anything.
why: For a literary press the text is the product; browser defaults stay fast and readable and signal an anti-brand stance. Date-led news lines make the house's activity scannable.
steal: Lead each list item with the date on its own line, then one sentence with one inline link; set the title big and leave the rest at defaults.
moves: title as the only large type

title: Kanaal40
name: Kanaal40
one_line: Entry gate for a micropop broadcast space: a tilted plaster-textured 3D logo that doubles as the cookie button.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk bold with a bold-italic second line, ~14px, black, centred on the object: 'Click to enter / and accept cookies'.
look.color: Pure white ground, chalky off-white object with grey shading, black type; the main site later uses yellow #ffff00 and blue and green accents.
look.layout: One object dead-centre on empty white; the text sits on the object; nothing else on screen.
look.imagery: A sculpted logo with a chalky, scan-like surface, tilted as if turning on a plinth.

behaviour: One click enters and records cookie consent; WordPress with cursor-follow, mix-blend-difference and looping video and audio in the main site; 'submit your work' below.
signature: 'Click to enter and accept cookies': the consent notice is the front door, and the door is a 3D sculpture of the logo.
why: Merging the legal requirement with the entry ritual removes a second popup, and a physical-looking object on empty white sets the channel's tactile character before any content loads.
steal: Make the cookie notice the enter button: one centred object, one line 'Click to enter and accept cookies', nothing else on screen.

title: Systemantics
name: Systemantics
one_line: A web studio's entire homepage is one sentence whose highlighted words are the filters and links.

look.type: Solo Sys grotesk at one size (~80px, scaled by a --rem variable to fill the screen), set tight, left-aligned, in highlighted blocks.
look.color: White page; black block behind the name, grey #bfbfbf blocks behind sectors, pure lime #00ff00 blocks behind contact words; black text throughout.
look.layout: One ragged paragraph filling the viewport edge to edge; highlight blocks wrap word by word like marker pen; no header, footer or menu.
look.imagery: None: no images or icons; the highlighter blocks are the only graphics.

behaviour: Sectors are checkbox-role links (aria-checked) that filter the project portfolio; the black word is home; green words are contact and page links; Vue SSR with page transitions.
signature: Navigation written as a sentence: 'Systemantics develops websites in the fields…', colour-coded word by word.
why: Three highlight colours encode three roles (who we are, what we cover, how to reach us) inside normal prose, so the interface is read, not scanned, and needs no menu.
steal: Write your homepage as one sentence at 60px or larger and highlight only the words that are links; use one highlight colour per role (identity, topic filters, actions).
moves: one colour per role (identity, sectors, actions)
phone and email set inline in the sentence

title: polinsski site
name: polinsski site
one_line: An artist's site inhabited by a 'site-spirit' with an age and energy, a diary log and a draggable splitter.

look.type: IBM Plex Mono Italic ~13px in cornflower blue for the log; Heinz Beta serif for names and panel headers; links on grey highlight bars.
look.color: Butter-yellow ~#f0e4b3 ground with blue ink, set by an 'energy' stylesheet; the live page shows an inverted plum #431e2e and yellow theme.
look.layout: Three columns: wide diary log, a thin splitter of dotted arrows, a 300px side panel of site-spirit stats, weekly photo and a question.
look.imagery: A warm photo in a 'Sunday media' panel (ear, stone earring); an ASCII-noise 'sitewear' block for the spirit.

behaviour: Age counts days from a birth date; an energy stylesheet swaps the palette; older log lines fade; the splitter drags column widths; HTML comments speak in the spirit's voice.
signature: The site is alive: a birth date, an energy that changes its colours, and a voice in HTML comments addressed to the 'HTML Traveler'.
why: A character turns maintenance into narrative: visits feed the spirit and neglect fades the log. The question 'do you sometimes look at the…' rewards curiosity.
steal: Give your site a persistent state with a visible face (age in days, last update, 'energy'), let neglect fade older entries,…'s voice.
moves: site given a character with age and energy
HTML comments as a second voice

title: Critical Atlas of Internet
name: Critical Atlas of Internet
one_line: A research atlas of fifteen spatial hypotheses about the Internet, drawn as hairline diagrams under letter-spaced serif titling.

look.type: Extremely letter-spaced serif caps title, spaced lowercase subtitle, a text serif ~16px with slanted i-dots, a sans pull-quote in a dotted box.
look.color: White page with solid yellow #ffff00 strips down the left and right edges; black text, grey hairlines; yellow is the only colour.
look.layout: Wide margins; rotated 'INDEX' and 'ABOUT' on the side edges at mid-height, 'Francais' top-right; a framed diagram beside a Perec quote box.
look.imagery: A thin grey network diagram: about twenty outlined boxes with crossing arrows inside a dotted frame, plotter-like.

behaviour: The live page did not load, so behaviour is unclear; the rotated edge labels look like navigation, and a language switch sits top-right.
signature: Index and About live on the screen edges as rotated tiny labels between two raw-yellow strips, leaving the centre to the text.
why: Edge-mounted nav gives the page the margins of a printed atlas; one hot colour used only at the borders makes the white interior look carefully held.
steal: Rotate navigation labels 90 degrees into the left and right margins at 9px with wide tracking, and add one flat colour strip along each edge as the page's only colour.
moves: vertical edge nav in the margins
quote in a dotted box beside the diagram
single bright colour only at the borders

title: The catalogue of UK Entrances to Hell
name: Entrances to Hell (UK)
one_line: A deadpan 2002 catalogue of UK 'entrances to Hell' in default HTML with cyan link bars and one photograph.

look.type: Browser-default sans via font tags: ~40px bold blue underlined link as headline, bold-italic ~18px tagline, 9px footer.
look.color: White page, cyan #99ffff bars behind links, default link blue; the photograph supplies brick brown and soot black.
look.layout: A centred ~690px table: link bar, headline box, tagline, a 620px photo, 'most popular entrance' link, a repeated link bar, tiny footer.
look.imagery: One documentary photograph of a bricked-up arch under a railway viaduct, with graffiti and soot.

behaviour: Static tables, no JavaScript, 2 KB of HTML; the headline is a link; a weekly 'MOST POPULAR ENTRANCE' line ranks one page.
signature: A bureaucratic format applied straight-faced to the absurd: 'This week's MOST POPULAR ENTRANCE is Quetty Orarna.'
why: Deadpan tone plus a documentary photo of a mundane bricked arch is the joke; the unstyled 2002 template guarantees sincerity. Content, not decoration, carries the design.
steal: Pick an absurd subject and give it dull institutional structure (catalogue, 'this week's most popular', 'your emails') in default type; let one plain photo do the rest.
moves: link bar repeated above and below

title: FICHTRE! ® - Sébastien Cappuccia - Marseille
name: FICHTRE!
one_line: A one-screen GIF-built homepage: royal-blue scanline field, a white dog-head logo and pixel-lettered links in the corner.

look.type: Pixel outline lettering for FICHTRE and tiny bitmap caps for names and links, all baked into GIFs; white and pink.
look.color: Cobalt blue (~#1f3bff) filled with 1px white interlace lines, a white logo, hot-pink link labels.
look.layout: A header block in the top-left ~250px (logo, name, two link rows); the rest of the screen is an unbroken pattern field.
look.imagery: 13 GIFs in two tables: a dog-head mascot, pixel icons (floppy, wifi, heart), a tiled scanline background.

behaviour: Static 5 KB page; the text is images; the background tiles; links go to contact, Instagram and a second name's page.
signature: A whole screen of tiled white scanlines on blue with a tiny header in the corner: all the weight is texture.
why: A 5 KB page can feel immersive when the pattern is bold and the content tiny; scale contrast and a two-hue palette give it identity. The cost: text as images is inaccessible.
steal: Use a tiled 2-4px bitmap pattern in two colours as the whole ground and park a small pixel-lettered header in the corner; give every GIF alt text.
moves: tiled scanline pattern as the page
everything built from GIFs in tables

title: 258pm salon
name: 258pm salon
one_line: A vintage-clothing shop whose homepage is hand-drawn marker category cards scattered down white, captioned as filenames.

look.type: Space Mono 12-16px in chocolate brown #5f330b for nav and captions; a handwritten-script logo; lowercase file-name captions like '_new arrivals_258.jpg'.
look.color: White ground, brown ink; each card a different scribble in teal, yellow-green, pink, orange or black marker on whiteboard grey.
look.layout: Cards of differing sizes, ~16px rounded corners, soft shadows, staggered left and right in a loose zigzag; thin Shop / logo / Cart bar.
look.imagery: Marker doodles of '258 PM SALON': spirals, a C-curve, numbers 1-9, circled letters; no product photos on the first screen.

behaviour: Shopify theme with scroll-snap, container queries and :has() selectors; each card is a category link; a small banner announces an event (11.14+11.15).
signature: Shop categories are hand-doodled whiteboard cards labelled with raw file names, laid out in a loose zigzag instead of a product grid.
why: Doodles replace stock imagery and make a resale boutique feel personal; file-name labels add a desktop-folder joke. The zigzag slows scrolling so each category lands alone.
steal: Replace category thumbnails with one hand-drawn card per category, label each with a fake file name in mono, and stagger them left and right down the page.
moves: event banner as a tiny top line

title: Plain Text Sports
name: Plain Text Sports
one_line: Live sports scores as typewriter text: ASCII box scores with winners bold and losers grey, in one narrow column.

look.type: Courier 13px throughout, centred; bold for winners and headings, grey for losers; links in periwinkle; no other sizes.
look.color: White page or #101010 with #f0f0f0 text via a Dark Mode toggle; periwinkle #9090ff links; red, green and blue appear only as status colours.
look.layout: A single narrow centred column: load timestamps, date arrows, league links, then two-up grids of ASCII boxes.
look.imagery: No images: score boxes are +, - and | characters; the Super Bowl champion gets an ASCII trophy.

behaviour: Each score box is one link to its game page; 'Page loaded' and 'Data loaded (~15 seconds ago)' stamps show freshness; light and dark toggle; 36 KB total.
signature: Box-drawn scorecards made of plus signs and pipes, each box a link, with data-freshness timestamps printed at the top.
why: Zero decoration gives instant load, perfect scanning and one visual rule (bold means winner). Freshness stamps make the data trustworthy, and the ASCII trophy adds one smile for free.
steal: Render tabular data as fixed-width text boxes, use only bold and grey to rank, make the whole box the link, and print the load time at the top.
moves: ASCII box as card and link

title: Other Office
name: Other Office
one_line: A design studio's project viewer framed by outlined text boxes pinned to every screen edge: name, nav, counter.

look.type: A neutral grotesk ~13px for nav labels and a book serif ~13px for project controls ('Previous Project', 'Girl Outdoor'), each in a 1px black box.
look.color: Pale cream-yellow (~#fbfff0) ground, black text and 1px black borders; the project media (blank in the capture) would supply all colour.
look.layout: Boxed labels line all four edges: title and arrows on top, info down the sides, counter '1 / 8' at bottom; centre empty for work.
look.imagery: None in the capture (work area blank); the outlined labels are the only graphic.

behaviour: The live page returned 403, so this is read from the 2020 capture: a project slideshow with previous and next studio projects and a '1 / 8' counter.
signature: The studio name is split across opposite corners ('Other' top-left, 'Office' bottom-right), so the whole viewport becomes its logotype.
why: Pinning nav to the viewport edges frees the centre for the work and makes the window itself the layout; outlined boxes look like form buttons, a quiet systematic identity.
steal: Pin 12 to 16 small 1px-bordered labels to the viewport edges, keep the centre empty for the work, and split your studio name across two opposite corners.
moves: navigation pinned to all four edges

title: Oneohtrix Point Never: Archive
name: Oneohtrix Point Never
one_line: Artist site whose saved screen is a boxed status line, 'Oneohtrix Point Never : Loading.'; now an album-campaign page.

look.type: Tight heavy grotesk (Helvetica-like bold, negative tracking) ~30px black; elsewhere Pantasia, Parabolica and Helvetica Narrow.
look.color: Light grey #eee ground, black type, a hairline grey box; today's CSS adds cyan #00bbff accents and #fffff7 pages.
look.layout: One hairline-bordered label dead-centre on empty grey; today a multi-section page with tracklist headings A1, A2, A3.
look.imagery: None in the capture; the loader is pure type.

behaviour: Vite with Swup page transitions, Alpine and Swiper; Bandcamp embeds; the loading line is the first thing every visitor sees.
signature: The loading screen is the title card: artist name, a colon and 'Loading.' in a hairline box, set in a tight heavy grotesk.
why: Turning the wait state into a typographic statement gives the site a voice before any content arrives; the colon and full stop make the sentence read like a file label.
steal: Design the loader as a one-line label in your display face inside a hairline box on flat grey ('Name : Loading.') and keep that box language afterwards.
moves: hairline box around a type line

title: Another Graphic
name: Another Graphic
one_line: An archive of typographic graphic design: a four-column grid of black-matted posters and spreads under grey name bars.

look.type: Monotesk mono-grotesk: ~28px logotype, 16px bulleted designer names on grey bars, 10-12px caps for LIST VIEW, SHOP and ABOUT.
look.color: Light grey #f0f0f0 page, #c8c8c8 name bars, black image mats, one cobalt #0000d2 pill for SHOP and the cart count.
look.layout: Top bar; 4-column grid of equal cards (grey name strip over a black square field); fixed bottom bar with About, Search, Newsletter and socials.
look.imagery: Posters, book spreads and zines photographed flat and centred on black; very different type treatments side by side.

behaviour: Grid and List toggle; about 100 entries per page; WordPress with search, newsletter and a shop; a cookie banner and an ad overlay cover the footer.
signature: Every design object sits on the same black square under only the designer's name: the mat standardises a wildly varied archive.
why: A uniform black mat and one-line caption let the typography inside each piece be the only variable, so you compare treatments. The Grid and List toggle serves both browsers and researchers.
steal: For a visual archive, mat every item on the same black field, caption it with only the maker's name in 16px mono on a grey strip; add a grid/list toggle.

title: Contributions
name: Critical Coding Cookbook
one_line: A cookbook of critical-coding recipes, filterable by meal and language, on a hot-pink field with outlined cards.

look.type: Avara Bold quirky serif 20-32px for headings and nav; Tiresias PC, an accessibility sans, at 12px for excerpts; centred text.
look.color: Hot pink-magenta (~#ff8cff) ground, black 3px outlines and text, light grey nav bar, a pink knob on the toggles.
look.layout: Header with nav and two toggles; centred line-drawn coil logo; two rows of pill filters; then three-column cards with ~50px corner radii.
look.imagery: One black line drawing of stacked rings as the logo; no photographs; outlines and hashtags carry the look.

behaviour: Pill filters (breakfast, lunch, dinner, p5, javascript, python, sql); 'Effects Off' and 'Light' toggles, stored in localStorage; Accessibility and Downloads pages.
signature: Meal names (breakfast, lunch, dinner) become the first filter, and every contribution is a heavy-outlined card with tags.
why: One metaphor (cooking) renames a technical library and makes it welcoming; heavy outlines on a single flat colour give strong contrast, and an 'Effects Off' switch is built in.
steal: Name your categories with one domestic metaphor (meals) and put a visible 'Effects Off' toggle beside the theme switch so motion is optional on page one.

title: Ola Radio
name: Ola Radio
one_line: A webradio's framed home: left rail with DIRECT play cell and black block links, vertical INFORMATIONS strip, centred logo.

look.type: Heavy monospace caps 14-16px (Space Mono-like); 'INFORMATIONS' rotated 90 degrees at ~28px on the right edge; hand-lettered 'Ola' logo.
look.color: Pure black on white; 1.5px black rules between panels; no other colour.
look.layout: Three zones split by black rules: a 200px rail (logo, DIRECT, buttons), an empty centre with the logo, a 55px rotated-label strip.
look.imagery: A hand-drawn logo: a black spiky burst with a white open hand and squiggly 'Ola' lettering, used small and large.

behaviour: DIRECT with a play arrow presumably starts the stream; PODCASTS, OLGA PRODUCTIONS and DON are black block links. The saved URL now returns a Next.js 404.
signature: One hand-drawn burst logo used twice (rail and stage) inside a rigid black-ruled frame, with the single word DIRECT as the play control.
why: A strict three-zone frame with one illustration keeps a radio site calm; the live-play control sits at the top of the rail where hands expect it, and black blocks make big targets.
steal: Frame an app as ruled panels (rail, stage, edge strip), put the 'live' control at the rail's top with one verb, rotate the info label 90 degrees.

title: Virtual Enjoyment
name: Virtual Enjoyment
one_line: A research project's lecture series: pale pink dusted with magenta ink flecks, lecture cards in a row along the bottom.

look.type: A wide high-contrast Didone-like serif in magenta: 'VIRTUAL ENJOYMENT' caps ~24px; lecture titles in italic serif ~12px, names and dates roman.
look.color: Two colours only: blush (~#ffe4e4) ground and hot magenta (~#ff0080) for type, borders and every fleck; tabs are solid or outlined magenta.
look.layout: Small 'Lectures' tab top-left, title centred, '2022' outlined tab top-right, a full-screen speckle field, outlined lecture cards in a strip along the bottom edge.
look.imagery: Hundreds of tiny magenta flecks and hatch marks scattered like dust or seeds; no photographs.

behaviour: The live page did not load, so unclear; the flecks look like a canvas or SVG field that may drift or react to the cursor; the lecture cards run on sideways.
signature: A full-screen scatter of tiny magenta marks in a strict two-colour palette, with the programme tucked into outlined cards at the bottom edge.
why: A two-tone riso-like palette makes a heavy theory topic feel tactile; keeping the programme in a fixed strip under the field means the atmosphere never hides the information.
steal: Pick one hot ink on a pale tint of the same hue, scatter hundreds of tiny marks as texture, and pin the schedule in outlined cards along the bottom edge.

title: Pair Up
name: Pair Up
one_line: A site for creatives to trade time: lime hero, giant tumbling wordmark, phone mock of profiles; now a farewell notice.

look.type: Riegla chunky rounded grotesk ~250px for the wordmark, every letter rotated differently; 16px sans body; black pill buttons.
look.color: Lime (~#e5ff7f) hero on cream #faf5e8, black ink, dark-green, blue, peach, pink and yellow blob avatars; saturated but warm.
look.layout: Rounded lime panel inset 12px, wordmark across the top, intro and buttons bottom-left, phone mock bottom-right, four blob tiles below.
look.imagery: Abstract flat-colour blob avatars (arches, U shapes) instead of faces; a phone UI mock cut off by the panel.

behaviour: Next.js app with sign-up and log-in; 38 rotate transforms tilt letters and cards; today's page is a long farewell notice with FAQ anchors and a waitlist.
signature: The letters of 'Pair Up' are tilted and overlapped like stickers, so the wordmark looks like people leaning on each other.
why: One huge wordmark and flat-colour blobs give a brand in one glance; abstract avatars avoid portrait bias and keep every profile visually even.
steal: Give each letter of the wordmark a slight different rotation and overlap, set it at 200px+ on a rounded flat-colour panel, and use abstract blob avatars instead of photos.
moves: phone mock cropped by the panel

title: Light-Water: Mosaic
name: Light-Water: a Mosaic of Meditations
one_line: Mid-2000s electronic literature: ten poem links scattered as mauve tiles with water images on a near-black page.

look.type: Times italic title ~24px in dull olive, author line in roman; tile labels in dark serif ~16px laid over each image.
look.color: Near-black purple #0e0814 with faint scanlines; translucent mauve tiles; olive-gold light on water; a pale-yellow Post-it.
look.layout: Title top-centre, ten word-tiles dropped irregularly across the upper half, two smoky figures between them, the sticky note lower-left.
look.imagery: Each tile holds a tiny oval crop of sunlit water; smoky olive shapes float between tiles like fish or oil.

behaviour: Each tile links to one meditation page; a rotated yellow sticky note from the Electronic Literature Lab explains the 2023 repair and offers 'close note'. The URL 404s today.
signature: A rotated yellow sticky note from the archive's conservators sits on the dark poem, saying what they changed in 2023.
why: Archival honesty becomes a design element: the conservator's note is dated and dismissable and leaves the original artwork intact. Scattered word-tiles let readers wander rather than read in order.
steal: When restoring old work, annotate it with a dismissable sticky note stating what changed and when, instead of silently patching or rewriting it.
moves: poem navigation as scattered word tiles
oval-cropped image behind each link word

title: Coffee Receipt Stories
name: Coffee Receipt Stories
one_line: A collection of stories drawn on coffee receipts; the intro is pencil hand-lettering on pale grey with a scroll cue.

look.type: Hand-drawn all-caps pencil lettering ~20px with an uneven baseline, a drawn dashed underline under 'a little story', a tiny drawn 'SCROLL' label.
look.color: Pale grey #ebebeb ground and graphite-grey lettering only; nothing else in the first view.
look.layout: A centred ~650px block of short paragraphs with generous breathing room, a right-aligned signature with dashes, a drawn arrow centred below.
look.imagery: Drawn marks only: dashed underlines, a pencil arrow, the signature 'ODDING' over a dashed rule.

behaviour: Readymag scroll story; the drawn arrow invites you down into the receipts; no page text exists in the HTML (everything is drawn).
signature: The artist's own pencil handwriting is the…'scroll' cue.
why: Hand lettering tells the origin story in the same medium as the work, so you trust it. Grey space and a tiny cue make the first screen feel like a quiet notebook page.
steal: Letter your intro by hand (or in a handwriting face) at about 20px on pale grey, sign it, and add a drawn arrow cue instead of a 'Scroll down' button.

title: Webpage title
name: A Vertical Geography of Mushrooms
one_line: A graduation thesis using mushrooms as research method: wobbly serif title, white outline fungi on grey.

look.type: Basteleur-style soft wobbly serif ~65px in mid-grey (~#6b6b6b) for the title; smaller faces (Azeret mono, Be Vietnam, Latitude) deeper in; system cursor hidden.
look.color: White-to-pale-grey vertical gradient, grey type, white chalky outlines, one glowing green dot and a thin green line at the left edge.
look.layout: Title top-left, then a loose scatter of ten fungus outlines in rough rows with wide gaps; a green line runs down the left edge.
look.imagery: Chalky white contour drawings of mushroom forms with slightly noisy edges, like scraped or etched lines.

behaviour: The system cursor is hidden and replaced by a glowing green follower; 11,000 words and 268 links in the thesis; WordPress export on GitHub Pages.
signature: A glowing green dot replaces the cursor over pale-grey paper covered in white chalk-line mushrooms, like a spore moving through fog.
why: Low-contrast white drawings on grey read as fog or frost, a mood suited to hidden growth; the one glowing cursor is the only saturated element, so it guides attention. Risk: legibility.
steal: Replace the cursor with a soft 12px glow in one saturated colour on an otherwise grey page; keep decorative drawings low-contrast and body text at full contrast.
moves: white outline drawings on grey gradient

title: SLOW NET
name: Slow Net
one_line: A 4 KB default-HTML page documenting a zine, a slow chat and a slow router built against data collection.

look.type: Times New Roman at browser defaults: 40px caps title, centred italic standfirst, 12-18px paragraphs with first-line indents, bold subheads.
look.color: Black on white with default blue #0000ee links; the only tone is a warm-grey sepia photograph.
look.layout: A centred ~800px column: title, standfirst, a bordered photo, a numbered link list, a dotted rule, then essay paragraphs and nested lists.
look.imagery: Monochrome flat-lay photo: a zine with a snail drawing, a phone showing the chat, a Raspberry Pi with network cable.

behaviour: Static page, no JavaScript, 4 KB; three numbered links lead to the zine, the chat and the router.
signature: The page enacts its argument: 4 KB of Times New Roman, no scripts, nothing to track, for a project about resisting data capture.
why: Form enacts argument: a site about resisting data collection loads instantly and asks for nothing. The single photo lays out the whole project (zine, phone, router) in one arrangement.
steal: Open a project page with one flat-lay photo of all its parts (print, phone, hardware) under a one-sentence italic standfirst, then a three-item numbered list of entry points.
moves: flat-lay photo of all project parts
dotted rule between overview and essay

title: Online Omnichord
name: Online Omnichord
one_line: A playable web replica of the Suzuki Omnichord: chord buttons, strum plate, rhythm pads, drawn as a flat illustration.

look.type: Tiny blue sans labels (MAJOR, MINOR, 7TH, ROCK, WALTZ) about 9px on the instrument; an italic outlined blue logo; 'info/instructions' in default link blue.
look.color: Sky-blue (~#bcd2ff) page, white body with navy outlines, cream-yellow keys on a tan plate, pink rhythm pads, a red power LED.
look.layout: One huge instrument filling the viewport at a slight perspective tilt with a drop shadow; one tiny link at the bottom-right.
look.imagery: A flat illustration of the instrument: sloped chord grid, strum plate of cream keys, speaker-grille dots, a faux-3D side edge.

behaviour: Press chord buttons, drag across the strum plate for harp notes, pick a rhythm, tempo and volume; Howler/Web Audio, keyboard shortcuts; React app.
signature: The interface is a full-size drawing of a real instrument, with its original labels and logo, that you can play immediately.
why: Skeuomorphic fidelity removes any need for onboarding: people who know the object know the page. One screen, one object, one tiny info link.
steal: If your tool replicates a physical object, draw it at full viewport scale with its real labels and make every control work before adding any explanatory text.

title: BP
name: BP (badpreacher)
one_line: A designer-DJ's Cargo site split into 'For your eyes' posters and 'For your ears' SoundCloud mixes.

look.type: Diatype ~19px in grey on black for the two lead-ins; underlined grey links; the posters supply all display lettering.
look.color: Black (~#101010) ground, grey text; posters bring mercury chrome, orange, cyan, pink and violet; SoundCloud cards add orange accents.
look.layout: Two-thirds and one-third split: left a gutterless mosaic of posters, right a rail of stacked SoundCloud players with '- past recording -' dividers.
look.imagery: Club-night posters with ornate chrome lettering, dragons and dancing figures, cropped edge to edge in rows.

behaviour: Cargo loads 85 images; captions such as 'Zhao Dai pres.' Series (Ongoing) sit between rows; SoundCloud iframes play in place.
signature: The header splits in two, 'For your eyes as PJ/BADPREACHER' beside 'For your ears as DJ TRUCK', and the page follows.
why: Two practices (design, DJing) become two columns with their own alias, so a visitor can choose a sense and the site stays uncluttered. A black ground lets loud posters glow.
steal: Name your two practices by the sense they address ('for your eyes / for your ears'), and give each its own column with matching media embedded in place.

title: Neurodiversity Design System
name: Neurodiversity Design System
one_line: A design system for learning platforms made with neurodiverse users, shown as eight colour-coded icon tiles.

look.type: Atkinson Hyperlegible Bold 48px headline, 18px regular body at generous leading, 16px bold tile labels; one family, large sizes, left-aligned.
look.color: Pale sage header, eight pastel tiles (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, violet, pink) with black outline icons and a darker bottom edge.
look.layout: Open Menu button and logo top-left, big headline and standfirst, then a 4 x 2 grid of square tiles with generous gaps.
look.imagery: Black 2px line icons: numerals, a db/qp letterform study, a text box, colour wheel, cursor and hand, speech bubbles.

behaviour: Static pages with no JavaScript (157 KB of CSS); the menu is a labelled button; colour-scheme and reduced-motion media queries are honoured; each tile opens a rules page.
signature: Each principle is a coloured tile with a thick bottom edge like a physical button, and its icon spells out the rule (db/qp for letterforms).
why: The site follows its own rules: one legible typeface, big type, icon plus label redundancy, flat colour blocks and no motion. Tiles make eight topics scannable and unambiguous.
steal: Build the home as a grid of big colour tiles, each with one 2px line icon, a bold label and a 4px darker bottom edge that reads as pressable.

name: Sun Stream
one_line: A browser clock that is a 24-hour song whose sound follows available light; its title is made of white dots.

look.type: 'SUN STREAM'built from white dots (SVG), stacked…'Warming up...' in tiny 11px type at the bottom; Superstudio and Maison Neue elsewhere.
look.color: Taupe-grey vertical gradient (~#a39e95 to #8a8279) with a soft butter-yellow (#f2f6ba) sun glow behind the letters.
look.layout: Everything centred: the stacked dotted title in the middle, the glow behind it, a loading line at the bottom edge.
look.imagery: A blurred yellow sun disc and a dot-matrix wordmark on a soft grey sky.

behaviour: Per its description: 14 sun positions map to 14 audio loops, extra layers are generated live, bells mark each hour, and the mix follows the visitor's available light (mechanism unclear).
signature: A dotted title lit by a soft yellow sun that quietly moves through 14 positions as the day's light, and the music, change.
why: Sound, colour and time are driven by one variable (light), so a quiet screen holds a whole day; even the loading line 'Warming up...' belongs to the same metaphor.
steal: Drive background colour, sound and one glow from a single environmental variable (hour or light) and let the loading text speak in that metaphor ('Warming up...').
moves: one variable drives sound and colour

title: Oracle Cards of Design Manifestos
name: Oracle Cards of Design Manifestos
one_line: An oracle-card randomiser: each refresh deals a quote from a design manifesto on tilted blue-on-lime cards.

look.type: Blue grotesk ~28px on the cards with bold serif emphasis; a chiselled display serif ~110px for the ghosted title behind them.
look.color: Exactly two colours: acid lime-green (~#2ed100) and electric blue (~#1a1aff), with blue glow shadows; all text and outlines are blue.
look.layout: Two big rounded cards tilted a few degrees and stacked down the screen, ghost title behind, diamond 'Ready?' and round 'Shuffle' buttons top-right.
look.imagery: No images: cards, glow shadows and giant type only; a small round 'R/m' mark bottom-left.

behaviour: Readymag scroll story; the 'Ready?' and 'Shuffle' buttons suggest drawing a card; per the rules, each refresh deals a new manifesto line.
signature: Two-colour poster logic: electric blue on acid green, with cards tilted like dealt tarot and a blue glow in place of a drop shadow.
why: A maximum-contrast pair is the whole identity, so cards, buttons and title need nothing else; the oracle metaphor turns reading quotes into the ritual of drawing one.
steal: Choose two clashing saturated colours (blue and lime), use one as ground and the other for everything else, and replace drop shadows with a soft glow of the text colour.

title: Home Page
name: Magical Mushroom Company
one_line: A mushroom-packaging company's homepage: motion-blurred factory photo behind six colour-coded pill nav buttons.

look.type: Suisse Int'l: bold caps stacked wordmark ~26px, 20px regular in the pills, 13px cookie text; caps headline below the fold.
look.color: Earth-toned pills: sage, burnt orange, charcoal brown, coral, forest green, plum; the photograph adds steel grey and pink light.
look.layout: Hamburger top-left, wordmark top-centre, nav pills wrapping onto two rows over the photograph, a white cookie card bottom-right.
look.imagery: A motion-blurred worker in a grow room, racks of white mycelium bricks on steel shelves under pink light.

behaviour: Next.js; hover and mask effects in the CSS; cookie consent offers 'Necessary Only' beside 'Accept All' with equal weight.
signature: Six nav pills, each a different mushroom-earth colour with an arrow, float over a motion-blurred worker in the grow room.
why: The photograph shows the product being made at scale, which proves the claim; colour-coded pills give wayfinding a palette drawn from the material. Equal-weight cookie buttons are honest.
steal: Over a hero photo, offer nav as pill buttons coloured from the product's own palette with a trailing arrow, so the main routes show without opening a menu.

name: Sky Scraping
one_line: A full-screen looping sky video plus five hidden PNGs that a cursor script reveals; a 'sky-scraping' pun.

look.type: One 12px sans-serif white credit block bottom-right (concept, footage, copyright); no other text.
look.color: Deep sky blue with white cumulus clouds, all from the footage; white credit text; nothing added.
look.layout: Fixed full-bleed video, overflow hidden so nothing scrolls; five absolutely positioned images hidden until the script shows them.
look.imagery: Looping sky footage with one animal-shaped cumulus; five PNG overlays that are not visible in the capture.

behaviour: A cursor-follow script (not captured) likely shows or moves image-1 to image-5 over the muted autoplay video; 2 KB of HTML, no framework.
signature: A pun staged on a looping cloud video, driven by a cursor script: 'sky-scraping' with (presumably) towers following the pointer.
why: One strong video plus one mechanic is enough; the credit line names concept and cinematographer separately, which models good attribution. A tiny file gives an immediate payoff.
steal: Use a fixed, muted, looping video as the whole page and attach one cursor-driven behaviour to it; credit concept and footage separately in 12px white text in a corner.
moves: credit line separating concept from footage

title: volvox.observer
name: Volvox Observer
one_line: A public diary anyone can write into, set inside a pond-themed community site of tabs, archive and chat.

look.type: Hershey plotter fonts as web fonts: engraved-looking serif caps for titles, monoline geometric sans for body, set small with airy leading.
look.color: Charcoal #212121 sidebar tabs, lilac header bar, cards in pale lime-white #f3f9e6 with plum #664c71 text; yellow-green #9acd32 elsewhere in the CSS.
look.layout: Full-height sidebar of stacked dark tab blocks split by hairlines; a centred 500px form card and two info cards over a tiled photo.
look.imagery: Wood-grain photograph as the desk surface; an algae-bloom texture in the CSS; no other images.

behaviour: Vue single-page app on Glitch: diary form submits entries (100-word minimum) to a public archive; hit counter, p5 sketches, glitch and title animation, a pond chat room.
signature: The entry form is written as a letter: 'Dear diary,' above the textarea, 'Love,' above name and email, then 'send'.
why: Form labels become salutation and sign-off, so submitting feels like writing rather than filling fields; the wood desk and soft palette make the site read as a physical object.
steal: Rename every form field as a line of the genre you are collecting: 'Dear diary,', 'Love,', 'send'. Put the form on a photographed material, not a white page.
moves: plotter fonts as the UI face

title: Websitesite
name: Websitesite
one_line: One full-width table indexing every small website Jisu has made, with year, function and version thumbnails.

look.type: Basier-style grotesk (Arial fallback) at 9 to 15px, centred in every cell; bold header row; links in plain underlined blue.
look.color: White page, black 1px table rules, screen-blue links (#0074ff); mint #04e890 is declared for accents but barely visible.
look.layout: One 7-column table: three thumbnail columns (v.1 v.2 v.3), Title, Year, Function, Description; centred text, tight rows.
look.imagery: 43 tiny screenshot thumbnails, mostly near-blank pages, with a few saturated yellow, green and black ones.

behaviour: Static table on GitHub Pages with a little jQuery keyboard handling. Every row links out to a separate small site; no filtering or search.
signature: A 'Function' column labels each site by what it does: Joke, Phone, Fortune teller, Signage, Webzine, Answering machine.
why: Classifying work by function instead of medium turns a portfolio table into a witty inventory, and v.1/v.2/v.3 thumbnails record revisions in the same row without any extra page.
steal: Index your projects in one bare table with a Function column and version thumbnails; name each function with a plain noun like 'Signage' or 'Joke', never 'web design'.
moves: default-blue links in a ruled table

title: HFBK Bühnenraum
name: HFBK Bühnenraum
one_line: An art-school stage-design project index where each title is preceded by a strip of that project's thumbnails.

look.type: Hybrid 'timesnewarial' face: serif header nav, sans titles, all at one vw-scaled size with line-height 1 so rows pack solid.
look.color: Pure white ground, black text, no accent; all colour comes from stage and installation photographs in the strips.
look.layout: Each row is a left-aligned thumbnail strip of variable width followed by its title, so title starts stair-step across the page.
look.imagery: Dozens of tiny stage and installation photographs butted edge to edge; some strips run past the viewport.

behaviour: One Kirby page holds 81 projects, 411 images and 15,000 words, so projects likely open in place; blend-difference and drag listeners present. Exact behaviour unclear.
signature: Strip length equals image count, so every title is preceded by a bar chart of how much documentation the project has.
why: The index carries data in its own shape: row length encodes project size while the text stays plain. You scan texture first, then read titles; no icons, filters or captions needed.
steal: Replace bullets in a project list with a strip of that project's images, left-aligned and butted together; let strip length vary and put the title at its end.

title: Gegenwart: Doing Youth
name: Gegenwart: Doing Youth
one_line: Festival site for a Hamburg exhibition-and-performance project, written with lookalike glyphs and kaomoji on black.

look.type: vw-sized system sans, white, tight leading; headline and 'MENU' bold with an eight-way chartreuse text-shadow outline; labels respelled with syllabics and katakana lookalikes.
look.color: Pure black ground, white text, lilac #e599f7 and baby-blue #95e7f6 fills with chartreuse outline; neon only on headings, logos and menu.
look.layout: One wide left-aligned text column filling the screen, stacked title lines, menu word top-right; long text scrolls on a 3D drum.
look.imagery: No pictures: ASCII kaomoji like (っ^‿^)っ and box-drawing runs act as inline ornaments within sentences.

behaviour: Lines roll in on a 3D drum (translate3d plus rotateX of 120deg under 250px perspective); blinking carets, large hover states; jQuery with mousemove and drag listeners.
signature: Menu and title are respelled in lookalike glyphs (ᘻ乇刀ひ for MENU, ᕲのﾉᘉᘜ for DOING): English you can read but that feels alien.
why: Youth slang is mimicked in letterforms, not copy: the strangeness is a skin you can read through, while body text stays plain and large. Kaomoji punctuate sentences like private jokes.
steal: Respell two or three labels (menu, title) with lookalike glyphs from another script; keep body copy in a plain system sans at large size so reading stays easy.

title: Hallo Festspiele
name: Hallo Festspiele
one_line: A festival programme as plain text under a fixed 20-column grid of tiles that invert regions of the page.

look.type: Neutral sans at about 32px (vw-scaled): roman for dates, regular-weight titles with a 2px underline, italic for venues; blank gaps between days.
look.color: Light grey #f7f6f6 paper under black text, a noise overlay at 70%, and difference-blended tiles that flip patches to white-on-black.
look.layout: Three nav items pinned to viewport edges (Program top-left, Info + Press top-right, Blog bottom-left); the schedule fills one wide column.
look.imagery: No pictures; a tiled noise PNG covers everything, and inner-page images are forced to greyscale.

behaviour: Fixed difference-blend tile grid with pointer-events off; scripts toggle tiles (mousemove and random listeners; Web Audio also loaded); exact trigger unclear. Images open full-screen.
signature: A checkerboard of difference-blend tiles flips patches between black-on-noise and white-on-black, like a test pattern laid over the schedule.
why: One blend mode turns plain HTML into a graphic field with no images: the programme stays selectable text while a separate layer supplies all the drama, which suits a sound festival.
steal: Lay a fixed, pointer-events:none grid of black squares over a text page with mix-blend-mode: difference; toggle some squares to white to invert the text beneath them.

title: Dweller Forever
name: Dweller Forever
one_line: A reading library of articles, interviews and documentaries on techno and house history, set like a hex dump.

look.type: Full-width extra-extended heavy sans logotype over letter-spaced 'ELECTRONICS'; grotesk body about 15px; tiny grey mono nav; 48px section titles.
look.color: Pure black ground, off-white text, mid-grey nav and line numbers; no accent colour at all.
look.layout: Left gutter numbers every line in hex (001 … 00A, 00B …); content is one wide column with a title, author, year list.
look.imagery: No images: the giant logotype, hex numerals and dashed hairline rules carry all the graphics.

behaviour: Unclear: the live page offered only a t.co redirect stub. The screenshot shows a static blog library page with dashed rules and a three-column list.
signature: A hexadecimal line-number gutter runs the full height of the page, so every line of text has a memory address.
why: Numbering reframes a reading list as machine memory, which suits a site about electronic music, and gives a long list a rhythm to scroll against, with zero imagery.
steal: Add a 10px monospace gutter that counts every text line in hexadecimal, grey on black; it makes any plain text column feel like a dump of source.

title: Saint Heron
name: Saint Heron
one_line: A creative collective's 2020 homepage: a mustard graph-paper field with the name stretched along a diagonal dimension line.

look.type: SAINT in light grotesk caps, HERON in italic serif caps, both around 36px; 8px bold caps for the ticker and mission text.
look.color: Mustard-olive ground with near-black hairlines and type; one hue, no accent.
look.layout: Whole screen is a graph-paper grid of tall cells; a 1px diagonal runs from a circle marker to a square marker joining the name halves.
look.imagery: No images: grid, circle and square markers, and a small rotating circular logo top-left.

behaviour: A top ticker scrolls every division (Studio, Design, Press, Records, Sounds, Films, Dossier). Today the domain redirects to a Nuxt-built PIN-UP encyclopedia instead; grid behaviour unclear.
signature: SAINT and HERON sit at the ends of a diagonal dimension line across graph paper, one in sans, one in italic serif.
why: The name is drawn as a measurement on a drafting sheet, implying a practice that measures and builds; the two typefaces split it into craft and heritage, all in one colour and one grid.
steal: Place a two-word name at opposite corners, join the words with a hairline and small end markers, and give the ground a visible grid in the text colour.
moves: name split across a dimension line
sans plus italic serif in one name

title: Tilling Soil
name: Tilling Soil
one_line: A short illustrated essay of garden lessons where list items become hand-drawn stickers with slanted captions.

look.layout: A narrow centred text column, then stickers and tilted captions break out below it, scattered as if on a table.

signature: A bulleted list becomes a spatial collage: each item gets a doodle and a tilted caption placed freely, with no bullets.
why: Form matches message: lessons from nature are laid out as nature is, loosely and unaligned. A calm single-hue column keeps the essay readable while the doodles supply the play.
steal: Replace a bullet list with stickers: draw one doodle per item, set a 13px caption beside it, rotate each 3 to 8 degrees, and scatter them below the intro paragraph.
moves: list items as doodle plus tilted caption

title: List of 50 Trees
name: List of 50 Trees
one_line: Cornell's 1990s field-guide index: 50 trees in numbered columns, each linking to a description page.

look.type: Browser-default Times: common name as a link, Latin binomial in italic parentheses beneath, centred title in navy via font tags.
look.color: White page, default blue links, black text; navy title and maroon intro from old font tags.
look.layout: Numbered list flows through three table columns (1 to 30), then two columns with 'The Maples' and 'The Oaks' subheads; bracketed footer nav.
look.imagery: None on the list; each tree page has a small image linked to a larger one.

behaviour: Static 9 KB HTML: 58 font tags, table layout, no CSS or JavaScript at all. Every entry is a plain link.
signature: Every entry is two lines: the linked common name, then the Latin name in italic parentheses, under one continuous numbering.
why: The structure is the information design: number, common name, scientific name, one link. Nothing is decorated, so a student scans 50 species in seconds; the bracketed footer doubles as breadcrumbs.
steal: Build reference lists as number, linked common name, italic technical name on a second line, flowed into balanced columns with a table; end with bracketed sibling pages.
moves: common name above italic Latin name

title: printedweb.org
name: Printed Web
one_line: The whole site is one 96px Times sentence; each noun phrase is a violet link opening a Google Doc.

look.type: Times New Roman at 6rem (96px) on 6rem line-height, auto-hyphenated, no bold or italic; a Terminal Grotesque font-face is declared but never used.
look.color: White ground, black text, links in electric violet #9900ff; on hover a link fills with a violet block.
look.layout: A single h2 in the top-left with 32px margins; everything below it is empty white.
look.imagery: None.

behaviour: Static, 3 KB: one h2, two CSS files. Links open Google Docs and Wikipedia in new tabs; hover fills each link with violet.
signature: Navigation is the descriptive sentence itself: 'physical archive', 'research', 'teaching', 'experimental publishing' and 'News' are the only links.
why: It collapses nav, about page and hero into one readable sentence. With huge type and a single colour, what to click is obvious and the whole site costs three kilobytes.
steal: Write your site's description as one sentence in 6rem serif; make each noun phrase a link in one saturated hue, invert it on hover, delete the nav bar.
moves: hover fills link with colour block

title: Places
name: Climavore
one_line: A research platform's Places page: Skye, Sicily and other coastlines as cream silhouettes floating on cobalt sea.

look.type: Old-style serif about 20px in cream for the nav and place labels, labels underlined; no headline, type deliberately minor.
look.color: Cobalt blue sea (#2b5fbd) with warm cream land (#ffe5b4) and cream text; two colours only.
look.layout: Silhouettes at different sizes scattered across the screen with tiny underlined labels; fixed top bar: name left, five links right.
look.imagery: Flat vector landmass silhouettes with soft organic edges; no photographs, borders, scale or coordinates.

behaviour: Today a Next.js rebuild with d3, canvas, custom cursor images, animated favicon, dark-mode switch and a festival-news home page; the saved screenshot shows the older Places map.
signature: A map with no map: places are cream blobs on blue, named by tiny underlined serif words, with no scale or grid.
why: Removing geography leaves only shape and name, so each place reads as a character rather than a pin. Two colours suit food and sea, and the empty blue gives every shape room.
steal: Draw places as flat single-colour silhouettes on a one-colour ground, add 14px underlined serif labels beside them, and scatter at different scales instead of aligning to a grid.

title: The Playground Project Architektur für Kinder – architectures for children Spielplätze playgrounds aires de jeux legepladser...
name: The Playground Project
one_line: A research archive on playground history: peach WordPress page, strapline listing 'playground' in a dozen languages.

look.color: Peach ground, near-black text, emerald-green nav and links, grey strapline; black-and-white photography.
look.layout: Twenty Nineteen-style single column: title block, dropdown nav (Künstler, Themen, Städte, Länder, Bücher), 440px bilingual intro, then a full-width photo.
look.imagery: Full-width black-and-white archival photo of children bouncing on an inflatable in a terraced street; 74 images in the archive.

behaviour: WordPress with dropdown taxonomy nav by artist, theme, city, country and book; RSS feed; a small canvas script; thorough keyboard focus styles.
signature: The strapline lists 'playground' in a dozen languages in grey under the German-English title, making the subject international before any text is read.
why: An archive's claim is reach across places; naming one object in many languages states that in one line and adds texture without graphics. The peach ground warms an austere archive.
steal: Under your title, run the key noun in as many languages as you have audiences, lighter grey on the same line, to signal reach without an image.

title: memory metadata
name: memory metadata
one_line: A black cover page for a research essay on photo memory: stepped-pixel title, author name, nothing else.

look.type: Title in a chunky, stepped, notched display face (likely ManuSquared) near 100px, lowercase; author in Forma DJR Micro at about 18px.
look.color: Pure black ground, white type, nothing else on the cover.
look.layout: Centred object: a two-line title with the name beneath, floating in vast black margins.
look.imagery: None; the letters nick and step like low-resolution pixels and stand in for the image.

behaviour: WordPress. The cover is static; below it three numbered chapters (pixels, place, vision) hold 26 images and 5 embeds, with sticky navigation.
signature: The title is set in a stepped, notched bitmap-style face, so the typeface itself is the degraded-photo artefact the essay discusses.
why: The theme, memory degraded by phone cameras and metadata, is stated by letterforms rather than a picture. Black, white and one display face is all a cover needs; the quiet name sets scale.
steal: Give an essay a cover screen: black, one chunky title in a face that visibly embodies the subject, author name in 18px sans, and no navigation until the first scroll.

title: fungal.page
name: fungal.page
one_line: A faithful Wikipedia 'Hypha' article that slowly grows fungal threads through its own text, images and margins.

look.type: Wikipedia's Vector skin (Linux Libertine headings,…'Fungal' font.
look.color: Wikipedia's white, grey and link blue #3366cc untouched; the only additions are violet-blue hyphae lines and black spore circles.
look.layout: Pixel-accurate Wikipedia frame (sidebar, tabs, infobox thumbnails) with a full-page canvas above; hyphae spill out of thumbnails into body text.
look.imagery: Microscopy drawings of Penicillium and Aspergillus; hand-drawn mycelium strokes and circle spores drawn live over the page.

behaviour: CSS keyframes animate the font's THCK and grow axes over 35 to 100 s, staggered per paragraph; masks reveal hyphae images over 15 s; canvas follows the cursor.
signature: A variable font with a 'grow' axis keyframed in CSS: the article's own sentences slowly sprout mycelium while you read.
why: The medium performs the topic. Cloning a familiar template exactly makes the intrusion legible, and the slow timing (35 to 100 seconds) feels biological rather than like an effect.
steal: Clone a boring trusted template exactly, then let one custom variable-font axis and a mask animation slowly corrupt it with your subject; stagger delays by element index.

title: Counterpart
name: Counterpart
one_line: A risograph publishing studio's whole site: one black screen, a circle mark top-left, one sentence at the bottom.

look.color: Pure black with white type; the riso-orange #ff7728 appears only as a 0.3s link hover colour.
look.layout: Fixed bottom-left statement with most of the screen empty above; tiny logo top-left; body overflow hidden, so no scroll.

signature: Everything is pushed to the bottom edge: a 77px sentence, then mono links, under a void of pure black.
why: Restraint signals confidence: the studio says what it is and how to reach it. Bottom anchoring and empty black make the sentence feel like a caption to the void, and the type contrast does the hierarchy.
steal: Fix your one-sentence intro to the bottom-left at about 77px, put contact links under it in 20px mono separated by slashes, and leave the rest of the viewport blank.
moves: large sans over small mono links

title: The Data Healing Recovery Clinic

why: One ink for text and one accent for everything else makes a text-heavy page feel designed. Card, ring and ticker are the only graphics and each repeats the palette.

title: 1969 Tarot
name: 1969 Tarot

signature: A record rendered as a completed form: every attribute is a checkbox, so a deck is described by what is ticked and what is not.
why: Taxonomy is the content. Showing the whole checklist with ticks lets you compare decks by pattern, and the grey system UI honestly signals a database rather than a brochure.
steal: Display each catalogue record as the full checklist of attributes with ticks, hairline groups and default form controls, so absences are as visible as presences.

name: Remote Garden

look.layout: Full-viewport field with absolutely placed pre blocks; the pond is an irregular blue ellipse at centre-right; nickname and creature picker top-right.

behaviour: socket.io real-time: each visitor is a creature with nickname and picker; the native cursor is hidden so you are the creature; the boombox links to a YouTube playlist.
signature: There is no cursor: your pointer is a duck (or bee) moving through a field shared live with other visitors.
why: Replacing the cursor with an avatar makes presence the interface, and ASCII scenery costs nothing. The waiting list in the pond gives visitors a way to leave a trace; the whole page is under 4 KB of HTML.
steal: Hide the cursor, make a creature emoji follow it, broadcast positions over socket.io, let visitors name themselves in one input, and draw scenery in ASCII pre tags.

title: Type Foundry → A Practice for Everyday Life

steal: Show each typeface in one meaningful sentence at about 30px with its name and a 'Buy →' link beneath, and shift every block one column across from the last.

why: Voice does the branding: a person explaining why morning pages matter builds more trust than a feature grid, and the long page filters for people who actually want to write 750 words.

title: Stealing Rocks!

why: Treating snippets as catalogue items gives each a shelf-ready identity: number, type, source, one-line description, preview. The tight table makes comparing and stealing fast, and the joke name sets the tone.
steal: Document each reusable effect as a three-row spec table (type, source, description) beside a live preview tile, and number the entries in reverse so the newest is first.

why: Pairing a high-contrast italic with a plain grotesk at one size lets emphasis happen inside a phrase without bold or colour. Countdown numbers and a '(new)' slot make the collection feel alive.
steal: Set the one verb or label you want stressed in a high-contrast italic serif at the same size as the surrounding grotesk, in parentheses, instead of using bold.

why: Colour is the only decoration, yet it codes the stories and gives the archive the weight of printed volumes; soft white serif titles stay legible on every tile, and the dates signal ongoing work.
steal: Give each archive item one flat background colour from a six-colour palette, a white 38px serif title top-left, a small-caps date bottom-left, and no thumbnails.

mission statement as a tall tile

run-in link list with coloured bullets

title: Glyph Drawing Club

why: It reimagines the pixel editor with type as the brush and exposes every control in plain default UI, because the tool matters more than its chrome. The shortcuts make it fast.
steal: Build a tool's UI from native controls at 10px mono with bold caps section bars, and map ten number keys to ten stored brushes, labelled on screen.

title: Vector Halftone Maker - Interactive PNG/SVG halftone pattern generator

why: Controls follow pipeline order (blur, grid, sampling, shape, colour) with live preview; icons preview each pattern, and the two-tone presets let non-technical users get a good result in one click.
steal: For a generative tool, put the canvas first, group sliders in pipeline order in a collapsible dark panel, and offer a row of one-click colour pair presets.

title: Dot by New Computer
