why: It treats the interface as typography. One text field holds status, controls and catalogue, so nothing sits in a box; the texture makes thumbnails pop, and coordinates as titles tie each painting to a place.
steal: Generate a background of random punctuation in one serif, justified edge to edge, then embed controls inline as inverted words in (((double parens))) instead of boxed buttons.

title: exhibition - Dissolving Earth
name: Dissolving Earths
one_line: An exhibition site in mist-green and grey whose pages are eroded by speckle and spatter textures.

look.type: Light grotesk 14px for the four-tab bar; Garamond-like serif near 26px, centred with tight leading, on event cards; rotated serif titles on images.
look.color: Cool mist palette: sage-grey tab, pale blue-grey photograph, white speckle ground and teal-grey spatter blots; one family of hues.
look.layout: Four tabs across the top; a full-width image carousel with rotated caption bottom-left and arrow bottom-right; below, a notched-corner outline event card.
look.imagery: Point-cloud and mesh scans of landscape with pines, sheets of speckled noise and spatter dots that dissolve section edges.

behaviour: Today the site returns HTTP 401 (login required), so interaction is unknown; the screenshot shows an arrow-driven slider and static event cards.
signature: Speckle and spatter grain over every surface make the page itself look like it is dissolving, as in the exhibition's title.
why: Texture carries the concept: instead of illustrating dissolution, the interface is eroded by noise and blots in one cool palette, and a cut-corner outline card adds the one rigid shape for contrast.
steal: Apply one grain-and-spatter PNG to backgrounds, fade it at section edges, keep one cool palette, and use a single outlined card with a clipped corner as the only hard shape.

title: Triple Canopy: How to Encounter a Puddle - V.1
name: v.1 (RISD)
one_line: A student publication's article page: big grotesk text with a persistent numbered issue contents rail beside it.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk: 24px body, 30px article title, 50px light 'v.1' masthead, italic 18px abstract, 16px author lines.
look.color: White ground, near-black text; one green marks the current issue and article in the contents list.
look.layout: Two columns: a narrow left rail with masthead, blurb and numbered contents; a wide right column for title, abstract, photos and body.
look.imagery: A triptych of three phone photographs of a fluorescent-green puddle with a caption, then long-form text.

behaviour: Cargo site, now returning 404 for this article, so it is dead; the contents list marks your position in green and links through the issue.
signature: A persistent numbered table of contents beside the article, with the current piece in green, makes an issue feel like a book.
why: Magazine navigation shrunk to essentials: issue name, numbered list with author lines, nothing else. Large type needs no zoom, and one colour marks where you are.
steal: Keep the issue's numbered contents in a sticky left rail, set author names smaller under each title, and colour only the current item.
moves: one colour marks the current item

title: Water Jokes — PMVABF I lucky risograph
name: Water Jokes (Lucky Risograph)
one_line: A riso book's shop page staged as floating…'water' ground, with audio players on the pictures.

look.type: Almost no type: a serif title on the book cover and Cargo system-sans grey 'Play' strips at 12px.
look.color: Deep cobalt #1b55a6 ground; every object glows with a pale cyan halo; blue marbled paper, cream pages, one green lawn photo.
look.layout: A centred vertical column of three large objects (cover, open spread, next spread) with small circular and square photos drifting left and right.
look.imagery: Spiral-bound book cover, an open marbled spread, a stone frog spouting water cropped to a circle, a fountain sculpture.

behaviour: Cargo page; play buttons attached to the circular photo and the fountain card start audio; the shop is now password-private ('This site is private').
signature: Every object is lit by the same soft cyan glow, so photographs of paper float as if underwater, with sound buttons riding on the pictures.
why: Colour direction from the book (blue marbling) becomes the whole storefront; a consistent halo unifies photos shot at different times, and audio on images adds a layer print can't offer.
steal: Colour the shop page to match the product's dominant ink, cut out each photo with a soft same-hue glow, and attach small play buttons to pictures for sound.

title: Tiny Factories
name: Tiny Factories
one_line: A paid creators' tribe presented in monospace green on cream, with a full-width ASCII forest, cabin and river.

look.type: DM Mono (Menlo fallback) throughout: 14px body, about 28px centred headline, nav items ending in slashes, slightly open tracking.
look.color: Cream-lime ground with dark forest-green text; Monokai pink, cyan and orange are declared in the CSS but not seen.
look.layout: Centred 470px text column under a slash-ended nav; the ASCII scene runs edge to edge between headline and body.
look.imagery: ASCII art only: pine trees, a smoking cabin, sparkles, a ground line ending in a wavy river.

behaviour: Glitch-hosted jQuery page: animated tab title, clock and date script, glitch effect, crosshair cursor, RSS feed; fixed type sizes.
signature: A full-bleed ASCII landscape of pines, cabin and river under the headline turns 'tribe' and 'treehouse' into a drawn place.
why: The community's metaphor, a private online treehouse,…'s own material (monospace characters), so illustration and typography are one system; one dark green on cream keeps long copy easy to read.
steal: Draw your central metaphor in ASCII across the full page width, in the same monospace and colour as the body copy; no image files needed.

title: Tomorrow Happens
name: Tomorrow Happens
one_line: A Brisbane web studio whose name is a scrolling sentence: 'Tomorrow' fixed, its endings rolling past.

look.type: Reckless Neue serif near 36px for the scroller lines; ABC Diatype 10px nav with hairline rules above each label.
look.color: White ground; the active line in black, every other ending in pale grey #e3e3e3, so only one reads at a time.
look.layout: One centred axis: 'Tomorrow' sits right-aligned left of the centre line, endings left-aligned right of it; tiny menu labels at the far-left edges.
look.imagery: Home is typographic only; the work index of 42 projects holds 84 muted looping videos as thumbnails and case-study media.

behaviour: Astro with GSAP ScrollTrigger and Splitting: 64 lines scroll through the centre, the 'Tomorrow' prefix showing only on the current line; Barba transitions; custom cursor; accordion index.
signature: 'Tomorrow' appears only beside the centre line, so 64 scrolling phrases read as one sentence: Tomorrow brings disappointment, Tomorrow confronts injustice.
why: One typographic device does branding, mission and navigation cue: the name finishes itself differently every moment, mirroring the studio's idea. Grey for all but the active line keeps the screen calm.
steal: Make the site name a sentence stem: fix its first word on a centre line, scroll 40 endings past it, show the stem only beside the active one.
moves: only the active line in black

title: h.p.
name: h.p. (Harsh Patel)
one_line: A designer's studio-archive page: sparse images scattered at different scales on white under a blackletter signature.

look.type: Calligraphic blackletter wordmark 'Harsh Patel'near 36px, top-left; no other visible…'Mailing List / Join' at lower right.
look.color: Pure white ground; a six-segment bar (black, red, pink, violet, cream, yellow) is the only designed colour; images supply the rest.
look.layout: Loose scatter of images in two staggered columns, each at its own size and offset, with generous white; wordmark and colour bar share the header.
look.imagery: Books and a silhouette poster, a pile of posters, twenty tiny sigil logos, a vitrine on a plinth.

behaviour: Today a 403 'Checking your browser...' page blocks it, so behaviour is unknown; the screenshot shows a static-looking image scroll.
signature: A thin six-colour bar beside the blackletter signature is the site's only colour code, above a white field of uncaptioned images.
why: No captions, no grid: the images are the archive and the white is the frame. The sigil grid and colour bar give an identity system without a logo, so the work looks collected rather than showcased.
steal: Skip captions and grids: place images at varied sizes in two staggered columns on pure white, and keep one thin multicolour bar in the header as the only brand mark.

title: Interactive Typography cheatsheet
name: Interactive Typography Cheatsheet
one_line: A giant old-style serif pangram whose anatomy parts glow green; tap one to learn its name.

look.type: Large transitional old-style serif near 170px in four tight lines; Arial 30px title and 14px prompt in the header; 9px credits.
look.color: Charcoal glyphs on whitesmoke #f5f5f5, a dark #333 header band, one lime-green (about #74c044) for the anatomy highlights.
look.layout: Header band, then a full-width four-line SVG specimen sentence; credit line bottom-right; nothing else.
look.imagery: Vector letters split into highlighted parts (serif, bowl, ascender, ear, spur) with a dotted stress-axis line through the o.

behaviour: Click or tap a highlighted part to reveal its name; one small JS file and inline SVG; the original cheatsheet is by Martin Silvertant, code by Christian Heilmann.
signature: Anatomy lives on the specimen itself: parts of real letters are painted green and become the buttons.
why: It teaches by pointing at the thing instead of listing diagrams; a pangram at giant size gives every part a target, one highlight colour marks the interactive zones, and it all fits one screen.
steal: Teach a vocabulary by setting a real sample huge, tinting the teachable parts in one highlight colour, and revealing names on tap, with no separate diagram.

title: BuildList.org
name: BuildList
one_line: A directory of on-demand manufacturers with instant quotes, drawn entirely as a blueprint on electric blue.

look.type: Roboto: 11px bold caps sidebar, 35px bold title, 14px body in pale blue, bold 13px manufacturer names.
look.color: Electric blue #2f52ff ground, white text, pale periwinkle #a8c0ff secondary text, deeper #2a4ae8 panels; no other hue.
look.layout: Fixed left sidebar of processes (3D printing, laser cut, CNC, zine printing, PCB, metal casting); a wide content column; listings grouped by region.
look.imagery: A blueprint-grid panel with a wireframe octahedron and circle; 494 small manufacturer logos in the lists.

behaviour: Static 100 KB page with sticky sidebar, smooth-scroll anchors and an intersection observer for the current section; 186 outbound links.
signature: A cyanotype-style page: one saturated blue, white lines and a tinted second text level, with a graph-paper diagram as the hero.
why: The blueprint look makes the fabrication subject legible at once, and two text tints on one blue build hierarchy without a second colour. The sidebar of processes mirrors how makers search.
steal: Pick one electric blue as the ground; use pure white for primary text and a pale tint of the blue for secondary; draw the hero as a thin-line grid diagram.

title: Supertape
name: Supertape
one_line: A band-website builder's landing page: a full-width 'supertape' wordmark and sticker badges at the margins.

look.type: Lowercase geometric sans wordmark near 240px edge to edge; Poppins about 48px headline, black then grey; 11px mono caps nav.
look.color: Off-white #fafafa ground, black type with a grey continuation, violet nav links; stickers in vermilion, cyan and lime.
look.layout: Wordmark across the top, a huge empty field, then the pitch at the bottom; three round stickers pinned to the viewport margins.
look.imagery: Circular stickers with text on a ring ('Made for bands', 'Sync'd and up-to-date', 'DIY tools'); no screenshots.

behaviour: Astro static page with variable-font and font-feature settings; today it is a shutdown notice (July 2026) pointing to a successor.
signature: A wordmark so large it fills the viewport width, followed by a headline whose second sentence fades to grey.
why: Scale does the branding and the empty field below is confident. A two-tone sentence gives lead-in and supporting clause without any size change, and round stickers add band-merch playfulness.
steal: Fit your lowercase wordmark to the full viewport width, leave a screen of blank space, then set a pitch whose first sentence is black and the rest 55% grey.

title: Constraint Systems
name: Constraint Systems
one_line: A catalogue of 29 experimental image and text tools in a ruled grid, each with a preview and Launch link.

look.type: Times bold 28px for the header and tool names, Arial 14px descriptions, native grey Preview buttons; Departure Mono inside the tools.
look.color: White cells, 1px black rules, black type; all colour comes from tool screenshots (pink Cascade, black Grid, retro-computer Mosaic).
look.layout: Edge-to-edge three-column grid of bordered cells with no gutters; each cell: name, preview, description, then Preview and Launch.
look.imagery: Tool screenshots about 300px wide showing real output: CSS Paint pixel art, text Grid on black, Mosaic of retro computers.

behaviour: React/Vite app on GitHub Pages; each cell offers Preview and Launch; the 'csOS' entry bundles all the tools together in one desktop-like place.
signature: Zero-gutter ruled cells turn a link list into a periodic table of tools: each cell is a name, a thumbnail and two actions.
why: Browser-default typography frames the weirdness, so the tools look like the designed objects. Showing each tool's real output explains it faster than any description.
steal: Show a catalogue as zero-gutter 1px-ruled cells in default Times and Arial, each with name, live screenshot, one-sentence description, Preview and Launch.
moves: a meta-tool that hosts the rest

title: ASH - Ai Pocket Field Guide
name: ASH (F!NH)
one_line: A portfolio case study of a handheld AI field guide for children: wordmark, big photo, grey mono intro.

look.type: Space Mono about 26px light grey for the intro; thin 40px grotesk title 'ASH'; 14px grey mono caps nav; Redaction faces loaded for later sections.
look.color: White ground, black title, grey mono text; one green shared by the hyphen, the on-screen detection box and the device's pill button.
look.layout: Centred 900px column: header row, title, intro, full-width product photograph, then text with generous gaps.
look.imagery: Hands hold a black 3D-printed device over a dandelion in a drain grate; its screen shows a green '#72_Dandelion' box.

behaviour: Webflow-built case-study page with jQuery; sections for projects, thoughts, process and contact; Shopify and Firebase scripts are loaded; reading page is static.
signature: The photograph shows the product in use with its own UI label ('#72_Dandelion'), and the page echoes that label's green in a single hyphen.
why: One honest product photo explains the idea in three seconds (hands, plant, device, detection box). Grey monospace at reading size and one green borrowed from the photo tie text to image.
steal: Lead a case study with one in-context photograph, sample one accent colour from the object, and spend it only on a hyphen, a link or a highlight.
moves: accent colour sampled from the object
grey mono intro at large size

name: Julijonas Urbonas
one_line: An artist-engineer's site where titles and menus are set letter by letter on waves and rings.

look.type: Unica-Gravity grotesk: spaced caps titles with each letter offset along a wave; 11px news text; vertical letter stacks; blue italic for current items.
look.color: White ground, black type, one periwinkle blue (#7b86ff) for the active section and line 1; grey #bcbcbc line numbers.
look.layout: Three panes: news, a projects-and-texts menu, and a wide reading column with a grey line-number gutter running 1 to 22 and on.
look.imagery: Project photographs float inside the text with captions; an SVG ring menu of words on a circle; 237 lazy-loaded images.

behaviour: jQuery site with a flying-letters script that offsets every letter, an SVG ring of filters (videos, projects, texts, talks, tags, keywords, images), and lazy-loaded media.
signature: Words float: every title is set on a gentle wave and menus curl into circles, as if levitating, while body copy stays straight and numbered.
why: The typography enacts the work (levitation, gravity, accelerators) without a single illustration. Limiting the wobble to titles and navigation keeps body text readable; line numbers make the column feel like a document.
steal: Offset each letter of titles and nav a few pixels along a sine wave, set filter options on a circle, and keep body text straight with a quiet line-number gutter.
moves: line-number gutter in the reading column

title: Graphic Design Reading
name: readings.design
one_line: A filterable reading list of critical graphic-design writing as a ruled table with icons for PDF, web and book.

look.type: Work Sans medium near 20px for titles, authors and years in three columns; 14px bold header; 20px base.
look.color: White rows split by 1px grey rules, black text, black header bar; no accent.
look.layout: Full-width list of tall rows (icon, title, author, year); a fixed outlined KEY box bottom-left and CREDITS button bottom-right.
look.imagery: Three tiny icons (website arrow, book, PDF page) are the only graphics.

behaviour: Static list of about 450 outbound links on GitHub Pages with jQuery topic filtering through FILTER (accessibility, architecture, feminism, history and more); the legend is fixed to the viewport.
signature: A fixed outlined KEY box (PDF, website, book) floats at the bottom-left, so the row icons are always decodable.
why: A reading list needs only title, author, year and format. Tall rows give scanning room, and the persistent legend plus one FILTER keep it self-explanatory; the black bar anchors a very plain page.
steal: Make a reading list a ruled table (icon, title, author, year) with a fixed legend box and a single FILTER control tied to topic tags.

title: recoding everyday technology | recoding everyday technology
name: re-coding everyday technology
one_line: A hybrid web-to-print publication on everyday technology, with live visitor chips and a mixed-media contents index.

look.type: Times about 24px for statements and previews; tiny Authentic Sans in default-blue links for titles and format tags; red index numerals.
look.color: Light grey #f0f0f0, black Times, link blue #0000ff, red numbers; green and yellow only in presence chips and hovers.
look.layout: Sticky left column (statement plus blob wordmark) and a ragged right contents grid whose items have different widths, each with number, tag and preview.
look.imagery: Mixed previews: glossary text, an object grid, a pink-and-grey world map, a slot-car track photo, a fax-machine linocut cat.

behaviour: Vue app: scrolling header marquee and real-time presence, where visitors appear as 'Dear [Animal]' chips and a log notes 'left the site'; a black dot tracks the pointer.
signature: Visitors are named in the header like guests ('Dear Steady Salamander') and a log line says when one 'left the site'.
why: Publishing as a live place: the magazine knows who is reading it. Plain Times and default-blue links keep it feeling like a text, while tags show each contribution's format (text, hack, hardware, website).
steal: Show current visitors as small chips with random animal names in the header and log departures; label every contents item with its format in a small blue tag.
moves: format tag above each contents item

title: Internet Artifacts
name: Internet Artifacts
one_line: A museum of old-internet relics: marble entry hall, carved plaque title, and a line-art frieze of meme figures.

look.type: Cinzel-like small-caps serif near 40px on a plaque, tiny tracked caps subtitle 'YOU MAY TOUCH THE ARTIFACTS'; 'ENTER →' in the same serif.
look.color: Warm terracotta-peach marbled plaster, brown line art, cream fills and soft shadows; monochrome sepia.
look.layout: Symmetric temple hall: Ionic columns at both edges, cornice across the top, double-ruled plaque and button centred, crowd frieze along the bottom.
look.imagery: Hand-traced line-art figures (hamster, masked wrestler, wedding couples, dinosaur costume) in cream and brown; stone column photography.

behaviour: Today Cloudflare returns a 403 'Just a moment' check, so only the entry screen is known; the subtitle invites touching the artifacts inside.
signature: Museum signage as UI copy: 'YOU MAY TOUCH THE ARTIFACTS' under a carved plaque title turns old memes into antiquities.
why: One metaphor, a classical museum, is applied to every element: columns, plaque, marble, line-drawn busts. The copy does the joke, so the premise is understood before the first click.
steal: Stage your subject in one physical institution: build the entry from its architecture and signage, write instructions as its house rules, and draw all figures in one line style.
moves: line-art frieze at the bottom edge

title: DANIEL - EMMA
name: Daniel Emma
one_line: An Adelaide design studio's splash: powder-blue screen, two white tags (Store, Studio) and a smiley monogram.

look.type: Bold wide-tracked caps near 18px in cobalt inside white tags; the D_E monogram letters tiny and black.
look.color: Powder blue #dbf2ff ground, white tags with cobalt type, a pink circle with a red smile.
look.layout: Two buttons dead centre; the monogram at bottom centre; nothing else on a one-screen gateway.
look.imagery: Only a 46px pink circle face made from the initials: D and E as eyes, a red smile below.

signature: Initials become a face: 'D_E'as two eyes and a red…'s whole brand mark.
why: A gateway with two doors routes visitors in one click to a shop or a practice; powder blue with cobalt type is friendly rather than corporate, and the face gives personality with one shape.
steal: Open with a gateway screen: two white tags centred on a flat pastel ground, with your monogram redrawn as a small face at bottom centre.

title: Fonts
name: NaN Fonts

look.color: Acid mint-lime ground, near-black type; neon green in the logo block and scribble; four dot switches (white, black, blue, rainbow) in the nav.
look.layout: Fixed top bar (green logo block, caps nav, cart); an intro statement; then a wrapping run-in list of faces under a hairline.
look.imagery: No images; a hand-drawn neon-green marker scribble sits over the intro text, and the type is the illustration.

signature: The catalogue is one wrapping sentence of font names, each in its own typeface with tiny style-and-script metadata beside it.
why: It replaces the specimen grid with a single flowing line where weights and widths contrast at one size, and metadata like '108 styles, ARABIC + CYR + GRK' gives scale. The acid ground says weird.
steal: List your products as inline words, each set in its own typeface at one size, followed by 10px mono metadata, wrapping naturally under a hairline.
moves: each name in its own face

title: Ezekiel Aquino
name: Ezekiel Aquino
one_line: A studio homepage that is a generative score: two staves bent into concentric rings, with Play and Information.

look.type: Basel Grotesk in the corners, alternating with italic Ogg serif lines ('presents', 'Undulations in C'); notation drawn in the Bravura music font.
look.color: Pale grey #f4f4f4 ground and black ink only; a tiny copyright line at the bottom; no colour at all.

look.imagery: Engraved music: treble and bass staves wrapped into circles, beamed notes and hairpins crowding at the 3 o'clock point.

behaviour: Next.js with a canvas rendering Bravura glyphs on a no-scroll page; Play presumably starts the generative piece; blend-difference on fixed labels. Exact audio behaviour unclear.
signature: Sheet music as interface: two staves wrapped into rings, notes bunching and thinning as the piece unfolds, with Play in the corner.
why: The studio's offer, programmatic design, is shown as a finished playable piece instead of a case-study list. The programme-note title block borrows concert conventions: sans for fact, italic serif for poetry.
steal: Make the homepage one piece of work you can play; write the title block like a concert programme alternating grotesk facts and italic serif titles; pin controls to the corners.
moves: music notation font as drawing material

title: Odie
name: Odie
one_line: A tool that turns a published Google Doc into a subdomain webpage, with an ASCII mascot and one short form.

look.type: SF Pro style system sans 13 to 14px; bold 20px form heading, 25px underlined 'Odie' title; ASCII cartoon dog in monospace.
look.color: White, black and one grey border around the form; mint #79ffe1 only as the text-selection colour.
look.layout: Three columns: the ASCII dog, a bordered 'Make a new Odie' form, and explanatory text with Directory and 'Odie of the moment'.
look.imagery: A 30-line ASCII drawing of a standing cartoon dog; no raster images.

signature: The CMS is a Google Doc: edit the doc and the site updates, with a one-field form to claim a.odie.us name.
why: It removes the editor by reusing one nearly everyone already knows; the page explains itself in three sentences and numbered steps, and 'Odie of the moment' makes a showcase out of a directory.
steal: If your tool depends on something people already use, show its three setup steps beside the form in plain text and feature one live example under it.

title: URGENT PEDAGOGIES
name: Urgent Pedagogies
one_line: A pedagogy archive whose red-on-grey homepage turns the mission statement's key phrases into outlined filter pills.

look.type: Open Sauce light caps near 96px for the title, 26px for mission text; 11px mono-like text in index boxes; Noto Nastaliq and TC for scripts.
look.color: One vermilion #ff331a on warm grey paper-grain ground; type, outlines, pills and buttons are all that red.
look.layout: Full-width title, then the mission paragraph; two outlined boxes (Recently published, Explore categories) side by side; a floating red pill bottom-right.
look.imagery: Hovering a link raises a fanned stack of cards (event photo, issue cover, blurred announcements) over the text; otherwise none.

behaviour: WordPress with Masonry; phrases in the paragraph are category pills; hover reveals image cards; hamburger menu; reduced-motion rules; Internet Explorer gets a rejection message.
signature: Key phrases inside the mission statement are wrapped in thin rounded outlines, so the paragraph itself is the category filter.
why: Navigation inside prose keeps the statement readable and makes categories feel like the project's own vocabulary. One red on grey is memorable, and fanned hover cards add richness only on demand.
steal: Wrap the topic phrases of your intro paragraph in 1px rounded outlines that link to filtered views, and use one saturated ink for every element on a paper-grey ground.
moves: single red ink on grey paper

title: soundsports powered by BASE
name: Sound Sports
one_line: A Japanese apparel shop on BASE with a left text menu and a single electric-blue pictogram hero.

look.type: Wide-tracked light sans caps (Muli loaded) at 11 to 13px for the menu in black; bold rounded blue wordmark near 24px.

look.layout: A left rail of category links with plus signs for groups; the right half holds the blue glyph cluster; tiny footer links bottom-left.
look.imagery: Four bone-shaped X figures arranged in a diamond with a solid dot: a flat blue pictogram of bodies or stars.

signature: A flat electric-blue four-X pictogram sits alone in white space, so the brand is a symbol and a link list, not a banner.
why: A templated shop still gets an identity from one symbol and one colour; the plain tracked-caps left menu keeps shopping predictable while white space frames the glyph.
steal: On a templated shop, change three things only: pick one saturated blue, set wordmark and a single pictogram in it, and move the menu to a text-only left rail.

title: Heresies PDF Archive : THE HERETICS
name: Heresies PDF Archive
one_line: A film microsite's archive of the feminist art magazine Heresies: cover thumbnails and PDF downloads on charcoal.

look.imagery: Scans of magazine covers (red Heresies #1, mint Lesbian Art, hot-pink Organized Women Divided) at thumbnail size.

behaviour: WordPress with jQuery; each cover links to a high-resolution PDF download; the film's pages (Trailer, Screenings, Purchase) share the template; RSS feed.
signature: The charcoal ground makes the covers glow like slides on a light table, one per row with title, volume, date and 'Download PDF'.
why: An archive's job is access: cover, issue…'s red masthead frame the mismatched covers.
steal: Give each archive item the same four lines (issue number, bold-italic title, volume and date, a coloured download link) beside a 90px cover, on a dark ground.

title: Whole Earth Index
name: Whole Earth Index
one_line: Near-complete scanned archive of Whole Earth Catalog-era magazines, indexed by their six mastheads.

look.type: TeX-style roman serif with old-style numerals at 17-24px for prose; a small mono for nav and captions; no bold, no heading scale.
look.color: Pure black ground, white type and 1px rules; magazine logos inverted to white; colour likely arrives only with cover scans lower down.

signature: Circled numerals ①-⑥ in each cell corner double as the key to the numbered section headings below.
why: A contents page that is also the first screen: the grid is the navigation, the numerals are the legend, and sparse chrome lets the archive's own mastheads supply all the personality.
steal: Make the homepage a bordered grid of collection logos with one circled numeral each, and reuse those numerals as section headings so the index and the page agree.

title: Meye
name: Meye
one_line: A free library of cut-out tree photographs for architects, filtered by season and Latin genus.

look.type: Rounded geometric sans (Be Vietnam-style) at about 18px; filters are plain running text separated by slashes, selected term in bold.
look.color: Flat light-grey ground (about #eaeaea), near-black text, grey secondary text; neutral so cut-out trees can sit on it.
look.layout: Wordmark left, three nav links right; Season and Species filter columns plus search and Sort-by sit on one row above the results area.
look.imagery: Cut-out tree photos in four seasons; the capture shows only a three-dot loader where they load.

behaviour: JS-fetched grid (the HTML has zero images); filter by season or genus, free-text search, sort menu; three-dot loader while thumbnails arrive; WordPress with Divi modules.
signature: Filters written as a slash-separated sentence of Latin genus names, the active one in bold, instead of dropdowns or chips.
why: A taxonomy shown as plain text is scannable, wraps naturally, costs nothing to build and speaks the users' language (botanical names). Every filter is visible at once, so nothing hides behind a menu.
steal: Replace filter chips and dropdowns with one wrapped line of terms separated by ' / ', bolding the active term; show every option at once.

title: brach und wild | Eine audiovisuelle Tour
name: brach und wild
one_line: Interview transcripts about wasteland set as a page of fading words, with hover GIFs and full-screen video.

look.type: TWK Lausanne Light at 35px/35px, black on white, set with word-break: break-all; a 5x3 dot-matrix variable font at 160px for clusters and symbols.
look.color: Pure black on white with pure-blue links for interview filenames; text selection inverts to white-on-black; colour comes only from the photos.
look.layout: One edge-to-edge 35px text field with 10px margins; words hold their space after fading, so paragraphs read as scattered fragments with thumbnails inline.
look.imagery: 20vw colour stills of the wasteland, inline GIFs that appear on hover, Vimeo clips; a blinking headphone icon.

behaviour: Words fade to opacity 0 over 1.5s, leaving gaps; hovering a passage restores them; dot-glyph clusters pop GIFs on hover; interview links open paired full-screen Vimeo videos.
signature: The transcript is full of invisible words: the gaps in the paragraphs are speech that has already faded, like land left fallow.
why: Typography enacts the subject: the performance is about fallow ground and memory, and the text itself decays and regrows. The mechanism is a few CSS rules, so the concept costs almost nothing.
steal: Wrap each word in an element, fade random ones to opacity 0 with a slow transition, and restore them on hover, so long transcripts read as decaying memory.
moves: words fade out but keep their space
variable dot-matrix font animates on hover
hover pops a GIF over the glyph
full-screen paired video overlay on an 8-column grid

title: annierau
name: annierau
one_line: A Wikipedia-influencer's homepage: pastel pink desktop with a TextEdit window bio and an emoji ticker.

look.type: Bold system sans (-apple-system / Neue Haas Grotesk) for nav and the footer call to action; monospace inside the screenshot window; emoji strip.
look.color: Flat lavender-pink #fae0ff page, periwinkle-to-violet gradient top bar, pale lime strip behind the emoji, black text.
look.layout: Fixed top bar, emoji marquee under it, a Mac text-file window floating left, an oversized link line at the bottom.
look.imagery: A screenshot of a macOS TextEdit window, an empty outlined rectangle, emoji; no photos of the author.

behaviour: Cargo site with a looping emoji marquee and a scroll listener; the lots-of-links page hangs off one oversized line at the bottom.
signature: A real macOS TextEdit window pasted in as the About section, caret and spellcheck squiggles included.
why: The author's voice (cute, self-deprecating, LOL) arrives before any layout cleverness: familiar OS furniture makes a bio feel like a note from a friend. Emoji and pastel do the branding.
steal: Paste a real screenshot of a familiar app window (Notes, TextEdit) as your About text, with spellcheck squiggles and caret left in.
moves: emoji marquee as a decorative band
links page as one giant underlined line

title: handwritten.blog
name: handwritten.blog
one_line: A blog whose index and posts are the author's own handwriting from a reMarkable tablet, links included.

look.type: Real pen handwriting as images: a brush-marker logo at ~100px, neat all-caps for headings and dates, a looser cursive for link titles in blue ink.
look.color: Black ink and one blue ink on pure white; blue marks links exactly as a blue pen would.
look.layout: Centered single column: huge logo with swoosh underline, then a dated index with right-aligned dates and left-aligned titles, signed by the author.
look.imagery: No images beyond the handwriting itself; every glyph is a pen stroke, with wobble and uneven baselines.

behaviour: Handwritten titles are real hyperlinks, blue ink marking them. Today the site is a typeset landing page in Caveat on cream paper, pitching handwritten blogging for others.
signature: Hyperlinks written by hand: the blue-ink title is the link, so the web's oldest convention survives in a pen stroke.
why: Slowing the author down is the product: the form (pen on e-ink tablet) forces short, deliberate posts, and the interface inherits that. Imperfection signals a person, not a feed.
steal: Hand-write your index page on paper or a tablet, export as SVG or PNG, and turn each title into a link coloured like a second pen.

title: Web Browser 🌱 Digital Garden
name: Digital Garden (Hypha)
one_line: A cooperative's public notes site: each note beside a live force-graph of every linked note.

look.type: Work Sans Light at 96px for note titles, small mono for labels and graph nodes, body sans in orange; light weights throughout.
look.color: One hue: burnt-orange text, edges and pills on a pale lime-green ground; white note card, peach link chips.
look.layout: Split screen: left a rounded white note card with metadata, title, text and backlink cards; right a full-height graph of curved edges.
look.imagery: No photos; emoji (seedling, tree, wheat) as nodes, likely marking growth stage, joined by thin orange arcs.

behaviour: d3 force graph of all notes beside the open note; current note ringed in purple; wiki-style link chips; drag, localStorage and RSS present.
signature: The whole garden is always on screen as a graph; the note you read is a purple ring inside it.
why: Showing a note next to its neighbours turns reading into navigation: you see where you are in the whole, and one hue keeps text, graph and chips reading as one object.
steal: Pair every note page with a persistent graph of its neighbours, highlight the current node with a ring, and colour everything in a single hue on a tinted ground.
moves: single-hue palette on a tinted ground

title: LOW←TECH MAGAZINE
name: LOW-TECH MAGAZINE (solar)
one_line: Solar-powered, dithered-image magazine site that publishes its own battery state and goes offline at night.

look.type: Browser-default Times New Roman: 40px masthead with a left-arrow glyph, 20px lede, 16px body in a narrow column; no web fonts.
look.color: Cream #fff5d1 ground, black text; section links coloured blue (#162dab), red (#d11305) and green (#006951); photos dithered to two olive-cream tones.
look.layout: Masthead and tagline over a full-width rule, a colour-coded nav line, a full-width hero image, then a narrow text column beside a page-size note.
look.imagery: Coarse two-tone dithered photos that weigh a fraction of normal JPEGs; one solar-server photo as the hero.

behaviour: Static pages from a static-site generator; a sun icon and battery notice reflect the solar server's state; page size printed on the page; twelve-language switch; RSS.
signature: The page prints its own weight (Page size: 542.17KB) and admits the site sometimes goes offline because the sun is down.
why: Every constraint is the content: no fonts, dithered images and a visible page weight make the argument for low energy use by being it, and the austerity gives the site a recognisable look.
steal: Set a byte budget and print the page weight on the page; use system serif, dither photos to two tones, and colour-code nav links by section.
moves: printed page weight as a badge

title: Idea of Shop
name: Idea of Shop
one_line: A shop selling objects of the mind: every product is a one-line imagined scene in a bordered cell.

look.type: System sans (SF/Inter-like), all lowercase: 80px title, 26px centred product lines, one weight throughout.
look.color: White page, 1px light-grey cell borders, black text; the only colour is a tiny red dot in some cells' bottom-right corner.
look.layout: Three equal square cells per row filling the width, text vertically centred in each; a small outlined connect button top right.
look.imagery: None: each product is only its sentence, like leaf on a windshield or air trapped in a soap bubble.

behaviour: Unclear in detail; the connect button suggests wallet-gated purchase of the ideas, and the red dots probably mark owned items. The domain no longer resolves.
signature: Every product is a single sentence describing a tiny fleeting scene, sold as if it were an object.
why: The storefront template (grid of cells) is real, the goods are not, and the gap is the joke and the poem. Plain type lets the sentences carry all the imagery.
steal: Borrow a commercial layout (product grid, connect button) and fill it with poems or sentences instead of photos; keep type plain so the words do the imagery.
moves: red dot as the only status mark
lowercase title bigger than anything else

title: Home
name: The Portal (Cori Olinghouse)
one_line: An artist-archivist's entry page: one flat ellipse portal on deep indigo, one underlined word to enter.

look.type: Standard Book grotesk at 16px in off-white for the welcome line and Enter; a 32px size exists; nothing else is set.
look.color: Deep indigo #240092 full-bleed ground, cream #f7f6f1 ellipse and text, cobalt hairline asterisks (#2c3ddb); two hues plus cream.
look.layout: Single screen: welcome sentence pinned top-left, ellipse dead centre with Enter underneath, everything else empty.
look.imagery: A flat cream ellipse like a pool seen at a low angle; a thin blue asterisk hovers above it, reflected.

behaviour: Gatsby site; the browser tab title animates and the asterisk likely spins; Enter opens the expanding index of work.
signature: The portal is literally a flat cream ellipse: a doorway reduced to one shape, and the only button is the word Enter.
why: A threshold page frames the archive as somewhere you go. One saturated field, one shape and almost no text build anticipation at nearly zero cost.
steal: Open an archive or portfolio with a one-shape threshold page: a saturated field, one geometric object, one sentence, one underlined Enter.
moves: underlined Enter as the only control

title: Medialab
name: Medialab (Times Museum)
one_line: A museum media lab's site where seven translucent, perspective-tilted colour planes stack as the menu.

look.type: Tiny UI text (about 16px) in a plain grotesk inside thin-outlined rounded bars; Rand, Rand Mono and Nib are declared; sizes run to 300px.
look.color: White page with seven vertical-gradient planes: periwinkle, orange, mauve, green, near-black, pale yellow, pink, each speckled with confetti flecks.
look.layout: Top bar (stack icon, title, language toggle) and bottom About bar frame a centred stack of full-width trapezoids receding in perspective.
look.imagery: No photos: CSS gradients and speckle textures drawn as tilted translucent sheets, like layers of coloured acetate or paper.

behaviour: Planes likely react to scroll or drag (swiper, mousemove, CSS perspective); Chinese/English toggle; custom cursor images.
signature: The menu is a stack of coloured acetate sheets seen at an angle: choosing a section means picking a layer.
why: A lab about media makes its navigation a physical metaphor (layers) using only CSS 3D and gradients, so the site feels like an object while loading fast.
steal: Make the menu a stack of full-width, semi-transparent gradient planes tilted with CSS perspective; give each section its own hue and a light speckle texture.

title: Times Museum Journal Issue #2
name: Times Museum Journal #2
one_line: A museum journal issue read in one blue ink: outlined boxes for contents, search and share over blue-grey paper.

look.type: Large grotesk body at about 22px with generous leading in blue; contents list in 16px; caps issue title; a fine serif for author names.
look.color: Single ink: royal blue text and 1px outlines on pale blue-grey paper; no second hue anywhere.
look.layout: Wide text column centred with a floating outlined contents panel at top-left; menu and search as stacked square buttons top right; Share box bottom right.
look.imagery: None in view; every UI element is a thin blue rectangle, so chrome looks like drawn lines, not buttons.

behaviour: Vue single-page app, so the live page shows an empty shell; the contents panel opens over the article; a chevron collapses it; menu, search and share are fixed outlined squares.
signature: Everything, including the table of contents, is drawn in the same blue hairline: the interface shares the text's ink.
why: One ink for text and chrome makes the page feel printed (a two-colour job), and outlined boxes read as editorial furniture rather than app buttons, which suits a journal.
steal: Pick one ink colour for all text, rules and controls; draw buttons as 1px outlined squares and put the contents list in a floating outlined panel.
moves: single blue ink for type and chrome
numbered contents list with article titles

title: Cool Symbols ✰ ✍ ❀ ✈ (Copy & Paste 7K+ Symbols and Emojis) - Glyphy
name: Glyphy Cool Symbols
one_line: Copy-and-paste library of 7,000+ symbols and emoji, each in its own tile, with a text input on top.

look.type: Heavy grotesk title at 48px; a typewriter-like mono for nav and body; symbols at 24px in tiles.
look.color: Acid yellow-green header (about #eef760), white rounded input and tiles with soft shadows on white, black glyphs; one loud field, otherwise neutral.
look.layout: Header band, then sections (Arrows, Stars, Hearts...) each a 16-column grid of equal square tiles; 22,000 divs in all.
look.imagery: The symbols are the imagery: black Unicode glyphs in white tiles, plus a title row of five sample glyphs.

behaviour: Click a tile to copy the glyph; text box above; Next.js page with 22,000 elements and 1.9MB of HTML; English/Spanish toggle.
signature: Every glyph gets a finger-sized tile: the catalogue itself is the interface, so choosing is just looking.
why: A utility that shows the goods immediately in a dense uniform grid beats search forms; the single acid-yellow band gives the brand memorability while the rest stays neutral so glyphs read.
steal: For a copy-paste utility, put the catalogue in a uniform grid of hit-sized tiles under one loud colour band, and make a click do the copy.
moves: mono nav against heavy grotesk title
sample glyphs in the title row

title: Alexei Shulgin, Form Art, 1997
name: Form Art (Alexei Shulgin, 1997)
one_line: Alexei Shulgin's 1997 Form Art: the word FORM built from default HTML buttons, plus who-what-where fields.

look.type: No type styling: the browser's default control font (Arial-like 13px) on every button and input; letters are formed by button shapes, not glyphs.
look.color: Pure white page; the only colour is the grey bevelled gradient of default buttons, giving a pixel-font in greys.
look.layout: FORM in a 5-row button matrix at centre; credit fields scattered at hand-placed positions near the edges; a FORM ART COMPETITION button on top centre.
look.imagery: No images: 43 input elements across 11 forms and 6 tables are the entire artwork.

behaviour: Pure HTML page with no CSS; the credit rows read like a database record (who, what, where, browser: Netscape 3.0); static.
signature: Interface elements used as raw material: the form's own buttons spell the word FORM, so the medium is its own subject.
why: Form Art turns native controls into aesthetic material; with zero CSS it proves an idea needs no styling layer, and plain HTML has kept it alive for decades.
steal: Spell a word or draw a picture using only native inputs and buttons of varying widths, arranged in a table, with no CSS beyond what you need to place them.
moves: letters made of native buttons of different widths
browser name as part of the credit

title: Concrete poetry interactions
name: Designing Writing
one_line: A bibliography-in-progress about writing and design, opening as a bold type poster with a looping verb list.

look.type: One bold Helvetica-style grotesk at about 48px, left column ragged-right and right column right-aligned, asterisks as bullets; no other size.
look.color: Black type on white, plus a greyscale fern photograph; no colour at all.
look.layout: Two columns edge to edge: descriptive blurbs left, a tall right-aligned stack of gerunds right; photo starts below the blurbs.
look.imagery: One high-contrast black-and-white photograph of fern fronds, cropped as a hard rectangle.

behaviour: The right-hand verb list repeats (Echoing, Gardening, Thinking... then Echoing again), so it probably loops as a marquee; the live page timed out.
signature: A list of gerunds (Echoing, Gardening, Collecting, Rerouting, Anting...) that restarts itself: research as a verb loop.
why: Describing a project as verbs makes it feel alive, and one weight at one poster size means hierarchy comes from position alone.
steal: Introduce a project with two columns of one-size bold type: what it is on the left, a right-aligned list of verbs that loops on the right.
moves: one size, one weight at poster scale

title: Infinite Artwork
name: Infinite Artwork
one_line: A Twine-built generator that writes a fresh fake artwork title, medium and artist statement on every refresh.

look.type: Inconsolata monospace at about 20px with generous leading in a 590px column; titles in italic; two bold coloured links.
look.color: Black on white; refresh and about links in bold violet and blue; the CSS also defines peach and aqua animations.
look.layout: One narrow left-offset column with a 200px margin, links stacked under the statement, nothing else.
look.imagery: None: the artwork is the generated sentence.

behaviour: Twine/Harlowe story: arrays of phrases (visceral, disorienting, virtual reality...) are combined at random into title, materials and statement; refresh re-rolls.
signature: Artist-statement language (subject-object hierarchy, big data, reenactment) recombined at random until it reads as both parody and plausible art.
why: A bare text template makes the critique: the art-world register is formulaic enough for a few arrays to imitate it. The layout stays minimal so the sentence is the artwork.
steal: Write a generator for a genre's boilerplate (artist statements, press releases): arrays of phrases, random joins, one refresh link, monospace, nothing else on the page.
moves: refresh link as the only control
mono column as gallery wall label
Twine used as a generator engine

title: poetics/politics of computation
name: poetics/politics of computation
one_line: Lecture slides from a School for Poetic Computation talk, published as a dark web slide deck.

look.type: Source Sans Pro semibold caps at about 44px for the title; light sans for author lines; everything centred.
look.color: Charcoal #222 ground, white title, sky-blue (#42affa) author and institution lines; a one-accent dark theme.
look.layout: Centred title slide: two-line caps title, then three centred credit lines, empty space above and below.
look.imagery: None on the title slide; the other five sections are not visible in the capture.

behaviour: Six full-screen slides in a reveal.js-style deck with 3D transitions and keyboard navigation; canvas and mousemove code present.
signature: A lecture published as a link: the slides are the page, with title, speaker and school set as a title card.
why: Putting teaching material on the open web as slides keeps it linkable and forkable; dark ground and one accent stay legible on any projector.
steal: Publish a talk as an HTML slide deck on GitHub Pages so the URL is the handout; dark ground, one accent colour for names.

title: Ben DuVall
name: Ben DuVall: The Anti-Archive
one_line: A site that erases its own content daily; its rules page sets seven numbered laws in huge default Times.

look.type: Times New Roman at about 45px for rules, tiny blackletter-style pixel type for header and subtitle, mono numerals between items.
look.color: Black on white with periwinkle links and five tiny blue square icons; a 1px rule under the header.
look.layout: Header strip (logo mark, two tiny text blocks, last-updated stamp), then a centred numbered list: numeral above, rule text left-aligned below, wide margins.
look.imagery: A round black peace-sign-like mark at top left; no other images.

behaviour: Content is meant to be erased daily and archived offline; a Last updated stamp shows when; today the URL returns a 404 titled This Page Does Not Exist.
signature: The site's own rules (seven laws of…'s 404 is the project working as designed.
why: The concept is enforced by the medium: a website that deletes itself makes link rot the artwork. Default type keeps attention on the rules; the tiny pixel type gives a custodian's voice.
steal: Publish a manifesto as a numbered list in huge default serif with tiny labels, add a last-updated stamp, and let the rules govern the site itself.
moves: huge default serif for manifesto items
tiny pixel type as the custodian's voice

title: Welcome
name: PageMasters
one_line: A London risograph print studio's 2020 placeholder: a fluorescent mirrored riso pattern around one tarot-style print.

look.type: Hand-drawn blackletter logo at 80px; tiny bold wide-tracked serif (Wolpe Pegasus) for the address; hand-lettered TEMP WEB SITE stamps.
look.color: Fluorescent yellow and hot pink with orange and white, plus the print's sky-blue, black and mustard; ground is a mirrored two-ink pattern.
look.layout: Bilaterally symmetric: centred print card, mirrored pattern wings and mirrored TEMP WEB SITE stamps either side, logo above, address below.
look.imagery: A multi-colour risograph illustration (robed figure, black cat, paper stack, sun) with halftone dots, on a mirrored scan texture.

behaviour: The capture shows a static splash; today the site is a shop with skippable intro, swiper galleries, a cursor-following element, blend-mode overlays and a bag.
signature: A placeholder page treated as a print job: TEMP WEB SITE is stamped twice like a rubber stamp onto a mirrored riso pattern.
why: A temporary page still shows what the studio makes: the printed object is the hero, in the studio's own medium, and mirrored fluorescent ink holds the eye.
steal: For a placeholder, put one real product image on a mirrored full-bleed pattern from your own materials, add a hand-drawn stamp, and list only the address and email.

title: Oliver Wise - @owise1
name: Oliver Wise (owise1)
one_line: A creative's project list as a monospace bullet list with lime highlighter marks, topped by a cartoon avatar.

look.type: Menlo/Courier-style monospace at 12px with generous line height; project names in bold on highlighter, descriptions regular; asterisk bullets.
look.color: Off-white paper with faint speckle (#fcfcfc), dark grey text, lime highlighter (#e5f6bc) behind titles, grey underlined links.
look.layout: Centred 380px text column under a small avatar, one entry per project (title, one-line description), wide empty margins.
look.imagery: One flat cartoon portrait of a bearded man with swept hair; no project screenshots.

behaviour: Tumblr-hosted static list of 90+ outbound links; each project gets a title and one sentence; tagline: We're creative. We'll think of something.
signature: Project titles wear a lime highlighter stripe, as if the author had marked their own list.
why: Mono text and one highlighter colour make 90 links scannable: the highlight is the only emphasis, so the eye jumps title to title. Descriptions stay one plain sentence each.
steal: List projects as highlighted title plus one plain sentence in monospace; use a single highlighter colour on titles instead of bold, headings or cards.

title: Superior Type
name: Superior Type
one_line: A type foundry homepage of oversized specimen panels, with one cobalt or yellow accent marking alternate glyphs.

look.type: Raptor Text neo-grotesk at about 110px in the hero panel and Raptor Mono below; site chrome is tiny 12px grotesk in a white bar.
look.color: Pale grey (#e4e4e0) panel with ink-black type and a single cobalt accent; a charcoal (#202020) panel with cream type and a yellow accent.
look.layout: Full-width white nav bar, then stacked panels split by a vertical rule: label column left (Aaa), big specimen right, caption row under a hairline.
look.imagery: The typeface is the image; four muted looping videos animate other specimen panels.

behaviour: SvelteKit shop; specimen text uses real-world strings (cities, brands); four autoplay muted video loops; cart and trials in the top bar.
signature: Alternate glyphs (a, L, G, r) are picked out in one accent colour inside real city names: Atlanta, London, Geneva, Berlin.
why: Colouring only the distinctive letters teaches what makes the font different without a feature list, and city and brand names give the specimen a believable context.
steal: Set specimen words in real names (cities, brands) and colour only the characters that are distinctive in your typeface, one accent per panel, under a hairline and vertical rule.
moves: accent colour on distinctive glyphs only
real city and brand names as specimen
tiny chrome so type is the show

title: Tüpokompanii
name: Tupokompanii
one_line: An Estonian type foundry whose homepage is one huge typewriter-face statement followed by its retail families.

look.type: Kourier, a Courier-like typewriter face, at about 64px centred for the statement and 12px in the nav; the logo is a heavy grotesk wordmark.
look.color: Black on white with no decoration; hover or accent colours in the CSS are pale green #e9ffce, lime #8fff00 and blue #0000ff.
look.layout: Thin nav row, then a centred wide statement block with generous white space, then a heading and list of retail families.
look.imagery: None above the fold; 36 images below show the typefaces in use.

behaviour: Next.js; the tab title animates; families are listed (Vee, Juunior, Vitamiin, Ladna, Trafarett) with on-demand and stories sections.
signature: Introducing a type studio in a Courier-like face at poster size: the most default-looking font becomes a confident statement.
why: Withholding the showpiece typefaces above the fold makes the first screen about voice: one sentence, centred, readable, with space around it. The foundry's skill shows in spacing and restraint.
steal: Open with one 60px+ centred sentence in a plain monospace or typewriter face and a tiny nav; put the product list below it.
moves: giant centred statement in a typewriter face
product list withheld below the fold
heavy wordmark against light typewriter text

title: YS
name: Yehwan Song
one_line: A designer's portfolio drawn as an Euler diagram: project dots sit inside overlapping category ellipses.

look.type: Nimbus Sans (Helvetica clone) at 12-21px: tiny three-column header ticker on white; white set labels, some rotated 90 degrees, on the dark field.
look.color: Near-black #141414 field with 1px white ellipse outlines and hollow white dots; a white strip header; one red (#ff5454) accent in the CSS.
look.layout: White three-column intro strip on top, then a full-width dark diagram of overlapping ellipses with about 70 dots, then three video thumbnails below.
look.imagery: Hollow circles for projects; below, screen recordings of sites on a laptop, a tilted 3D screen and a hand-held phone.

behaviour: Data comes from a Google spreadsheet, as the page says; a white arrow disc sits on the diagram, probably the cursor; dots likely open previews.
signature: A Venn diagram as the site index: a project's position tells you every category it belongs to, and overlaps are the interesting work.
why: Real portfolios straddle disciplines and lists hide that; a set diagram shows it in one glance and gives each category a territory. Hairline outlines on a dark field keep 70 dots legible.
steal: Replace the filter tabs of your portfolio with overlapping labelled ellipses; place each project as a hollow dot where its categories intersect, and drive it from a spreadsheet.
moves: projects as hollow dots at set intersections

title: Theo de Meyer
name: Theo de Meyer
one_line: An architect's index where numbered blue slots sit in a loose grid and a fixed bottom list picks the project.

look.type: Helvetica in pure web blue at 14-18px, one size throughout; the active index entry becomes a white-on-blue block.
look.color: Pure web blue (the CSS keyword blue) on white; red marks a second category of work; hover inverts to white-on-blue.
look.layout: A sparse grid of image slots shows only blue project numbers; a fixed bottom index in four columns lists 00-21 titles over a fade.
look.imagery: Flat blue vector drawings of furniture and pavilions (one visible: an arched arcade with a ladder), one image per slot.

behaviour: WordPress with jQuery: the home grid holds every project's images as numbered slots; the bottom index probably reveals them; the tab title jokes And yet another WordPress site.
signature: Images are represented by the project's number until summoned: the home page is a constellation of numerals the viewer can fill in.
why: One colour and one size make numbers and titles equal citizens, so the index is the design; hiding images behind numerals rewards curiosity. The inverted hover is the whole interaction vocabulary.
steal: Use one pure colour on white, one font size, and inverted white-on-colour blocks for hover and current state; show project numbers first and let hover or selection reveal images.
moves: project numbers as placeholders for images
pure web blue as the only ink
inverted block for hover and current state

title: Standards
name: Standards
one_line: Pre-launch teaser for a brand-guidelines platform: a wordmark, one sentence and counting hairlines on grey.

look.type: Soehne grotesk: bold lowercase wordmark with an orange full stop, 22px regular sentence, tiny 10px numerals; all lowercase.
look.color: Light grey #f2f2f2 ground, black type and rules, one signal orange-red (#ff2e00) on the full stops and the arrow.
look.layout: Left column wordmark and tagline, right half a set of 1px vertical lines hanging from the top at irregular spacing with tiny numerals under them.
look.imagery: None: only hairline rules and numerals suggest a grid or ruler.

behaviour: The lines and numbers (0, 2, 12, 1, 0) look like a counter or ruler, purpose unclear; today it is a full marketing site with looping videos and pricing.
signature: Wordmark and tagline end in the same orange full stop, and the arrow matches: punctuation as the brand mark.
why: A product that sells consistency demonstrates it: one grotesk, one grey, one orange and a visible grid of rules. Restraint on a teaser signals the product's discipline.
steal: Make the brand mark a single punctuation mark: end the wordmark and tagline with one coloured full stop and reuse it in arrows and bullets.

steal: Give each product page its own pair of CSS colour variables and use the product itself, scaled huge and translucent, as the page backdrop; keep paragraphs clear of it.

title: The stories Behind a Line

why: Removing the map removes spectacle, so viewers compare lengths and bends; initials protect identity while the line carries the story, and grey keeps the tone sober.
steal: When data is sensitive, draw each record as one grey hairline with start and end dots and a three-line caption; drop the base map so comparison is by shape.

title: Tracks as Envelopes

signature: Forty-four identical stars stand in for forty-four letters: an audio archive drawn as a hand-set constellation whose colour steps through four bands.
why: Counting is the design: one mark per item makes the archive's size felt at a glance, and colour bands add sequence without labels. Jitter keeps it human.

title: FOUND COLOR schemes for web and UI

signature: The outlined title takes its stroke colours from the photos beside it: the logo is itself a found colour scheme.
why: A site about colour should impose none: a neutral grey ground and a hairline title let the photographs' palettes speak, and a gradient stroke ties the identity to the content.
steal: On a neutral grey ground, set the site title as a giant stroke-only word tilted 30 degrees with a gradient stroke sampled from your imagery.

title: Coin Chart

signature: Time as an angle and country as a radius: 102 coins become a dial you read like a clock, with a readout in the corner.
why: A polar layout suits round objects, fills the screen without scrolling, and keeps two variables legible with only dashes, hollow dots and mono caps; the corner readout turns hover into a museum label.
steal: When data is cyclical or round, plot it polar: one ring per category, angle for time, hollow dots for items, and a four-line readout in a corner for hover.
moves: polar chart: ring = country, angle = year

last-updated and city stamp in the corner

why: A single border-radius and one orange make a playful, varied pattern from plain text; the topics are the content, and the hover GIF rewards curiosity with no cost at rest.

behaviour: Two default buttons (yes, no); a highlighted location presumably updated by hand (Today I am in Amsterdam); the site hosts whatever gets made; the domain no longer resolves.
signature: The page is a proposal written as an FAQ: low-stakes rules (one hour, just HTML and CSS, same room) make saying yes easy.
why: The site is the invitation and the venue: it hosts what the meetings make. Plain default type keeps the focus on the offer, and yes/no buttons make joining a two-option decision.
steal: Write a collaboration proposal as a short FAQ in default HTML, with yes and no buttons at the top and a hand-updated location line.

title: Raw Materials | An Unusual Design Company

why: Assigning each section a hue and number makes a long, flashy scroll navigable; rounded cards add tactility, and the oversized black grotesk holds contrast on every colour.
steal: Give each section a number and a hue, show them as stacked rounded tabs in a fixed left rail, and flood the active panel with the matching colour.
moves: perspective-grid tunnel as a section image
rounded panels stacked down the page

title: wilding.radio
name: wilding.radio

why: One control with a clear metaphor (mix two sounds) makes the visitor an active listener, and a full-bleed photograph of the place supplies atmosphere; the hairline UI never competes.
steal: For a sound piece, use one full-bleed photograph and a single 1px vertical slider with percentage readouts that crossfades two sources; explain it in one three-line caption.

why: A single hand-drawn motif in one colour carries a whole identity: cheap, memorable, and fitting for small handmade things. Scale variation gives depth without a second colour.
steal: Draw one simple motif (a flower, a leaf), fill it in one colour, and scale it along a curve from tiny to huge to build a header from one shape.
moves: one motif repeated and scaled along a curve
tiny is the theme: tiny trophy, tiny prize, tiny page

why: One CSS property (blur) plus randomised classes reproduces the colour-field look; slow linear transitions make it feel painted and meditative.
steal: Fake a painter's soft edges with filter blur on plain divs, randomise their colour and size classes, and let transitions run for seconds.
moves: random colour, size and spacing classes

title: HOLO
name: HOLO
one_line: Art, science and technology magazine whose homepage is a four-column stream of news cards, quotes and covers.

look.type: Courier Prime ~12px for dates, blurbs and source links; plain sans ~18px for pull quotes and titles; tiny HOLO wordmark.
look.color: Near-white ground, black type, light-grey image boxes; only book covers and thumbnails add colour.
look.layout: Four-column card grid with wide gutters: date line, quote or title, mono blurb, source link, image; final tile counts the archive.
look.imagery: Book covers, GIF stills and a black wireframe isometric cube drawing.

behaviour: WordPress with a Shopify shop; contrast-toggle icon, plus and menu icons, Become a Reader button; canvas, clock and drag scripts are present.
signature: A news stream where each card pairs a big sans pull quote with a small typewriter blurb and a chain-link source.
why: A typewriter face for metadata under a plain sans for voice makes a dense aggregator feel edited, and the counter tile (1,888 items) invites further browsing.
steal: Set metadata and blurbs in a mono face and quotes in a plain sans; end the grid with a tinted tile that counts the archive.

title: Schauspielhaus Zürich
name: Schauspielhaus Zurich 2021/22
one_line: Theatre season microsite drawn entirely in black contour lines: wobbly outlined numerals, a bird, a satellite, a map.

look.type: Book-style serif ~15px overlapped by drawings; giant hand-cut outline numerals '2021/22' ~170px; tiny En and close X.
look.color: Black 2px outlines on pure white; no fills at all, so the page is a line drawing.
look.layout: Full-bleed white canvas with drawings of different scale overlapping text blocks and each other; centred welcome note.
look.imagery: Monoline illustrations: torn-edge numerals, a dove with sunburst, a satellite on a line, a country outline, spiral notebook frames.

behaviour: Probably a scroll-driven season preview with an order-the-brochure notebook; the URL returns 404 now so mechanism is unclear.
signature: Season numerals drawn as wobbly cut-paper outlines with a satellite tethered to the slash.
why: Zero fill and one line weight let drawings overlap text without hiding it; the wobble reads as hand-cut and warm, giving a formal institution a playful voice.
steal: Commit to outline-only illustration at one stroke weight so drawings can overlap text and each other without losing legibility.

title: RADICALS RADICANTS EPIPHYTES PARASITES
name: Radicals Radicants Epiphytes Parasites
one_line: Essays, notes and news on gardens, laid out as coloured bands of bevelled, brick-like link tiles.

look.color: Traffic-light bands of green, teal-grey, yellow and red, each item a lighter bevelled tile on its band.
look.layout: Full-width horizontal bands stacked down the page; items are variable-width tiles wrapping in rows like a brick wall.
look.imagery: None; chunky outset bevel borders make the bricks and paving.

behaviour: Probably plain links; the domain now forwards to an unrelated '..Loading..' tracking page, so the original mechanism is unclear.
signature: Chunky outset bevels in flat earthy colours turn link lists into a wall of garden bricks.
why: The old-web bevel border is used as a material, not as irony: bricks match the garden theme, and band colour sorts content types at a glance.
steal: Reuse a browser-native border style (outset bevel) in flat tinted colours as a tile material, one colour per content type.
moves: one colour band per content type

title: On Publishing: Graphic Designers Who Publish
name: On Publishing
one_line: Interviews with graphic designers who publish, shown as a book spread with a per-visit edition number and collation time.

look.type: Red monospace slab caps ~48px, letterspaced, for the title; Atlas Grotesk body; tiny red colophon at the foot.
look.color: White spread with a deep grey gutter shadow; all type in one pure red.
look.layout: Open-book spread: blank left page, title on the right page, gutter shadow down the middle, Make Book link top right.
look.imagery: None on the cover; interviews carry 46 photographs; menu items are marked with unusual Unicode symbols.

behaviour: Cargo with Lenis smooth scroll; clock-driven colophon 'Edition 1280, Collated October 26, 2022 at 9:31'; Make Book link (likely a printable edition, unclear); 26,000 words of interviews.
signature: A colophon reading 'Edition 1280, Collated October 26, 2022 at 9:31', stamped from the visitor's clock.
why: The web page stays faithful to a printed book: spread, gutter, edition number. Each visit becomes its own printing, which dignifies reading online.
steal: Make the page a spread with a gutter shadow and a generated colophon line: edition number plus the current date and time.

title: Be With
name: Be With
one_line: Spiritual-exploration shop and newsletter: a sticker-bomb of a dancing-Shiva photocopy, stars, labels and heavy blue caps.

look.color: White ground, black ink, one process-cyan #00a3e8 for the logotype; a black ellipse holds the signup.
look.layout: One-screen collage: statue at bottom-left overlapping giant letters, tilted stickers, dashed line, ticker strip at the foot.

signature: A photocopied dancing deity stepping on the letters of BE WITH, wired to sticker labels by a dashed line.
why: Zine tactics (outlined stickers, dashed pointers, one spot colour) give a commerce site the warmth of a handmade flyer while the ticker states the mission.
steal: Use one spot colour for the logotype, photocopy a single figure, and attach tilted outlined label stickers with a dashed line.

title: Forever Magazine

signature: A gilded gate hovering in the clouds as the entire front door.
why: One cliche object, small in a huge field, is a joke and a threshold at once; image-buttons keep the nav part of the collage.
steal: Use a single cut-out cliche object centred on a full-bleed stock photo as the front door, and make nav items PNG stickers.
moves: single cut-out object on stock sky
praying-hands emoji as the only text

look.imagery: Scanned aeronautical chart of the Los Angeles basin with thick grey route arrows; yin-yang style and crosshair markers.

behaviour: 217 images and 60 iframes behind markers; jQuery with drag, mousemove, keydown; crosshair cursors; an audio element. Text describes an expedition guided by an artificial search dog.
signature: A real aeronautical chart turned into the menu, with sites marked by black-and-white dots.
why: Navigation as geography: following the wires is literally the interface, and greyscale leaves the dots and films as the only focal points.
steal: Use a desaturated real map as the whole interface and mark each story with a simple black-and-white dot instead of a menu.
moves: greyscale chart with translucent beam overlays

title: Frontpage — Baltic Circle

signature: Giant dark-teal ink blobs with lime centres hovering over ordinary news cards like mirrors.
why: A systematic identity motif laid over a standard template gives the festival a memorable face while content stays in a usable, conventional grid.
steal: Keep the content grid conventional and layer one oversized hand-drawn frame motif over it, partly covering the text.

title: Tjorven Stein

signature: Project names debossed into a cairn of soft grey pebbles under a glowing sun.
why: One physical metaphor drawn with CSS shadows alone makes a list of links tactile and calm; the debossed small caps echo carved stone.
steal: Draw nav items as stacked soft-shadow pebbles with inset highlights and debossed small caps, and size them in vw.
moves: debossed small caps via inset text-shadow
sun glow as the hover colour

title: longstoryshort.glitch.me

signature: Paintings arranged around the screen as clock numerals, tilted so some hang upside down.
why: One layout formula (rotate, translate) arranges everything; the tilt makes each painting an object in a ring until you choose one.
steal: Place a dozen thumbnails on a viewport-sized circle with rotate-then-translate in vmin units, and let a click straighten and enlarge one.

title: Marketplace

title: ♡ cinni’s dream home ♡

why: Total commitment to one pixel language, down to cursors, buttons and counters, makes the site a place; the me/you nav split makes a huge link collection navigable.
steal: Draw your own frame, buttons and cursors in one pixel style, split the nav into 'me' and 'you' lists, and offer a theme switch through CSS variables.

title: FORM

signature: Tick boxes and radio dots used as pixels, drawing letters out of the web's most boring widgets.
why: It finds an aesthetic inside the medium's default parts, and the controls stay interactive, so the artwork looks different in every browser and decade.
steal: Treat native form controls as a pixel palette: place checkboxes and radios on a grid to draw shapes and let visitors click them.

why: The typeface enacts the artist's subject inside the interface, and three columns plus a circular menu make a large archive browsable on one screen.
steal: Let your typography enact your subject: offset each letter's baseline randomly, and set menu words around a circle.
