name: What shape is the internet?
one_line: A grid of 33 patent-drawing crops, each centred on whatever shape the drafter used to depict 'Internet'.

look.type: Lato bold ~28px title; Lato regular 14px for byline and standfirst; no other text on the page.
look.color: White page, black line drawings, one link blue (#4283d1), thin #ccc frames around each tile.
look.layout: Three equal columns of ~370x240px tiles with ~10px gutters; title, byline and one-sentence standfirst above.
look.imagery: Cropped patent figures centred on the labelled 'Internet' shape: cloud, starburst, hexagon, bean, highway, lump, neighbours clipped.

behaviour: No JavaScript; 33 CSS background-image tiles, each a link out (presumably to its source patent); sizes use vw units.
signature: One question as the h1, then a uniform grid of patent crops all centred on a shape labelled 'Internet'.
why: Same crop, same scale, same frame makes the shape the only variable, so the grid argues for itself; the question as title needs no commentary.
steal: Make an argument with a uniform grid: crop every example to one frame and size, make the question the h1, and add no commentary.
moves: uniform crops centred on one label
each tile links to its source
thin grey frames and tight gutters

title: Manifesto for (Web)Site-Specific Art
name: Manifesto for (Web)Site-Specific Art
one_line: A manifesto on websites as art: text columns running off the right edge under ASCII clouds, in four layouts.

look.type: Typewriter-like mono caps ~20-28px for titles; light grey Helvetica-like sans ~12px for body; ASCII glyphs as drawing.
look.color: White page; black mono titles, mid-grey body, lighter grey questions; small turquoise chain icons and black flower glyphs.
look.layout: Text columns about 300px wide in a horizontal row running off the right edge; centred title and view switch above.
look.imagery: ASCII clouds drawn with parentheses and underscores in light grey; black flower dingbats scattered along the foot; turquoise chain icons.

behaviour: A switch under the title offers Box, List, Popup and Doc views; back arrow top-left, 'How to read' top-right. The live page timed out, so details are unverified.
signature: The same manifesto offered in four layouts (Box, List, Popup, Doc), so the reader chooses how to read it.
why: Offering the text in several forms enacts the claim that a website is material; ASCII clouds draw decoration from the text's own characters, so the page stays one voice.
steal: Offer long text in several reading modes behind a four-word switch under the title, and draw decoration from the same characters as the text.
moves: four-way reading-mode switch (Box, List, Popup, Doc)
questions in lighter grey after each section
dingbat flowers scattered at the foot

title: Code of Design
name: Code of Design
one_line: Ten ethical principles for designers, set as a numbered list of links in black on pure screen green.

look.type: Inter: black-weight title ~80px, medium-weight list up to 48px under fluid clamp(1.35rem, 4vw, 3rem); every item underlined.
look.color: Pure #00ff00 background with black text and rules; links are underlined black, not blue; nothing else.
look.layout: Left-aligned stack at the top: outlined language box, title, ten-item list filling the width; a thick black rule closes the screen.
look.imagery: None; text only.

behaviour: Svelte app (3 words in static HTML); each principle is a link; an outlined 'English (United States)' language switch sits top-left.
signature: Ten principles as a numbered list of underlined links at poster size on full-saturation #00ff00.
why: Pure screen green is the loudest possible ground, so ten sentences read as a manifesto; the list is itself the navigation, so nothing competes with the words.
steal: Put the whole argument on the front page as a numbered list of links at 4vw on one flat full-saturation colour with black text.
moves: language selector as a plain outlined box

title: Fuse.kiwi - Interesting Internet
name: Fuse.kiwi
one_line: Guide to the creative web: a physics ball-pit filter above a hairline grid of submitted links.

look.type: Syne (wide quirky grotesk) ~26px for titles and nav; Syne Mono ~12px for category, domain and date; tiny mono labels.
look.color: Pale grey #f2f2f2 page, #1a1a1a text; acid-lime balls, black pill labels, #ebff00 yellow as hover accent.
look.layout: Top icon-and-label nav row; a ~600px ball-pit canvas; then a six-column hairline grid, each card with the same six slots.
look.imagery: Submitted sites' thumbnails (posters, apparel, type specimens) in cards; hundreds of flat lime circles with dashed outlines in the pit.

behaviour: Next.js canvas physics: balls pile up and category pills float among them; Shuffle and Ball Pit toggle views; paste-link submit pill; tip-jar link.
signature: A physics ball pit of lime balls with category pills floating in it is the filter, sitting over a hairline grid of links.
why: A playful physical filter makes choosing a category something to poke, while the hairline grid below keeps every item to identical slots so scanning stays fast.
steal: Pair one toy-like control (physics balls, pill filters) with a strict hairline grid where tag, flag, image, title, domain and date sit in the same slot every time.
moves: physics ball pit as the filter
paste-link submit pill in the corner

title: Websitesite
name: Websitesite
one_line: One person's whole practice as a bordered table of small websites, each with a one-sentence description.

look.type: Basier-like grotesk 11pt in cells, tiny bold column heads, all centred; links in default blue underline.
look.color: White page, 1px black table borders, default #0000ee links; the only colour is the thumbnails' own.
look.layout: One full-width table: three version-thumbnail columns, then Title, Year, Category and Description; every cell centred, a small title above.
look.imagery: Tiny screenshots of each site's v.1, v.2 and v.3 in the left columns, many cells empty.

behaviour: jQuery with keydown; 91 links; each title opens a separate small website; the table is the only navigation.
signature: A portfolio that is only a table of 20-odd tiny websites, each described in one plain sentence, with version columns v.1 v.2 v.3.
why: Treating the practice as a spreadsheet shows scale and variety at once; plain descriptions ('A way to call Jisu good night') carry the humour; version columns make revision part of the work.
steal: Show a body of small projects as a bordered table: title, year, category, one-line plain description starting 'A... to...', plus version thumbnails.
moves: version columns v.1 v.2 v.3 with thumbnails

name: A Critical Field Guide for Working with Machine Learning Datasets
one_line: A 17,000-word guide to ML datasets laid out inside a fake spreadsheet with column letters, row numbers and merged cells.

look.type: IBM Plex Mono throughout: ~32px caps for title and contents head, 13-15px in cells; links in pure blue.
look.color: White cells, black cell borders, light grey (#efefef) row and column headers, #0000ff for links; nothing else.
look.layout: Faux spreadsheet: lettered columns A to BH, numbered rows, content in merged cells; title block framed by a mosaic of tiny cells.
look.imagery: No images; the cell grid, subdivided into nested squares of different sizes, forms the decorative border.

behaviour: Pure HTML and CSS (1 KB of JS); 22,130 elements render the sheet, footnotes are {1} {2} braces, links go to numbered sections; 1.5 MB of HTML.
signature: A long essay about datasets is laid out inside a spreadsheet, with column letters, row numbers and cell borders as the page chrome.
why: The container is the argument: reading about datasets inside rows and columns makes the reader feel the data form; one monospace face and one blue keep the illusion exact.
steal: Let the subject's own form be the layout: render real headers, merged cells and cell borders in HTML, with default-blue links, for content about data.
moves: whole essay as a spreadsheet UI
mosaic of nested cells as decorative frame
column letters and row numbers as chrome

title: 02042023 — access ecologies
name: access ecologies - 02042023
one_line: A daily blog page addressed by date: one italic sentence, one winter photograph, arrows to the neighbouring days.

look.type: Bold geometric-sans caps title, light tagline, plum serif caps nav, navy mono date, olive italic display serif ~60px for the quote.
look.color: White page with a faint halftone cream veil at the top; olive quote, plum nav, navy date, charcoal title.
look.layout: Narrow ~790px column: title and nav row, date with arrows, three-line quote, then a full-width photograph aligned to the quote's left edge.
look.imagery: One colour photograph of snow on pine branches per entry; dithered halftone veil fading in at the top.

behaviour: Entries live at date URLs (/02042023) with previous and next arrows beside the date; an archive page exists. The live page did not load, so unverified.
signature: Each day is a page named by its date: one italic sentence in olive, one photograph, arrows to yesterday and tomorrow.
why: Five type voices still read as order because each has one fixed job (title, nav, date, quote); one photo and one sentence a day turns the blog into a ritual.
steal: Give each entry one photograph and one italic sentence, name the page by its date, and put previous and next arrows beside a mono date.
moves: italic pull-quote above a full-width photo

title: De|reconstructing Interactions: Computing Concepts for Designers (beta)
name: De|reconstructing Interactions
one_line: Workshop page for Computing Concepts for Designers, in browser-default Times with a tilted title and a 1990s 3D render.

look.type: Times New Roman at default: tilted ~120px title, blue ~70px tilted subtitle, 32px body; strikethrough used as an honest edit.
look.color: White page, black text, link-blue subtitle, and a teal-and-purple 90s 3D render; no designed palette.
look.layout: Rotated headline overlapping a top-right image, a tilted blue subtitle beneath, then a centred ~950px text column with wide gaps.
look.imagery: Low-poly teal-and-purple 3D figure crouched beside a retro computer; 13 GIFs on the page.

behaviour: Webflow page with 13 GIFs and 4 iframes; title and subtitle rotated in CSS; struck-through text shows the beta call is closed; links to a newsletter and YouTube.
signature: A Times New Roman headline tilted across a 1990s 3D-render man crouching beside a beige computer.
why: Deliberately default type plus a period 3D image signals 'computing from first principles' before a word is read; striking through the closed call, rather than deleting it, is an honest edit.
steal: When teaching fundamentals, use browser-default Times and one period-correct 3D image; tilt the title; strike through out-of-date offers instead of deleting them.

title: Daylight
name: Daylight
one_line: One-screen page for Daylight, an app that notifies you when days get longer; the domain has since expired.

look.type: Grilli Type grotesk ~28px for the statement, ~16px for labels and credits; names set darker than the surrounding sentence.
look.color: One warm apricot ground (~#fed99b) with rust-brown text (~#a0451a) at several opacities; the sun disc runs yellow to orange to periwinkle.
look.layout: One ~490px column offset left of centre with generous vertical gaps: statement, row of three icons, credits, footnote.
look.imagery: Three app icons: pale rounded squares with an orange-violet gradient sun disc, Android's a full disc; small blue dot.

behaviour: Static page; today the domain redirects to an expired-domain sale listing (daylight.today for sale), so the original is gone.
signature: The page colour is the daylight: one orange-violet gradient disc is the whole logo and illustration on an apricot field.
why: Making the subject (sunlight) the entire palette makes a tiny app feel finished; tonal text, with names darker than sentences, builds hierarchy from a single hue.
steal: Pick one warm ground colour tied to your subject, set all text in darker tones of it at two opacities, and let one gradient circle be the whole logo.
moves: one-hue page: apricot ground, rust text at two opacities
icon row with open and get links
names darker than the sentence around them

title: Interspecies Library
name: Interspecies Library

signature: A neon-green halo around a photo of a face hidden behind a creature book, under a melted-chrome LIBRARY logotype.
why: One saturated glow on an otherwise quiet grey page marks the single image that matters; the chrome lettering gives the subject, hybrid creatures, a form of its own.
steal: On a quiet neutral page, give the hero photo one saturated neon glow and set the paragraph in a semi-mono in a deep ink colour, centred in a narrow column.

look.imagery: Installation and print photos (iridescent glass, book in grass, ice sculpture, rune graphics) plus video players with default grey controls.

signature: A tabloid-style feed where each project is a dated paragraph led by an arrow glyph, under a masthead pairing grotesk with blackletter.
why: Writing projects as one-paragraph notes (what, when, with whom) makes the portfolio read like a newspaper column; blackletter against grotesk gives the masthead character.
steal: Write each project as a dated one-paragraph note led by a glyph, stagger them in four columns with media between, and put one blackletter word in a grotesk masthead.

yellow highlighter on a status tag

title: Lineto.com
name: Lineto: Bradford

look.color: White canvas; chips in black (pages), red-orange ~#ff3a0a (open section), green (family), light grey (cuts), all with white text.
look.layout: Left-aligned chip column where indentation shows hierarchy; floating segmented control top-centre; empty canvas right; theme toggle bottom-left.
look.imagery: None in the capture (specimen area still blank); type specimens fill the canvas once loaded.

why: Colour-coded chips show hierarchy with no icons; one chip per style lets a designer jump to a weight in a click, and the empty canvas leaves the specimen as the only content.
steal: For a family with many styles, give each style its own small tag in a vertical stack; colour the open section red, the family green; leave the canvas empty.
moves: colour encodes role: page, open section, family, cut

title: Rapid - Typefaces - Source Type
name: Source Type: Rapid

steal: Tint the whole page in the typeface's own identity colour, keep four corner controls (back, section, login, add to cart), and draw the cookie prompt as a bitmap-font speech bubble.
moves: whole page tinted with the typeface's colour

title: GAZING
name: GAZING
one_line: A shared night-sky site that only opens 7PM to 5AM local time; by day it shows one apology line.

look.type: Bold typewriter-style slab mono ~28px headline over ~13px mono body, centred, charcoal on white.
look.color: Pure white page and charcoal text; the night view is unseen in the capture.
look.layout: Two centred lines in the middle of an otherwise empty viewport; nothing else.

why: Time-gating turns the experience into an appointment; a polite closed sign teaches the rule, builds anticipation and gives the night view its meaning, and the plainness makes absence deliberate.
steal: Gate an experience by the visitor's local time and design the closed state: one bold sentence plus the opening hours, nothing more.

one shared sky for everyone at once
empty white day page against a dark night

title: MEETINGROOM
name: MEETINGROOM

steal: Split the first screen into two white halves with one thin saturated gutter line; list sub-sections as caps links with hairline rules under each row.

yellow gutter between two white halves
caps menu rows with hairline rules

why: The tool's output is the interface: the generated type sets its own title, so demo and brand are one thing; two colours keep attention on the glyphs.
steal: Set the page title in the tool's own output, and keep all controls to white hairline outlines on one saturated field with one hot active colour.

one saturated field plus one hot red

steal: On a resource landing page, scatter the actual assets around the headline and use two of them as arrows aimed at the one button.

title: AWX

one_line: A 'node' whose access depends on live weather and ecological data, shown as a table of generative environment widgets.

signature: A website that opens or closes with the weather at its server, shown as a switchboard of small weather instruments.
why: The concept is the interface: environmental data governs the page, and the plain ruled table makes it feel like field equipment rather than branding. Timeouts may be intended.
steal: Tie one real data feed to the site's behaviour or availability and expose it as a labelled table of small instruments in default fonts.

steal: Where articles lack art, generate a flat-colour cover with title top and author bottom, and mix with photo covers on a zero-gutter three-column grid.

signature: A wordmark so blurred and halftoned it looks in motion, sitting alone on white.
why: Edge blur gives a static logo kinetic energy; keeping everything else to a plain two-line header gives the mark full authority.
steal: Blur and halftone the edges of a bold logotype, then leave the rest of the page as a plain bold sans name and a serif caps nav line.
moves: bold sans plus serif caps pairing

title: Raymond Arevalo

why: Tiny, tight grotesk text signals confidence and speed; one moving ticker carries the only call to action, so the page asks for exactly one thing.
steal: Put availability in a fixed rounded-pill marquee at the bottom of the viewport and keep everything above it at 13px.

title: aitorbaigorri
name: Aitor Baigorri

look.layout: Four-column text strip, then the huge centred timer overlapped by outlined hand-lettering, then alternating white and black bands.

signature: A giant serif countdown to the next issue, overprinted by loose outlined hand-lettering.
why: A ticking number gives the page urgency; mixing a sharp grotesk with an outsized serif and a hairline scribble keeps a monochrome layout lively.
steal: Set a live countdown at 150px in a serif, overprint it with a hand-drawn outline scribble, and caption it in bold grotesk caps above.

title: a website is a sanctuary
name: a website is a sanctuary (Escape the Algorithm)

look.color: Pale aqua #cfe6e8 ground, mint #5ad1a1 buttons, a cream-yellow embedded site, dark ink.
look.layout: Standard centred Substack column with a wide embed: rounded room cards at left, a window video at right.
look.imagery: Embedded Firefly Sanctuary: photo thumbnails of home objects (cables, kitchen shelves, bed, guestbook) in rounded cards; a window-screen video.

behaviour: Standard Substack template; the substance is the interview and the embedded site, where each part of a home is a card linking to a 'room'.
signature: A home presented as a website: each corner of the apartment is a rounded card with a small photo and a lowercase label.
why: The page chrome is ordinary; the idea inside is worth keeping as a pattern: treat the rooms of a place as hypertext cards, each a photo and a name.
steal: Show a place as a grid of rounded cards, each with one small photo and a lowercase label, and let each card open a 'room'.
moves: interview as an embedded site tour

title: Invocation — Generative NFT Collection
name: Invocation (Nowhere Gallery)
one_line: Landing page for a 1,000-piece generative audiovisual NFT drop: three stacked 'Invocation' words and a round MINT button.

look.color: Near-black, green-tinted ground; mid-grey title; a steel-blue artwork; the tagline in #222 on black, almost invisible.
look.layout: Monogram top-left, three centred nav items, wordmark stack over an arched artwork, tagline, a circular MINT button at the foot.
look.imagery: An arch-shaped window of blue-grey generative noise behind the title.

behaviour: Wallet connect and mint flow, with the artwork presumably animating in the arch; today the host returns an SSL 503, so unconfirmed.
signature: 'Invocation' repeated three times with the I stems fused into one tall line, like a chant.
why: Repetition performs the title; the arch turns a screen into a window or chapel, and the dark-on-dark tagline suggests something still to arrive.
steal: Repeat the key word as a stack and let the first-letter stems join into one tall rule in front of an arched image.
moves: repeated word stack with fused stems

title: GASS Records
name: GASS Records
one_line: Record label site: a red and green stacked list of releases and links whose rows slide over each other.

look.type: Huge flourished swash-caps 'GASS' wordmark (~320px) in lilac; tiny Neue Haas Grotesk Display caps for rows; HWT Bulletin and Perfetto elsewhere.
look.color: Deep green #00220b and pure red #ff0000 in alternating bands, a lilac nav bar, black-and-lilac op-art checks.
look.layout: Split header (red wordmark panel, op-art lens), a lilac nav bar, then full-width rows labelled RELEASE or LINK that stack as you scroll.
look.imagery: Op-art checkerboard with a bulging circle, a cigarette in a grey gradient strip, peach rounded cover thumbnails peeking behind rows.

behaviour: Next.js; sticky rows appear to overlap as you scroll; Bandcamp embeds; drag and pointer handlers; Adobe Fonts.
signature: Release and link rows are full-width red and green slabs that slide over each other like a deck of cards.
why: Two hard colours turn a plain list into a rhythmic stack; the swash wordmark against tiny caps gives extreme scale contrast.
steal: Alternate two saturated full-width colours for list rows, make each row sticky so they stack as you scroll, and label each in tiny caps.

title: Adam Ho — Index
name: Adam Ho, I.S.P. (Index)
one_line: Designer's portfolio laid out like a Notion document: page tree in a sidebar, three columns of projects, an XP-bar loader.

look.type: Six faces: ABC Oracle variable for ghosted headings, GT Alpina Typewriter, Verily Serif Mono, Herbik; ~11px mono captions; rotated running text.
look.color: White and #ebe6e3 paper, black text, periwinkle #948eff accents; pink, lime and yellow only inside artwork.
look.layout: 180px page-tree sidebar, then three columns: info with a legend matrix, project list, more projects; rotated title strip on the right edge.
look.imagery: Brand and motion work on white cards: a Liquidities logo, Cash App stripes, a Coinbase card render, layered bubble-gum artwork.

behaviour: Loader shows 'Level / Class A' with an XP bar and ASCII 100%; custom cursor; p5, 200 iframes and autoplay videos; sidebar index presumably jumps to projects.
signature: The portfolio opens like a game ('Level, Class A', XP bar) and then reads as a documentation tool with checkbox legends.
why: Treating the portfolio as a working document makes the work feel like a system; the checkbox legend matrix tags every project with disciplines at a glance.
steal: Add a legend matrix of checkbox squares mapping projects to disciplines, plus a page-tree sidebar that doubles as the table of contents.

title: Sissy Screens - Queer Screen Culture
name: Sissy Screens
one_line: Queer screen-culture magazine whose index is a long list of wide-caps titles, each filled with a category-coloured gradient.

look.type: Benton Sans Wide caps ~26px for titles; condensed caps ~10px for nav and category labels; outlined vertical 'SISSY SCREENS' at the right edge.
look.color: Light grey ground; row gradients in yellow, red, pink, blue, indigo and green fading to pale; dark film-still photos.
look.layout: Left 480px list of full-width rows with tiny category labels; right pane: large preview, two thumbnails; vertical READ MORE bars at the edge.
look.imagery: Film stills in the preview pane; the list itself has only type.

behaviour: Hovering or selecting a row likely loads its preview; categories (interview, review, video, merch, photography) filter the list; WordPress with jQuery.
signature: Each article title is a wide-caps row filled with a gradient whose colour encodes its type.
why: Colour coding by category makes a long list scannable without icons; extreme-width caps turn headlines into a graphic texture.
steal: Colour-code content types with a left-to-right gradient fill on each list row, and put a preview pane beside the list.

title: Discwoman
name: Discwoman
one_line: Electronic-music collective's site (now a digital archive…'AMPLIFY EACH OTHER' slogan.

look.type: Extra-wide Eurostile-style caps: slogan ~80px, names ~16px; tiny monospace for the tweet strip and tab nav.
look.color: Plum-black #231c26 ground; everything else, type, rules and tinted photos, in one electric blue (rgb 31,51,241).
look.layout: Tab-style nav, full-width slogan between 1px rules, a tweet ticker row, then a three-column grid of square portraits with names below.
look.imagery: Artist portraits duotoned blue on dark so every photo shares one tint.

behaviour: jQuery; the tweet strip is a carousel with up and down arrows; roster, mixes, about and shop pages; Plausible analytics.
signature: Every photo is tinted the same electric blue, so a varied roster reads as one body.
why: A single-colour duotone unifies photos of mixed quality and lighting, and the blue-on-plum pair stays bold at any size.
steal: Pick one saturated hue, tint every portrait to it on a near-black ground, and set all type and rules in the same hue.

name: Wette auf die Zukunft (Malte Bartsch)
one_line: Exhibition site where visitors flew a real robotic zeppelin through Kunsthalle Wilhelmshaven; now shows autopilot video loops.

look.type: Colossal Helvetica-style grotesk title (~210px, three lines) in violet; tiny neon-green caps UI labels; a serif face in the long texts.
look.color: Grey centre fading to violet side gradients, #6c4cff display type, pure #00ff00 HUD lines and one red alert arc.
look.layout: Three-panel HUD: controls left, giant title centre, zeppelin photo and status right, joined by 1px green lines; radar D-pad below the title.
look.imagery: Photo of a silver zeppelin on wheels, sky and room camera views, line-drawn radar arcs, a circular direction pad.

behaviour: Control panel for the zeppelin: D-pad, sky-camera slider, sky/room view toggle, battery, lidar and motor status; today autoplaying loops; Locomotive scroll; desktop-only notice on mobile.
signature: A colossal violet title dwarfs a neon-green flight console, as if the exhibition were a game HUD.
why: Two systems clash: loose editorial display type against rigid instrument UI; the real robot behind the controls makes the HUD honest rather than decorative.
steal: Set the title enormous in one hue; build functional controls in a second, tiny, high-contrast hue joined by 1px lines.

title: Kunsthalle Osnabrück
name: Kunsthalle Osnabrück
one_line: Kunsthalle site built as a hairline table; the saved hero stacks broken-image icons under giant overlapping blue serif.

look.type: Rand grotesk for the UI at poster size; hero in a Times-like serif ~220px, tracked so tight the letters overlap, white discs biting in.
look.color: White ground, black 1px grid, one pure blue (#0000ff) hero, pale grey frames; broken-image icons add small red and blue marks.
look.layout: Hairline-ruled table filling the viewport; header in the bottom rows: name, hours, DE/EN toggles, then War / Ist / Kommt / Shop / Info.
look.imagery: Browser broken-image and missing-plugin icons scattered inside empty grey frames; the type is the picture.

behaviour: vw sizing scales the whole page like a poster; DE einfach / EN simple plain-language toggles; the screenshot's 'Design +/-' cells seem to be a search field today.
signature: Past, present and future are the nav: War / Ist / Kommt, set at poster scale in a hairline table.
why: The institution's system is a table scaled by viewport units, so nav, address and toggles read as one typographic poster, and plain-language options sit in the main header, not a footer.
steal: Make the site header a ruled table at the bottom of the screen with address, hours, language toggles and sections named by tense.
moves: nav named by tense (War / Ist / Kommt)
plain-language DE/EN toggles in the header

title: The Illustrated Mixtape
name: The Illustrated Mixtape

look.type: Comic Sans MS set in vw units (1vw root) for the player and info text; almost no type on the landing screen.
look.color: White ground; colour comes from crayon, marker and cut paper: yellow, red, green, navy, pink, black.
look.layout: A loose scatter of cut-out drawings in the middle of a white square; player bar and Info / Tracks links at the corners.
look.imagery: About 60 hand-drawn shapes with paper, crayon and watercolour textures, abstract rather than literal.

behaviour: Each drawing seems to be a track: a click likely plays the song in a player (markup has video-placeholder, time and track elements); drag handlers; INFO and TRACKS panels.
signature: The track list is a heap of paper cut-outs you can rearrange; each shape is a song.
why: Making the index into an artwork gives every entry a face without a thumbnail grid; Comic Sans in viewport units makes even the credits part of the play.
steal: Turn a playlist into a scatter of hand-cut shapes, one per track, and keep the text list in a corner drawer.

title: GUT Magazine
name: GUT Magazine

look.color: White ground; blue-grey silver metal fill from steel grey to pale silver.
look.layout: One centred object on an empty white screen; nothing else is visible.
look.imagery: A raster logo rendered in scratched aluminium.

signature: A wobbly, hand-drawn word cast in scratched metal, alone on white.
why: Soft, clumsy letterforms in hard metal texture embody the magazine's 'instinctual, clumsy and raw' brief in a single image.
steal: Use a single hand-drawn logo with a physical material texture as the entire first screen.

title: Klimaschau FH Potsdam
name: Klimaschau FH Potsdam
one_line: University climate-semester exhibition: student projects on a pannable canvas, a pill index on the left, a minimap.

signature: A pill-shaped index that fades at its edge, and a thumbnail minimap in the corner showing where you are on the canvas.
why: The canvas shows every project at once while the pills give linear access; the grain gradient gives mood without relying on images.
steal: Pair a freeform canvas with a pill index list and a corner minimap, so people can browse spatially or by name.

title: Beepy Bella
name: Beepy Bella
one_line: Jewellery shop whose home page is a 3D-rendered portrait with chrome pink script lettering spilling past the frame.

look.type: Chrome-rendered pink calligraphic logotype ~500px; Söhne for shop UI at 10-13px; a letterspaced serif marquee on a lime strip.
look.color: Pink, raspberry and mauve in the render; chartreuse strip; white page, black UI text, lilac #b9a5ff accents.

signature: A chrome-lettered logo bigger than the picture, crossing the frame and the viewport edge.
why: Lettering that breaks out of the image frame creates depth and makes the product world feel like one rendered universe; plain shop UI underneath keeps buying simple.
steal: Let a 3D-rendered logotype overflow its hero image on one side while nav and shop UI stay tiny and plain.
moves: marquee strip for the shipping notice
emoji and kaomoji in menu labels

title: Papiripar
name: Papiripar

signature: A poster-sized magenta blob-matrix on vermilion, with navigation set as grey highlighter chips along the bottom.
why: Sizing everything in vw makes the page behave like a poster; chip-style nav is cheap yet unmistakable, and the clashing colour pair is memorable.
steal: Size all type in vw so the page scales like a poster; set nav as flat grey chips at the foot and use one clashing pair for the emblem.

title: N10.AS® RADIO - WORLD WIDE WADIO
name: N10.AS Radio

look.type: Fixedsys Excelsior pixel font (~15px) in windows and chat; huge white Helvetica Narrow show title (~70px) in a black bar; bold caps ticker.
look.color: Win98 greys with bevels, pure blue panels, a black title bar, yellow ticker, red close buttons and a red LED clock.
look.layout: Full-viewport desktop: left icon dock, top toolbar with player and thumbnails, overlapping floating windows (bulletin, shop, shows, chat), bottom ticker.

signature: A working 1998 desktop: drag windows, chat live and filter shows by genre tag while a cat sits behind.
why: The desktop metaphor gives each feature a natural home (window for chat, window for shop), and bevelled controls say 'press me' without extra labels.
steal: Use a desktop metaphor for multi-feature sites: one draggable window per feature, a dock for apps, and a ticker line for announcements.

title: Rutgers Design Lecture Series
name: Rutgers Design Lecture Series (Spring 2021)

look.color: Six flat pastels in rotation: yellow #f2eb41, lilac #d8cef9, green #75e571, ochre #dbc582, peach #ffd9ba, sky #b4cef9; white ovals; one blue disc.
look.layout: Full-width stacked bands: date oval at left, title centre, two ovals at right that stretch to the band height; a fixed round badge bottom-right.

signature: The white ovals deform with the row: tall rows make tall ellipses, so the buttons look like tablets of different sizes.
why: A 50% radius on content-sized boxes lets variable text drive the shapes, a rich look from one CSS rule; bright bands make the syllabus scannable.
steal: Give every list row a full-width flat colour and put the date and actions in 50%-radius white ovals that stretch to the row height.
moves: 50%-radius ovals that stretch with row height

title: Toph Tucker
name: Toph Tucker
one_line: A two-sentence bio whose letters behave as particles drifting across the screen, driven by D3 force and Perlin noise.

look.type: Browser-default Times-like serif; single letters range from about 14 to 30px; link letters render in default blue, plain text in black.

signature: The bio and its links are a swarm of individual letters, with link colour kept as blue letters in the cloud.
why: Making text physical shows the author's craft (a data-visualisation engineer) in one page; default fonts and colours leave the motion as the only decision.
steal: Turn your own bio into letter particles on a force simulation, but keep a default serif and native link blue so it still reads as text.
moves: tilt and pointer nudge the letters
bio kept in an HTML template

title: A real site of Sohyeon
name: A real site of Sohyeon
one_line: A site shaped like a building: six colour-square 'rooms' (101, 102, 201, 202, EG1, EG2), each a separate project.

look.layout: Fixed 50/50 split: gradient 'sky' with clip-art at left; 2x3 grid of colour tiles at right, each with a 9vh icon in its corner.
look.imagery: Animated bird GIF, photographic cloud strip, tree foliage PNG; black-and-white polygon-circle icons on the tiles.

behaviour: Hand-coded HTML/CSS, about 5 KB: fixed tiles, links turn yellow on hover, clouds drift via CSS animation, titles name rooms (Room 201: See you soon); rooms open other Neocities sites.
signature: The gradient on the left is cut into six squares on the right, and each square is a numbered room.
why: One palette used twice (as sky and as tiles) ties collage to navigation; room numbers turn a link list into architecture.
steal: Build the palette as one multi-stop gradient, then reuse each stop as a flat navigation tile; name the links like rooms.

title: umru
name: umru
one_line: Producer's Cargo site: a mirrored chrome-and-teal render beside a bio in which every name is a search-glyph link.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk ~22px grey body; teal underlined links each prefixed with a ⌕ glyph; a vertical 3D chrome logotype along the seam.

look.layout: Fixed split: image left, scrolling text column right; today the page opens on tour dates and stacks many more images.
look.imagery: A mirrored macro 3D render of glass or chrome with red and cyan glow; a spiky chrome wordmark.

behaviour: Cargo with scroll listeners and hover-heavy links; embeds for Bandcamp, Tumblr and Substack; about 400 images further down; the saved bio view is no longer the first screen.
signature: Every proper noun in the bio is a ⌕ search link: the 'search-engine-optimized musician' joke built into the typography.
why: One joke is made functional: links look like search queries, so the bio doubles as a link tree and keeps the tone, while one bright hue marks every link.
steal: Prefix every outbound link with a tiny glyph that carries a joke (here a search icon) and colour all links one bright hue against grey body text.

vertical chrome logotype on the seam

title: Tiger Dingsun
name: Tiger Dingsun
one_line: Designer's portfolio: a plain numbered list of 15 projects beside a heap of photos and drawings thrown at random angles.

look.color: White page; colour comes only from photographs, graph paper and coloured-pencil scribbles.
look.layout: 235px sidebar with a hairline right border holds the list; the rest is a pile of about 40 overlapping, rotated images.
look.imagery: Casual nature snapshots (forest path, lake, sunflower), graph paper with pencil hatching, tile patterns, soft shadows.

signature: A pile of photos on a desk beside a bare default-font list: the unstyled index sets off the casual heap.
why: Default type and a numbered list leave the heap as the only decision; random rotation and soft shadow read as physical prints.
steal: Pair a default-font numbered list with a heap of randomly rotated photos with soft shadows; let each list item surface its pile.

title: Reading Machines
name: Reading Machines
one_line: Publishing platform for non-teleological reading: a table of 22 texts, each reinterpreted as its own website.

look.type: Sans-serif title ~64px with tight tracking; ~16px table text centred in columns; italic tagline.
look.color: Cornflower blue (CSS named colour) ground with cornsilk text and hairlines; nothing else.
look.layout: Title row with a mute button, then a ruled four-column table (No., Title, Author, Mobile?), then two short paragraphs.
look.imagery: None; each title leads to a separate site.

behaviour: Tone.js web audio plays in many pieces; MUTE toggle top-right; a note says to click the screen if sound is blocked; 'Mobile?' says which pieces work on phones.
signature: A 'Mobile?' column in the index that admits which readings only work on desktop.
why: Naming limits honestly builds trust; two CSS named colours and hairline rules show how little a flexible index needs.
steal: In an index of experimental pieces, add a 'Mobile? Yes/No' column and a global MUTE button instead of hiding constraints.
moves: named CSS colours cornflowerblue and cornsilk

title: Chimeric Worlding
name: Chimeric Worlding
one_line: Tiger Dingsun's graphic-design thesis on poetics and world-building, laid out as four ruled panes with phylogenetic diagrams.

look.type: 80px grotesk title mixing roman and italic, Menlo monospace for the numbered exercises, ~17px sans body; every glyph the same olive.
look.color: Olive (the CSS keyword) type and 1px rules on gainsboro grey; the only other ink is the black linework of the diagrams.
look.layout: Four panes split by 1px olive rules that cross at a small circle: title, diagrams, exercises and essay each get one.
look.imagery: Nine black line-drawn phylogenetic tree diagrams (A to I) in rectangular, slanted and circular layouts.
