signature: A thesis page cut into four ruled quadrants that meet at a small circle, with one olive ink doing all the work.
why: One hue plus visible structure (rules, the circle) gives a long academic text a designed feel; the diagrams carry the pictures while the text stays plain and readable.
steal: Choose one hue for all text and rules on a neutral grey, then divide the screen into independently scrolling panes with 1px lines.
moves: ruled quadrant panes meeting at a circle
roman and italic in one title block

title: LP–20X20
name: LP-20X20
one_line: Twenty friends each pick twenty songs from 2020, shown as sideways-scrolling arched playlist columns over a giant CD.

look.type: High-contrast Didone-style serif ~38px for friends' names with roman-numeral superscripts; ~16px Helvetica-style sans for titles, smaller artist lines.
look.color: One dodger blue (#1e90ff) for every glyph and hairline on white, seen through the pastel rainbow sheen of the CD behind.
look.layout: Equal-width columns, one per friend: arched top border, name, then a numbered 1-20 list with hairline row rules; the page scrolls sideways.
look.imagery: One oversized blurred iridescent CD photograph fixed behind the lists; crossed-swords and clover emoji in the title.

behaviour: Columns scroll sideways; deviceorientation, geolocation, mousemove and drag listeners suggest the CD reacts to tilt or pointer; a MEGAMIX pill probably plays or merges all lists (unclear).
signature: Twenty personal playlists as twenty arched columns over one huge translucent CD, all inked in a single blue.
why: A playlist is a list, so the design is a list; personality comes from the arch tops, the Didone names and one colour rather than decoration, and the huge CD gives mood without hurting legibility.
steal: Give each contributor an identical column with an arched top and a serif name; keep every row the same height and let one blue do all the colouring.

title: OnX Variable
name: OnX Variable
one_line: A student variable-font specimen where the pointer morphs enormous letters between two forms on a blue field.

look.type: Custom variable font OnX with weight and sharpness axes; at weight 0 glyphs become spiky star-lattices; ~17px Apercu for labels, sizes up to 2800px.
look.color: Electric blue (#0047ff) full-bleed with white glyphs; later sections use #3e3e3e and near-black #07070a.
look.layout: Full-screen centred glyph cluster with live axis readouts pinned to opposite corners; later sections stack specimen grids, a 72pt sample and prose.
look.imagery: No images; the letterforms themselves, enormous and spiked, are the picture.

behaviour: Mousemove appears to write --wght and --shrp (0-100) into font-variation-settings; corner readouts show 'Weight' and 'Sharpness' live. Page asks for a larger screen.
signature: Move the mouse and giant letters melt through the 'middle space' between two forms while axis numbers tick in the corners.
why: The interface is the typeface: no menu or chrome, one control surface (the pointer) and numeric feedback, so visitors learn the axes by playing instead of reading a manual.
steal: Show a variable font at screen-filling size, bind pointer x and y to its axes, and print the live axis values in tiny type in two corners.

title: HTML Frames
name: HTML Frames
one_line: A thesis on 'jettisoning the frame' built as a literal eight-pane HTML frameset of thesis sub-pages.

look.type: Thin all-caps grotesk ~28px, centred, white on black in the title pane; other panes unreadable in the capture (blurred).
look.color: Pure black panes divided by light-grey gutters about 3px wide; the only colour is a blurred blue sky photo in the first pane.
look.layout: Frameset with columns of 20/50/15/15 percent and two rows; panes of very different widths tile the screen like an uneven wall.
look.imagery: Blurred pane previews: a sky photo, text blocks, thumbnails, white boxes; unclear whether the blur is deliberate.

behaviour: Static <frameset> loading eight sub-pages from the same author; the markup is sloppy (unclosed rows quote, stray backslash, href on a frame) yet renders. No JS, no CSS.
signature: A thesis about leaving the frame, delivered in the most literal frames the web ever had.
why: Form restates argument: an obsolete element is both subject and layout, so the thesis shows simultaneous states side by side instead of one scrolling page.
steal: When the topic has a literal web metaphor, use the matching obsolete element (frameset, marquee, table) as the layout instead of imitating it with divs.

title: PPS
name: PPS - Personal Positioning System
one_line: MFA thesis site by Laura de Baldeon; now gone because Glitch ended project hosting.

look.type: Helvetica-style grotesk ~40px in all caps, two lines per column, tight leading, acid yellow-green on blue.
look.color: Ultramarine band (about #0050ff) with acid lime-yellow text (about #dcff00); the rest of the capture is blank white.
look.layout: A full-width header band about 110px tall split into two equal columns, title left and author right; the viewport below is empty.
look.imagery: None visible; the page below the band is blank in the capture.

behaviour: Today Glitch serves 'project hosting is no longer available' (410). The capture shows only the header band; content was probably loaded by script and is lost.
signature: A two-column electric blue title bar in acid-yellow caps, then an unexplained void of white.
why: A saturated blue and lime pairing makes a thesis recognisable from type alone, at no cost. The empty body (loading or lost) shows the risk: nothing below the band invites a next step.
steal: Set title and author as a two-column all-caps band in one saturated ground with one contrasting text colour, and show something real directly beneath it.

title: A Fountain by Serena Chen (BFA 21')
name: A Fountain
one_line: Serena Chen's generative-design class piece: a full-screen dithered stone fountain with a typed line; Glitch hosting is gone.

look.type: Widely letter-spaced monospace-style sans ~16px at top-left, reading 'You a' as if mid-typing.
look.color: Strictly 1-bit black and white: stippled dots on white, no greys, no colour.
look.layout: The fountain image fills the viewport edge to edge; one small line of text sits in the top-left corner.
look.imagery: A 1-bit dithered photograph of a three-tier stone garden fountain, its spray scattered into single dots.

behaviour: Gone (Glitch hosting retired, 410). The cut-off 'You a' suggests text typing out over the image; spray may have animated, as the class brief was generative systems (unclear).
signature: A stock fountain turned into pure stipple, filling the whole screen with one sentence typing in the corner.
why: One dithered image at full bleed plus one line of text is enough to set a mood; the 1-bit constraint makes a stock photo feel like an early-Mac artefact.
steal: Run one photograph through 1-bit dithering at screen resolution, let it fill the viewport, and add a single typed line in a corner.
moves: one typed line in a corner

title: Graphic Design Triennial 2021
name: Graphic Design Triennial 2021 (RISD Portals)
one_line: RISD's triennial exhibition site: an enormous statement paragraph buried under a pile of 160 project images.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Display ~96px for the statement, so large it fills the screen; ~16-24px Neue Haas Text for captions.
look.color: Black on white; colour comes only from the work: acid #dcff00 accents, saturated posters, red and black cut-out shapes.
look.layout: Statement paragraph as the base layer; about 160 project images and black crescent cut-outs piled over it at varied sizes, hiding some words.
look.imagery: Posters, book spreads, photos, 3D renders and black cut-out shapes, rectangles overlapping like a pinned-up wall.

behaviour: Gallery split into 'retrospection' and 'speculation' rooms; 326 hover rules, rotation, keyframes, drag and mousemove hint that images shift or can be dragged. Exact mechanism unclear.
signature: The artists' work literally covers the welcome text: a pile of 160 pieces landing on a paragraph about portals.
why: Text becomes a surface that the work overwrites, so the intro is readable in the gaps and a collage backdrop at once; one rule (huge type plus a pile) organises 160 items.
steal: Set the intro in enormous type and pile the work on top at random sizes; let some words stay covered so the viewer moves things to read.
moves: intro text as the bottom layer

title: Flirty Sweet Perfect Sensual Fun Confident Feminine Fantasy
name: Flirty Sweet Perfect Sensual Fun Confident Feminine Fantasy
one_line: A perfume-ad parody: a long domain name as title, ad copy shouted in viewport-sized type on hot pink.

look.type: White Helvetica Roman at 13.5vw with pink glow; key adjectives swapped inline into script faces (Diamonds, SerenityScript) at 1.25-1.75em, overlapping the line above.
look.color: One hot pink (#ff3bc1) fading by vertical gradient to white, with white text glowing pink; nothing else.
look.layout: A single centred column of viewport-width text; each phrase fills a screen, lines stacked tight, nothing but the copy.
look.imagery: No pictures; script fonts supply the ornament. A small music-note icon sits top-left.

behaviour: Ad copy scales with the viewport (root size 13.5vw); custom cursor images, a cursor-follow script and keyframes; the note icon hints at audio (unclear).
signature: A domain name that is the whole product description, then perfume copy shouted at 13.5vw in glowing pink.
why: Absurd specificity and one saturated gradient make a joke about marketing language land in a glance; typography does the parody by cramming script faces into plain Helvetica.
steal: Scale body text with vw units until each phrase fills the screen, then drop key words into a script face with line-height around.25 so it overlaps.

title: dora
name: dora
one_line: Designer Dora Godfrey's whole site: two serif columns of bio, two emoji, an Instagram link and an email address.

look.type: Light text serif (Wremena) ~26px for the bio columns; Neue Haas Grotesk ~20px for the contact line; ragged right, generous leading.
look.color: Black on white only; the sole colour is two emoji, a red mushroom and a pink cherry blossom.
look.layout: Two equal columns, each headed by an emoji: degrees at left, bio at right; Instagram link top-right; large empty space below.
look.imagery: No photos or work samples; the two emoji act as column headings.

behaviour: Static Cargo page (scroll listener, zoom blocked); the work is withheld, with a plain request to email for the resume and commercial portfolio.
signature: A designer's site is two emoji, two serif paragraphs and an email address, with the portfolio held back on request.
why: Withholding the portfolio and trusting size, white space and two emoji makes the bio read as confident; the serif for story and plain sans for the action line separates telling from asking.
steal: Use one light serif for who you are and a plain grotesk for the one action you want (email), and replace section titles with a single emoji.
moves: serif for story, sans for action

title: Field
name: Field
one_line: Harm van den Dorpel's screen-filling grid of loading spinners, each at its own speed, that whirl when touched.

look.type: No type apart from the page title; the 'letters' are 12-bar loading spinners drawn as thin rounded bars at half scale.
look.color: Vertical gradient from near-black #2d2a2a to indigo #2b2f71 in dark mode, lavender #b9b6d0 to white in light; bars invert.
look.layout: A viewport-sized grid of about 17 by 11 spinners at 60px pitch, centred with a margin of a tenth of the shorter side.
look.imagery: Only the spinners: roughly 190 identical thin-barred loading wheels, black in light mode and white in dark.

behaviour: Each spinner turns at a random period (0.2-5.2s); hover makes it whirl at 0.2s for five seconds, mousedown freezes it; resizing reloads the grid; follows prefers-color-scheme.
signature: A lawn of loading spinners, each out of phase: the interface symbol for waiting turned into something calm to touch.
why: It takes the most overlooked UI element and multiplies it until it reads as pattern; one tiny rule (hover excites, press freezes) gives identical parts personality and invites play.
steal: Pick one system UI primitive, tile it across the viewport with a random phase per copy, and add one pointer rule such as hover to excite and press to freeze.
moves: grid of identical loaders with random phase

title: American Express
name: Agaric Fly
one_line: Small-batch incense shop with a collage hero and the slogan 'Language is a virus from outer space'; store now errors.

look.type: Hairline-outlined logotype with a rounded-box 'FLY' over a photo; small Helvetica strapline; incense packs carry varied display lettering.
look.color: Black announcement strip over a saturated grasshopper macro (acid green, navy); white shop grid below with silver and peach packaging.
look.layout: Full-width hero with hamburger left and search and cart right, an inset black-and-white photo card behind the logo, then four products spaced on white.
look.imagery: Macro grasshopper photo, black-and-white hand holding rocks, photographed incense packs on white.

behaviour: Shopify theme; today it returns 503 'There was a problem loading this website' (store down or closed). The original was a standard storefront with an announcement bar.
signature: One strange sentence in a black strip above a macro grasshopper hero: 'Language is a virus from outer space.'
why: A bold collage hero and one odd sentence give a stock Shopify theme a point of view; plain product photography lets the packaging carry the brand.
steal: On a stock store theme, replace the hero with a collage (macro photo, inset black-and-white photo, outline logo) and spend the announcement bar on one strange sentence.
moves: collage hero with inset b/w photo

title: Baltic Circle
name: Baltic Circle
one_line: Helsinki theatre festival's site: a red-on-cream news grid with photographed foliage laid across the columns (2022 edition).

look.type: Red humanist sans, ~28px headlines over ~17px body; bold condensed caps for category tags like 'Uutinen'; logo lettering in a custom face.
look.color: Red text, rules and line art on warm cream; the only other colour is a lemon block and the blossoms of the photographed sprig.
look.layout: Three-column news grid divided by 1px red rules beneath a red top bar; cards stack unevenly while the foliage crosses column lines.
look.imagery: A photographed sprig of leaves and red blossoms plus a red line-drawn coral-like plant, both spilling over the text.

behaviour: WordPress with intersection-observer reveals; the foliage overlay may be fixed or scroll-linked (unclear). Each festival year gets a new identity; the 2026 look was made with Aalto University.
signature: Photographed plants lying across a text-heavy news grid, so the content is read through leaves.
why: Living imagery over a rigid ruled grid gives an institutional news page a hand-laid, seasonal feel; the one-ink rule system keeps text legible underneath.
steal: Run a strict ruled grid in one text colour, then lay a single large cut-out photograph across several cards so the content seems to sit in a physical scene.
moves: category tag in bold condensed caps

title: All Light, Expanded: Interactive Companion
name: All Light, Expanded
one_line: Interactive companion to a documentary on cameras, policing and justice: a scrubbable constellation of references beside the film's reading list.

look.type: Wide-tracked geometric sans caps (Soleil) for the title; Adobe Caslon Pro italic and roman ~21px for text; tiny black time-code pills in bold sans.
look.color: Pale grey stage with grey plus marks, white right column, black ink, sparse cyan (#00b3ff) accent and a thin multicolour timeline strip at the edge.
look.layout: Split screen: 40% left canvas of idea constellations, 60% right scrolling column of title, numbered how-to and references; round black menu button top-right.
look.imagery: Scattered plus marks forming constellations, small interface thumbnails, archival photos such as a sun halo, short looping videos.

behaviour: Scrub the film's timeline to find notes, follow a constellation of related references; time-code pills jump between them; six muted looping videos; Next.js app.
signature: A film's reading list becomes a star map: each plus mark is a quotation placed along a scrubbable timeline.
why: Mapping knowledge spatially instead of as a bibliography makes browsing feel like exploring; six numbered thumbnails teach the unfamiliar interface in one screen.
steal: Teach a novel interface with six numbered thumbnails, one per step, beside a sentence that reuses the same numbers, placed above the first content.

name: And Or Forever
one_line: A near-empty pale-grey interactive piece with a hairline staircase and crosshair, built in SvelteKit and A-Frame.

look.type: No visible type in the capture; the live page shows SCTO Grotesk and FK Raster Grotesk Compact at 9-21px for an index overlay.
look.color: Near-white grey (#ececec), black 1px linework and faint white light streaks; the shared palette adds cyan #00b3ff in overlays.
look.layout: Empty field with a crosshair mark top-left and one black stepped line running off the page like a staircase or circuit.
look.imagery: Faint white flowing light ribbons, probably rendered in A-Frame, behind hairline geometry; no photographs.

behaviour: SvelteKit with swup page transitions and an A-Frame (WebGL) scene; Index and Close buttons only. Interaction beyond that is unclear from the static page.
signature: Almost nothing on screen but a hairline staircase and a crosshair over drifting pale light.
why: Extreme restraint: one thin line gives direction and scale, so the empty field reads as a space to walk through; faint light motion adds depth without decoration.
steal: Draw one continuous 1px line that bends at right angles across a pale grey field and put a small crosshair glyph at the origin as your only logo.

title: chronotrains-eu.vercel.app
name: Chronotrains
one_line: Map showing how far a train takes you from any European station; hover a station to see its reach.

look.type: Inter-style sans: bold ~30px navy headline, ~15px grey body with loose leading, mono caption for the legend; black underlined links.
look.color: Pale grey map ground and white panel with navy (#101828) text; the only colour is a five-step heat ramp from tomato red to pale yellow.
look.layout: Full-height map with a 350px white panel docked right (headline, explainer, legend, contact) and a close button; Mapbox logo bottom-left.
look.imagery: Vector map tiles (blank in the capture); reach is drawn as coloured isochrone bands around the hovered station.

behaviour: Hover any station to colour the map by travel time (1-5 h) via Mapbox. Today's app adds direct and night-train filters, a 1-12 h slider and an area search.
signature: Hover a railway station and the continent recolours as a heat map of how far a train takes you in five hours.
why: One question, one gesture: hover answers it instantly in colour. The panel states method and caveats plainly (20-minute interchanges), which earns trust for a data toy.
steal: Make the primary interaction hover-only and instant; dock a short explainer with its caveats beside a five-step sequential colour legend labelled in the unit.

title: Rave Scout Cookies™ 🚀
name: Rave Scout Cookies
one_line: A rave-safety collective styled as Scouts: gold badge, oath, duties and a 'rave-mergency' hotline, behind an ENTER gate.

look.type: Heavy extra-wide italic caps in gold for the title and ENTER; Karla ~20px for body; small caps ticker line below.
look.color: Gold (#dead28) on a black deep-space star photograph, with off-white #f5f2ee and cobalt #4c65c9 appearing further down the page.
look.layout: Splash: circular seal left, stacked title right, then two thick gold rules enclosing a huge ENTER and the mission paragraph, and a ticker beneath.
look.imagery: Hubble-deep-field star photo, a gold cookie-badge seal with circling text, emoji telephone icons.

behaviour: Splash gate with ENTER; the hotline ticker scrolls; Cargo site with rotated elements, drag and scroll listeners; pages for oath, duties and movement inside.
signature: Boy-Scout-badge parody for rave safety: a cookie seal, an oath, and a hotline ticker scrolling across the splash.
why: Humour carries a serious care mission: scout vocabulary (oath, duties, badges) makes harm reduction memorable, and one gold on black keeps the whole system recognisable.
steal: Borrow the structure of a familiar institution (scouts, guild, union) for your cause: invent the badge, oath and hotline, and keep them all in one colour.

title: Fuse.kiwi - Interesting Internet
name: Fuse.kiwi
one_line: A guide to the creative web: a giant headline in an acid-green ball pit above a grid of submitted sites.

look.type: Syne extra-bold ~170-280px for 'Interesting Internet' with soft blurred edges; Syne Mono ~12px for URLs and dates; Syne ~28px card titles.
look.color: Light grey page, near-black (#1a1a1a) type and a swarm of acid-green balls; the submitted thumbnails supply everything else.
look.layout: Icon-and-label nav row, a screen-height hero, then a six-column hairline-bordered card grid: category and flag, thumbnail, name, URL, date.
look.imagery: Screenshots and artworks of submitted sites as thumbnails; the hero is a canvas ball pit.

behaviour: Hero balls and category pills are physics bodies you can drag; Shuffle reorders the feed, Ball Pit swaps modes, visitors paste a link to submit; pills filter by category.
signature: A giant 'Interesting Internet' headline floating in a pit of green balls you can shove around.
why: The hero makes the curation feel playful before you read it, then the grid goes strictly informational; every card repeats the same five-line pattern, so scanning is fast.
steal: Open with one huge headline over a draggable physics toy in a single acid colour, then switch to a rigid hairline card grid with a fixed metadata pattern.
moves: flag and category on every card

title: FAE3
name: Future Art Ecosystems (FAE)
one_line: Annual art-and-technology strategy briefing, shown in one acid green with white book mockups and pill-shaped fields.

look.type: ABC Diatype ~28-35px lede with italic emphasis and arrow links; Apoc for display; everything one colour.
look.color: All text, link underlines, pill borders and toggle in one acid green (#00dc00) on white; each issue has its own hue (blue, purple, green).
look.layout: Wide single column of large text; three-position toggle top-right; three upright book mockups in a row; rounded-pill newsletter fields below.
look.imagery: White 3D book mockups on white, with titles coloured per issue (blue, purple, green 'coming soon').

behaviour: Per-issue colour; pill inputs with matching outline; a three-state toggle (empty, filled, half circle) at top-right, probably display mode (unclear); Swiper carousels and canvas elsewhere.
signature: The whole site is dipped in one colour matching the current issue's cover, so the brand changes whenever the product does.
why: One colour as the entire palette makes a text-heavy research site instantly recognisable, and recolouring per release encodes versioning without extra graphics.
steal: Pick one saturated hue per release and apply it to text, links, borders and form fields on a white page; change the hue for the next edition.

title: Toro y Moi
name: Toro y Moi
one_line: Album site dressed as an early-2000s web portal: weather widget, quote of the day, joke MSRP.

look.type: Default Times links in browser blue, Helvetica-style bold module headers, red Times quote, tricolour wordmark; sizes mixed like a 2000s portal.
look.color: Lavender-grey ground with primary-colour modules: blue, yellow, lime, green, red banner, white panels; default link blue and a purple clock.
look.layout: 700px boxed page: nav strip, red-framed carousel, guest bar, weather panel beside quote of the day, yellow link strip, email field, news and product boxes.
look.imagery: Street photo of a yellow GoCar with tiled 'BY TYM' watermark, storm-sky weather photo, line-drawn jeepney, LP cover.

behaviour: MAHAL-era widgets: 'Welcome, Guest' with date and time, SF weather, carousel, quote of the day, struck-through MSRP. Today: black-and-white Courier with a marquee.
signature: An album site as a 2000s ISP portal: 'Welcome, Guest', a weather widget and an MSRP of $1999.99.
why: Parodying a dead interface genre gives a musician a voice before any song plays; the details (default link blue, stray widgets, joke price) reward close reading.
steal: Pick a retired web genre (portal, forum, ISP start page) and rebuild its modules with real content, including its worst colour choices and a joke price.

title: Spring '83 Viewer
name: Spring '83 Viewer
one_line: A viewer for Spring '83 boards: strangers' tiny HTML pages pinned as tilted cards, newest first.

look.type: Browser-default Times for the chrome and ages; each board brings its own type: monospace commit logs, giant red italic grotesk, typewriter pink card.
look.color: Floralwhite ground, navy (#112e51) top bar, 1px black card borders; each board adds its own colour (black, pink, white).
look.layout: Tall cards in a loose masonry, each tilted a degree or two, with hash id and relative age as a bold header.
look.imagery: Each card is another person's page: photo collage, ASCII panther,…'THINKING AND WRITING'.

behaviour: Server-rendered feed of Spring '83 boards sorted by recency, with a login link for publishing. Today the live page shows only a login stub, so the feed is gone or script-loaded.
signature: A wall of strangers' tiny HTML pages, each a tilted card stamped with its age in minutes.
why: The viewer styles only the frame (border, id, age) and leaves each board's interior to its author, so the diversity of voices is the visual design; restrained chrome makes that work.
steal: Treat user content as pinned cards: give each the same plain frame with an id and relative age, rotate it a degree or two, and never restyle the inside.
moves: chrome-less viewer around authors' own styles

title: Hanzer Liccini
name: Hanzer Liccini (Studio HanLi)
one_line: Graphic-design studio's type page: each typeface is shown as one huge specimen line in its own pure colour.

look.type: Each family set as an 80-90px specimen line (Timezone serif, Matex grotesk, Colant) with its own HAL lettering; ~12px blue mono for nav and downloads.
look.color: White page; each family in one pure colour (green, red #ff0000, blue) with tiny light-blue (#0099ff) mono links under each.
look.layout: Centred vertical stack of specimens, a slim rail of project thumbnails down the right edge, tiny nav top-left and 'Download Trials' top-centre.
look.imagery: Book covers, posters and objects as slim thumbnails in the right rail; the type specimens are the hero images.

behaviour: Scrolling stack of specimen blocks with 'Download Specimen' links; thumbnail rail links to projects; swiper, typed text and mousemove scripts suggest interactive sample lines (unclear).
signature: Each typeface is a full-width line in its own pure colour, signed by a different custom 'HAL' lettering.
why: Colour and scale distinguish products without UI: no cards or labels, just each font shown as large as possible with one tiny link beneath it.
steal: Show each product as one huge line of live text in its own pure colour with one 12px download link under it; keep the project index in a thin rail.

title: AI — Meech Boakye
name: Meech Boakye - AI
one_line: An artist's field report on their first days with DALL-E 2: a short mono essay and a grid of outputs.

look.type: Monospace ~17px (Monument Grotesk Mono declared), dark grey, one uppercase slash-led heading; olive links.
look.color: Dark grey (#3c3c3c) text on white; olive-green links; the lilac and peach images supply all the colour.
look.layout: Left-aligned text column about 860px wide under a slash-led heading, then a five-column grid of square thumbnails with generous gutters.
look.imagery: DALL-E 2 outputs: a Stonehenge ring with a smiley, dozens of lilac hands holding perforated discs.

behaviour: Static Cargo page: one reflective essay, then about 190 images in a grid; links to the generator and an earlier post; zoom blocked.
signature: A plain mono field report on DALL-E 2 followed by about 190 pastel images of hands holding perforated plates.
why: Plain text plus a regular image grid lets the work be the evidence; the tentative first-person voice ('I don't really know what it means yet') makes documentation feel like a diary.
steal: Document an experiment as a short mono essay, then show every output in one regular grid at small size so patterns across them become visible.

title: The Kool-Aid Factory
name: The Kool-Aid Factory
one_line: A series of zines about how organisations coordinate, sold from a shop whose cart is called a to-do list.

look.type: GT Cinetype Mono ~38px for the headline, brand name in orange caps; GT Cinetype regular ~15px for nav and card titles; mono body.
look.color: Cream (#f8f5ec) page, black 2px outlines, vermilion brand colour, and ten flat cover colours: mint, amber, lilac, teal, green, orange, pink.
look.layout: Notched L-shaped frame for logo and six-cell nav, headline, two thin link strips, then a five-column grid of tall covers with folded corners.
look.imagery: Flat geometric diagrams per issue (concentric circles, node trees, coils, spirals) picturing coordination; corner ribbons and page-curl details.

behaviour: WordPress shop reskinned as zines: 'My content cart' and 'My To-Do List (0)' replace the cart; Lottie, canvas and reduced-motion rules; changelog page; newsletter strip.
signature: Each cover is a flat black-outlined diagram of a way teams coordinate, and the cart is a to-do list.
why: A strict system (2px outline, flat fill, one diagram per cover) makes ten colourful covers read as one series; renaming cart to to-do list keeps the joke inside the interface.
steal: Give every item in a series the same outline and card shape, a different flat colour and one geometric diagram of its subject; rename UI nouns to fit.

title: A Growing Culture | WE BELIEVE IN FOOD SOVEREIGNTY. FOR EVERYONE. EVERYWHERE.
name: A Growing Culture
one_line: A food-sovereignty non-profit's site: a hero video, then a four-line mission statement in huge white caps on black.

look.type: Helvetica Bold caps: ~12px nav, ~65px white mission headline; condensed caps for the wordmark; icon font in the footer.
look.color: Black and white only: black nav and statement section, charcoal video well, white type; no accent in the capture.
look.layout: Black nav bar, full-width hero video well, then a black section with a left-aligned four-line headline; footer links and social icons.
look.imagery: Hero video (failed in the capture, printing a raw 'Media error' message) with a centred seed-and-wheat logo.

behaviour: Autoplaying muted hero video (showing a visible codec error in the capture), scroll cue, dropdown nav; Divi on WordPress with many scripts.
signature: Four lines of white Helvetica Bold caps on black state the whole creed: food sovereignty for everyone, everywhere.
why: A single declarative sentence at poster scale gives a non-profit confidence; the failed video shows the risk of leading with media that has no fallback.
steal: Open with one mission sentence in four short lines of huge white caps on black; if you lead with video, give it a poster image and an error fallback.

title: xtraňo®
name: xtraño
one_line: A painter's portfolio: solarised, fluorescent still lifes scattered on white with gallery-label captions; Squarespace domain now expired.

look.type: Compact grotesk ~20px black for nav; ~12px captions with roman title and italic translation; a ~32px black marquee line at the bottom.
look.color: White ground; the works are solarised near-fluorescent yellows, greens, hot pinks and pool blues, so colour lives only in the art.
look.layout: Paintings scattered at different sizes and offsets across a wide white field, tiny captions beneath each, a title marquee along the bottom edge.
look.imagery: Posterised tropical still lifes (anthuriums on a tray, roses) and blue-tiled swimming pools, titled in Spanish with English in italics.

behaviour: Squarespace gallery with a horizontally scrolling title ticker ('Memories of Underdevelopment _ Memorias del Subdesarrollo'); the site is now a 'Website Expired' notice.
signature: Fluorescent solarised still lifes float on white with bilingual captions, under a scrolling Spanish-English title line.
why: The page steps back so saturated artwork is the only colour; bilingual italic captions with sizes in inches read like gallery labels and add authority without decoration.
steal: Caption works like gallery wall labels: title in roman, translation in italic, size in inches, 12px black under each unframed image.

title: lithuanian_space_agency
name: Julijonas Urbonas - Lithuanian Space Agency
one_line: An artist-engineer's site: letters on loose baselines, nav words in a ring, margin line numbers beside project text.

look.type: Declared face 'Unica Gravity', whose letters sit on shifting baselines; tracked caps ~13px for lists, ~20px mixed-case body; blue italic labels.
look.color: Black on white with one periwinkle blue (#7b86ff) for active labels, bullet dots and line number 1; the images carry the rest.
look.layout: Three columns: nav with a word ring and news; project index; long project text with margin line numbers 1-20 and vertical 'show' toggles.
look.imagery: Slightly rotated documentation photos with captions: a dark architectural model and a Venice pavilion interior.

behaviour: Vertical 'show: text / images / keywords' toggles recompose the page; nav words ring a circle; jQuery with drag and mouse tracking; hover effects unclear.
signature: The text feels weightless: letters bob on loose baselines while nav words orbit in a ring.
why: The typography enacts the subject (space, gravity) instead of illustrating it; editorial apparatus (line numbers, parentheses, vertical toggles) adds order so the play never costs readability.
steal: Make the type behave like the subject by shifting each glyph's baseline slightly, but keep margins, line numbers and column structure rigid so it stays readable.

title: Virtual Factory — Manchester International Festival
name: Virtual Factory
one_line: Manchester International Festival's online-artworks series: painted, hole-punched metal plates floating on dark green, one per project.

look.type: Graebenbach Regular, a tall neo-grotesk, at viewport-scaled sizes up to 160px with 1.1 leading; small caps labels like 'PRE FACTORY EVENT'.
look.color: Dark green (#0f230a) ground; plates in cream (#ecebe1), orange, brick red, teal and pale lime with painterly texture; mint (#00e7b9) accent.
look.layout: Free-floating die-cut plates over a full-screen dark field; title and project plates with notched corners and drilled holes overlap a video player and tooltips.
look.imagery: Painterly shapes like sheet-metal parts (red fragments, teal slab with holes, yellow wedge); tiny line-drawn figures in white discs.

behaviour: Shapes respond to the cursor (follow, drag), type scales with viewport width, plates open projects, a muted autoplay video, visits remembered in localStorage.
signature: A virtual factory built from die-cut, hole-punched plates in painted colours, floating on dark green.
why: One shape language (notched corners, punched holes) applies to titles, buttons and tooltips, unifying a festival of very different artists' works.
steal: Define one physical-part shape (corner notch plus two drilled holes) and use it for every title card and button, each in a different flat or textured colour.

title: ITZAVIBE 잇자바이브 공식 온라인 스토어
name: ITZAVIBE
one_line: Korean fashion label's store whose entrance splits the screen into KOREA and WORLD WIDE with giant pink-and-black cat renders.

look.type: Pink Edwardian-style script caps ('KOREA', 'WORLD WIDE') with soft glow on the splash; today's shop uses Pretendard and Unbounded.
look.color: Pink-lilac haze and white against jet-black fur, heavy film grain over everything; pink is the only hue.
look.layout: Two full-height halves like a gateway: left KOREA with a giant cat paw, right WORLD WIDE with a black cat on a pink planet.
look.imagery: 3D-rendered black cat paw with glossy pink pads, and a cat sitting on a pink moon planet, grain-textured.

behaviour: Splash asks visitors to choose KOREA or WORLD WIDE (shipping region). The live page is a Cafe24 shop with three.js; the split is not in the static HTML (unclear).
signature: A store entrance split into two huge pink-and-black cat illustrations: choose KOREA or WORLD WIDE.
why: Making the region selector the brand moment turns a chore into a hero image; strict two-colour restraint (black cat, pink everything) keeps it coherent.
steal: Turn region or language selection into a full-screen two-way split with one huge illustration per choice, each labelled in script type.

title: FC-UK
name: FC-UK (No Format)
one_line: A birthday web toy for Eman's 30th: build characters by swapping head, torso and legs from party photos; domain gone.

look.type: Hand-cut ransom-note 'NO FORMAT' logo, chrome 3D 'FC-UK' on a red scribble, a tiny red '??' glyph; no body type.
look.color: White ground; saturated sticker reds, yellows and blues; glossy green arrow buttons with drop shadows; faded sticker faces upper-left.
look.layout: Centred column: logo, then three stacked image strips (head, torso, legs) each flanked by green arrows; ghost stickers drift upper-left; icons at the bottom.
look.imagery: Party photographs cropped into head, torso and leg bands; sticker cut-outs; chrome type; early-2000s clip-art arrows.

behaviour: Click the arrows to swap each band and assemble a person from different photos (an exquisite corpse); the camera icon likely saves it (unclear). Domain no longer resolves.
signature: A birthday exquisite corpse: three arrow-driven slices of party photos reshuffled into new people.
why: Slicing portraits into three independent bands turns a friend group's photos into a toy where every combination is funny; chunky arrow buttons announce the interaction at once.
steal: Cut each photo into head, torso and legs strips and give each strip its own pair of arrow buttons, so visitors compose a person in six clicks.

title: Pissed Pants Academy
name: Pissed Pants Academy (Liby Hays)
one_line: A 'reading machine' by Liby Hays in a shared shell: generative text and sound, MUTE button, plus-shaped clock link.

look.type: Helvetica-style sans at 96px for a tight three-line title; tiny 11px caps for MUTE; 24px body appears as the machine types.
look.color: Gainsboro grey ground (#dcdcdc), with title, MUTE and plus all in dark goldenrod; one hue per piece.
look.layout: Huge title top-left, MUTE top-right, a plus-shaped clock link bottom-right, and an empty field for generated text.
look.imagery: None; the plus sign is two CSS bars that double as clock hands and a link back to the index.

behaviour: Tone.js sound and RiTa text generation type words into the field; MUTE toggles audio; an iframe loads the reading-machines index; what the machine writes is unseen (unclear).
signature: A giant title and a plus-shaped clock in the corner, then silence until the machine starts writing.
why: One colour pair, a huge title and three tiny controls form a tidy shell, so each author's generator defines the work; the template shows how a class can share a frame.
steal: Give a class or collective a shared shell (96px 'Title by Name', tiny MUTE, plus-shaped home link) and let each person choose only two colours.

title: THe Meaning Maker
name: The Meaning Maker (Jorge Palacios)
one_line: A 'reading machine' by Jorge Palacios in the same shell: cornsilk page, olive-green type, generative text and sound.

look.type: Helvetica-style sans at 96px for a two-line title 'The Meaning Maker / by Jorge Palacios'; tiny MUTE caps; plus sign bottom-right.
look.color: Cornsilk (#fff8dc) ground with olive-green type and plus; the same two-colour rule as its siblings.
look.layout: Title flush top-left, MUTE top-right, a plus mark bottom-right and the rest of the screen empty for the machine's output.
look.imagery: None visible in the capture; the plus mark is built from two bars.

behaviour: Same engine as its siblings: Tone.js audio, RiTa text generation typed into the field, MUTE toggle; what it writes is unseen (unclear); iframe loads the index.
signature: A title block over empty cornsilk: the machine's words are the whole event.
why: Cornsilk and olive give the same shell a warmer, paper-like voice than its grey siblings, proof that two colours are enough to make a template personal.
steal: When templating a series, let authors change only background and ink; the colour pair alone will give each piece a distinct personality.

title: SPIRAL
name: SPIRAL (Libby Marrs)
one_line: A 'reading machine' by Libby Marrs in the shared shell: cornflower blue on grey, with a hairline circle at centre.

look.type: Helvetica-style sans at 96px for 'SPIRAL / by Libby Marrs', 18px base size, tiny blue MUTE caps; plus sign bottom-right.
look.color: Gainsboro grey ground with cornflower blue type, plus sign and circle outline; a single hue again.
look.layout: Title top-left, MUTE top-right, a 120px circle outline dead centre as the machine's starting mark, plus bottom-right.
look.imagery: A 1px blue circle in the middle of an empty grey field, presumably the seed of a spiral.

behaviour: Same Tone.js and RiTa shell; the centred circle probably grows or spins into a spiral with sound (unclear). MUTE toggles audio.
signature: One thin blue circle in an empty grey field: a spiral that has not started yet.
why: A single hairline form at centre sets expectation more strongly than any instruction; the shared shell lets the form be the entire content.
steal: Start generative pieces with one hairline primitive at centre and wait for input; the empty screen invites the visitor to act.

name: Sepehr Mokhtarzadeh
one_line: A graphic designer's placeholder page: name, role and links left, a totem of black star, circle and half-moons right.

look.type: Arial-style grotesk ~22px black; name right-aligned beside 'Graphic Designer & Typographer' left-aligned; thick underlines on links.
look.color: Pure black on white; nothing else.
look.layout: Two text columns meeting at a gutter in the left half; a vertical totem of black shapes fills the right half.
look.imagery: Four solid black forms stacked: a tall four-point star, a circle and two stacked half-circle bowls.

behaviour: A single static placeholder page with links to Ello, Twitter, Instagram and Email; the domain no longer resolves.
signature: A holding page that still reads as a finished poster: text on the left, black star, circle and half-moons on the right.
why: Strict black on white plus oversized shapes shows personality without content; heavy 2px underlines make links obvious in a tiny vocabulary.
steal: Make a 'new site coming' page worth keeping: one short text block with thick underlined links and a stack of three or four solid black shapes as your mark.

title: Embassy of Internet
name: Embassy of Internet
one_line: A speculative institution's front page: a blue title block beside a four-row Roman-numeral index of questions and calls.

look.type: Atlas Grotesk caps: ~90px 'EMBASSY OF INTERNET' in pale grey; ~26px blue index rows; ~12px status and date columns.
look.color: Electric blue (#0033ff) title block and index type, olive-grey (#474d3a) panel, light grey (#ddd) ground; a fuzzy blue orb.
look.layout: Left 44%: blue title block over an olive panel with a glowing orb; right: a ruled index of four numbered entries with status and date.
look.imagery: A soft-edged blue radial-gradient sphere on olive; no photographs.

behaviour: React app on a Firebase-style backend (raw HTML says 'Loading...'); entries show Open or Closed status and dates, probably questions and calls collected from visitors.
signature: An institution's front page as a four-row ruled docket: Roman numeral, title, Open/Closed, date, beside a blue orb.
why: Reading the table is the navigation: numerals, status and date make a speculative programme feel like official business; two blues and one grey keep an abstract institution legible.
steal: List programme items as ruled rows (Roman numeral, caps title, status word, date) all in one blue, and give the opposite column a single soft orb.

title: Fotopub
name: Fotopub
one_line: Photo festival whose menu was a poster of flat colour slabs and a black ellipse; domain now hosts casino spam.

look.type: Arial/Helvetica ~22px labels in white or black at the poster edges; 'FOTOPUB' stacked vertically inside the ellipse.
look.color: Flat blocks: cyan #22bbff, coral #ff5b40, indigo #1d0b40, deep green #054a29, black ellipse, yellow pixel blob, on white.
look.layout: Cross-shaped composition: white centre column and four coloured bays (programme top, info left, social right, portfolio review bottom) with corner labels.
look.imagery: Pure geometry: a tall black ellipse, a yellow pixelated blob, a white ellipse; no photographs.

behaviour: Static menu poster with a cookie banner; each block is a nav item. Today the domain serves Slovenian online-casino review pages (hijacked); nothing of the festival remains.
signature: The navigation is a Bauhaus-style poster: flat slabs and an ellipse labelled FOTOPUB, with menu words at the page corners.
why: Abstract shapes in distinct flat colours give each section an identity before you click; corner labels keep the poster usable as a menu.
steal: Build the home page as a poster of flat colour blocks with one organic shape in the centre; put nav words on the blocks and in the corners.
moves: menu items as flat coloured slabs

name: Cul De Sac Studio
one_line: Colin Smight's design and art-direction studio, with shop: all interface text in one red ink on cream.

look.type: Roboto Condensed caps, bold and regular mixed within a paragraph; italic Garamond-style serif ~16px for project text; everything red.
look.color: One red (about #e8221f) for every glyph, rule and icon on cream (#fdfbf6); the artwork supplies all other colour.
look.layout: A 180px left rail with logo and four red icons; main column of project rows split by 1px red rules, text left, large image right.
look.imagery: Brand artwork: a hand-inked 'Lowell' wordmark on lime paper, a blue-and-fluorescent-green puff-ink earth tee.

behaviour: Studio and Shopify shop in one site: Instagram, sound, bag and flower icons; carousel arrows per project; cart drawer; Alpine and jQuery.
signature: One red ink on cream, like a one-colour print, with bold and regular condensed caps flowing together in the intro.
why: Restricting all interface to one ink and two type voices (condensed caps plus italic serif) makes the site feel printed; the artwork stands out because the frame never competes.
steal: Set all interface text in one spot-colour red on cream, alternate bold and regular condensed caps inside one sentence, and use italic serif for descriptions.
moves: bold and regular caps mixed inline

title: bvk
name: bvk (Bhavik Singh)
one_line: An artist-technologist's portfolio: live project windows scattered with hard yellow shadows, plus a button to reshuffle them.

look.type: Old-style serif (Garamond-like) ~24px with italic emphasis on 'Bhavik' and 'Brooklyn'; underlined italic links; tiny sans UI labels.
look.color: Light grey ground; electric yellow (#ffff00) hard offset shadows and control bar; the previews bring blue, mint, magenta.
look.layout: Two-column intro sentence at top, then previews scattered at different sizes and offsets, each framed with a yellow slab shadow.
look.imagery: Live embedded works: kaleidoscope face in a phone frame, avatar windows on blue, a Unity crowd scene, a flower generator.

behaviour: Bio states their local time; previews are live; 'Refresh layout' re-scatters them, FG/BG pickers restyle. Today: cream-and-brown redesign.
signature: A portfolio that tells you what time it is where they live and lets you reshuffle their live projects.
why: Live, playable windows prove the practice better than screenshots; hard yellow shadows and the local-time clause give a small, personal frame to technically varied work.
steal: Put the person's local time inside the bio sentence and give every embedded project the same hard offset colour shadow so a random scatter still reads as a set.
moves: live local time in the bio

title: BOOKSHOP LIBRARY
name: Bookshop Library
one_line: Bangkok CityCity Gallery's bookshop and e-catalogue: three columns, with search facets as soft gradient slabs.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk ~15px thin caps for header UI; 'umpush' display for headings; tiny 12px labels centred on the gradient slabs.
look.color: White UI with black hairlines, airbrushed vertical gradient slabs in orange, pink, lime and blue-grey, and green-grey blur bands around products.
look.layout: Three equal columns under a hairline header: Bookshop, Library, [Bookmark]; the middle column is four stacked slabs: Title, Publisher, Author, Search.
look.imagery: Product prints framed by strong vertical blur bands, and cropped browser screenshots of Thai-language magazine articles.

behaviour: Tri-split catalogue: the four gradient slabs act as catalogue filters; the [BOOKMARK] column shows the gallery's magazine; cart and bookmark counters in the header.
signature: Catalogue search facets as four soft airbrushed colour slabs in the middle of a three-column screen.
why: Filters become big colour fields you could mistake for artworks; each column behaves differently but the shared hairline header keeps three sections in one place.
steal: Turn filter options into tall soft-gradient slabs with one tiny centred label each, stacked in a column between your product and editorial columns.

title: NEARREST NEIGHBOR
name: NEARREST NEIGHBOR
one_line: UCLA Design Media Arts 2020 MFA online thesis show: eleven glowing gel blobs, one per artist, crowding over the title.

look.type: Heavy rounded black-weight sans (Arial Black or Kyiv) in cream at ~110px for the title, half hidden; tiny white 'Info' label bottom-left.
look.color: Pure black ground; cream (#fffdd8) title; periwinkle (#8da2d8) blobs with warm cream radial centres; nothing else.
look.layout: Eleven blob bodies fill the screen around a centred stacked title, overlapping it; nav labels tucked into corners.
look.imagery: Soft-edged, slightly translucent squircle blobs with radial gradients, like glowing gel, one per artist.

behaviour: Each blob presumably opens an artist's thesis; canvas animation with Howler audio; artist names sit in a nav list not shown in the capture; exact motion unclear.
signature: Eleven glowing gel blobs, one per MFA artist, crowd over the exhibition title like cells under a microscope.
why: Each artist is a same-size, same-material body, so nobody outranks anybody; the title showing through the translucent overlaps reinforces the idea of a cluster.
steal: Represent a cohort as equal-sized soft blobs in one gradient material on black, with the title showing through wherever they overlap.
moves: artist names kept in an HTML nav list

title: How Many Plants - Indoor and House Plant Resource
name: How Many Plants
one_line: A houseplant care resource whose hero spells the site name across five illustrated bookshelves with plants growing in front.

look.type: Quirky typewriter-slab display (Hellenic Typewriter) for the logo; Chromatica sans caps for nav and shelf links; huge black geometric letters in the hero.
look.color: Off-white page, mustard-olive shelf linework, black title letters, full-colour plants with pink, orange and blue picture frames.
look.layout: Header with hand-underlined nav; hero of five stacked shelf bands, title broken H-O-W / M-A-N-Y / P-L-A-N-T-S across them, plants overlapping.
look.imagery: Line-drawn shelves, vases, books and frames; painted-style houseplants (pilea, maranta, anthurium) as cut-outs over the lettering.

behaviour: Webflow site; nav items sit on the shelves as book spines and signs; search with suggested terms; a Plant Club banner; staged illustration rather than animation.
signature: The title is spelled out across five bookshelves, with plants in front of the letters and book spines as links.
why: Navigation hides inside the illustration (spines, labels, signs), so the picture is the menu; plants overlapping letters add depth while the mustard linework unifies a crowded scene.
steal: Draw one scene in a single linework colour, set the page title in huge letters inside it, and make the objects (book spines, signs) your nav links.

title: A Website Is A Room
name: A Website Is A Room
one_line: A manifesto about slow, quiet websites beside a visitor-submitted feed of places that feel like rooms.

look.type: Title built from tiny plus-sign dots at 96px; GT Pressura Mono ~15px for manifesto and table; ~11px caps for column headers.
look.color: Honeydew (#f0fff0) page with sage links and rules (#96b396, #d8e6d8) and near-black (#3c403c) ink; quiet green only.
look.layout: Left column manifesto with staircase-indented lines; right, a four-column table (description, location, contributor, timestamp) split by vertical hairlines.
look.imagery: None; the title and a dashed arrow ('----->') are drawn from characters.

behaviour: Live feed: visitors submit a site, description and handle through a form; entries list newest first from a spreadsheet; lost data was restored from the Wayback Machine in 2025.
signature: A site about websites that feel like rooms, whose contents are submitted by visitors in a plain mono table.
why: A plain table, steady mono type and pale green keep the focus on visitors' descriptions; the poem's staircase indent slows reading, matching the theme of slowness and quiet.
steal: Write your manifesto with progressively indented lines to make a staircase, then let visitors add rows to an unstyled mono table beside it.
moves: dashed arrow pointing at the feed

title: Haiku-Haiku
name: Haiku-Haiku
one_line: Collaborative haiku writing: strangers add one line each to frosted-glass blob cards under a wordmark that bleeds off the page.

look.type: Huge light grotesk 'HaikuHaiku' (~190px, tight) in pale grey, cropped by the top edge; Mincho-style serif ~18px for haiku; 24px status lines.
look.color: Gradient from crimson through vermilion to khaki; light grey and translucent white type and cards; no solid colour blocks.
look.layout: Giant wordmark; two columns of frosted blob cards for unfinished haiku on the left, one huge completed card right; pill buttons fixed bottom-left.
look.imagery: No images; irregular squircle and circle shapes with notched corners, made of frosted glass.

behaviour: Realtime shared writing: add a line to an unfinished haiku; three authors complete one; counters show authors online and completed haiku (189); Gatsby with page transitions.
signature: Each haiku is a frosted-glass blob that three strangers complete line by line.
why: A tiny rule (one line per person) plus a soft glass material makes collaboration visible; a different blob outline per card makes the page feel grown, not templated.
steal: Give user-generated cards frosted translucent fills over a warm gradient with a different blob outline per card, and cap what each person can add at one line.

title: 3C ⁠✧ 324
name: 3C (ISO Radio)
one_line: ISO Radio's collection of 8 mixes, 8 artworks and 8 essays, indexed on a pastel month calendar.

look.type: Airbrushed chrome-blue stretched wordmark; tiny mono calendar numerals; weekday headers in stylistic-alternate glyphs; ~12px sans in the player strip.
look.color: Lavender (#e2ddff) ground that changes among pale mint and sky pastels; thin dark outlines; artworks and a red star-field card bring saturation.
look.layout: A month calendar of rounded boxes; filled days hold artworks; a player strip with mix title and mood tags top-right; a card overlaps the grid.
look.imagery: Botanical line drawing, collage, red star-field plate, DJ photo, illustrated figures, each sitting in a calendar day.

behaviour: Eight days hold mixes with artwork and writing; a player strip names the mix and its mood tags; favicon and tab title animate; the page ground changes per mix.
signature: A month calendar where eight days hold radio mixes, each opening an artwork, a mix and an essay.
why: A calendar index makes a small collection feel like a season, and mostly empty days make the filled ones feel like events.
steal: Index a small set of releases on a month calendar of rounded boxes, leave most days empty, and show thumbnail art only on days with content.
moves: mood tag pills in the player

title: Brooklyn Art Book Fair
name: Brooklyn Art Book Fair
one_line: Annual art-book fair; the 2022 homepage was a salmon-pink poster with a white scribble fairy.

look.type: Light grotesk (Standard) ~105px white caps in three tight lines; ~24px sentence-case details with an underlined call to action.
look.color: Salmon pink (#ff8b8b) field with white type and white line art, nothing else.
look.layout: Poster-like single screen: title top-left, drawing bottom-right, two short detail columns bottom-left, a tiny asterisk bottom-right corner.
look.imagery: A white marker-line drawing of a winged fairy holding a magic wand-book, with sparkles.

behaviour: Static announcement for 2022; today's WordPress and Gatsby site carries 2026 dates (10-12 July) in a new orange and cyan identity.
signature: One white scribble of a book-wielding fairy on pink says 'art book fair' better than any photo.
why: One drawing, one colour and one headline turn an application notice into a poster; the call to action stays plain, underlined text, so it is still findable.
steal: Make an annual event's landing page a poster: one saturated field, one hand-drawn white figure, a 100px light caps title and a two-column details block.

title: The Town | Volvox Vault
name: The Town (Volvox Vault)
one_line: A community's front door as a town map of six emoji places; the site now fails with an SSL error.

look.type: Courier-like typewriter mono ~13px, grey, lowercase captions under each emoji; 'welcome to the town.' top-left.
look.color: Light grey (#e4e4e4) ground, dark grey type, and only the native colours of six emoji.
look.layout: A sparse map: six emoji landmarks scattered across a grey field with wide gaps; greeting top-left.
look.imagery: Apple-style emoji (airport, cafe, park, theatre, pond, community centre) used as map pins.

behaviour: Each landmark presumably links to an area of the community (events, chat, gallery); the live page did not load with an SSL error, so unclear.
signature: A whole community laid out as a town map of six emoji and lowercase labels.
why: Navigation as geography: with six places and generous space, wayfinding is memorable, and emoji give instant meaning without designing icons.
steal: Replace your menu with a map of five to seven emoji places scattered unevenly on a grey field, each with a lowercase mono caption.

title: Frontpage
name: Sternberg Press
one_line: An art-book publisher whose catalogue view is a 3D cloud of covers tumbling at every angle on pale grey.

look.type: Sainte Colombe serif ~25px for the logo (italic with a star) and 'Books'; Proto sans for UI and catalogue lists.
look.color: Pale grey (#d8d8d8) ground in the cloud view; the covers' reds, yellows, mints and blacks are the only colour.
look.layout: Full-bleed field of about 25 covers hanging at random 3D angles; slim header with 'Books' left, centred logo and a close mark right.
look.imagery: Book covers photographed flat, each rotated in three dimensions and overlapping like pages thrown in the air.

behaviour: A three.js/WebGL cloud of covers (shader and audio libraries bundled); clicking a cover presumably opens its record (bookId in the URL); classic WordPress shop below with cart.
signature: The whole catalogue as a swirl of 3D book covers drifting at every angle against pale grey.
why: A publisher's identity lives in its covers; showing many at once shows range at a glance, while the quiet serif header stays out of their way.
steal: Let the product images be the home page: put them in a navigable 3D cloud on pale grey with only a thin serif header and a close mark.
moves: close mark to exit to catalogue

title: Homepage - DICE Conference + Festival, Berlin
name: DICE Conference + Festival
one_line: Berlin music-and-discourse festival: giant mint letters D-I-C-E staggered like dice with a translucent 3D ribbon twisting through; now an archive.

look.type: Jost (Futura-like) geometric sans: ~340px mint DICE letters; 14px caps nav; today's page uses 18px body and an artist-name list.
look.color: Cream (#eeebdc) ground, mint (#5dd4ac) letters, a translucent darker green (#3a9e7c) form, dark green ink (#1f3d33).
look.layout: Four letters staggered in a zig-zag at the page centre with a 3D form over them; five-item nav top-right.
look.imagery: A glossy translucent mint twisted-ribbon 3D form overlapping the lettering; no photographs.

behaviour: 2021 edition: the translucent form probably turns (unclear). Today: a static hiatus notice, 'SWIPE' prompt and a scroll-snap list of past artists (82 items).
signature: Giant mint letters staggered like dice, with a translucent 3D ribbon twisting through them.
why: Overlap of translucent form and letters creates depth from two greens; staggered letter positions give a static logo kinetic energy.
steal: Stagger the letters of the event name in a zig-zag in one pastel hue, and run one translucent 3D shape in the same hue through them.

title: DADA PROJECTS
name: Dada Projects
one_line: Female-led 3D design studio showing work as glassy pebble-shaped tiles under a swash-serif wordmark.

look.type: Romie swash display serif for 'DADA' with curly ligatures, light Diatype caps for 'PROJECTS', both ~100px; 14-24px small text.
look.color: White ground; all colour comes from the CGI work: oxblood, chrome blue-black, root brown, pink.
look.layout: Wordmark across the top; below, rounded rectangles, circles and discs of varied sizes overlap in a collage; a round '...' menu button top-right.

look.color: White ground; all colour comes from the drawing: pink, cobalt, leopard print, lime, silver.
look.layout: Logo and a three-item nav stacked top-left; one artwork centred in a huge white field, about 420px of the 1000px screen.
look.imagery: Dense coloured-pencil illustration: ghost clock, blue moon mirror, flowers, patterned limbs, cut out on white.

behaviour: Cargo template: Work expands with a plus sign into a project list; no custom motion seen. Today the nav reads About and Shop.
signature: One dense pencil drawing floats alone in vast white space under a marker-written name.
why: Extreme emptiness makes one detailed drawing feel precious, and the handwritten wordmark ties the interface to the artist's hand so the template recedes.
steal: Write your name in your own handwriting top-left, keep the nav to three small grotesk words, and show one work at a time in a lot of white.
moves: one artwork centred with huge margins
Work (+) expander in a tiny nav

title: GOODZONES
name: GOODZONES
one_line: Shop whose navigation was seven empty bordered squares under a fake address bar, labelled like library call numbers.

look.type: Helvetica-like grotesk: bold caps about 11px for the URL bar and nav, 15px caps tile labels, a heavy rounded lowercase logo.
look.color: White page and one deep forest green for every line, border, letter and logo; no other colour.
look.layout: Top bar of 1px rules, a green logo, then seven 180px square tiles in rows of four, each labelled top-left.
look.imagery: None in the capture: outlined empty tiles, a broken-image icon beside the URL.

behaviour: Shopify store, now shut (Store unavailable). Tiles are nav links (Shop, Search, Product Reviews, GZ Weekly, _Directory); cart reads BAG (00); search is a bordered field.
signature: Navigation as empty 1px squares with catalogue-number labels such as 746.9/2020.12.011, under a faux browser bar.
why: The wireframe-like UI makes the shop feel like a catalogue; call-number labels and a zero-padded bag counter add archival seriousness, and one green keeps it from feeling cold.
steal: Use one ink colour and 1px outlines only; label tiles with catalogue-style numbers and show the URL as a fake address bar for an index-card feel.

title: Notes from the Field - Home
name: Notes from the Field
one_line: Online project portrait of an alpine village: dithered halftone photo, pill-shaped title, lead paragraph in huge serif.

look.type: Light grotesk caps about 50px in the pill title; Times NRMT serif about 36px for the lead; Diatype Pre buttons; 11px mono ticker.
look.color: Black-and-white halftone photo on white, black text, white pill buttons with a soft shadow; one cyan accent (#00b3ff) in the CSS.
look.layout: Top ticker, full-width photo with a caption row (credit left, Img. 02 of 44 right), serif lead below, fixed Explore pill at the bottom.
look.imagery: 1-bit dithered photograph of an observation hut (Philip Samartzis, Bogong High Plains, 2020); 44 images in the set.

behaviour: Fixed Explore pill slides off after exploring and scrolling; localStorage, custom cursor, intersection observers, a full-screen video player; land acknowledgement runs as a ticker.
signature: A dithered halftone photograph with a white pill-shaped title overlapping its top edge, then serif text bigger than most headlines.
why: Dithering unifies 44 photographs and keeps them light to load; one soft pill shape set against hard bitmap pixels is memorable, and oversize serif text makes the prose the main event.
steal: Dither every photograph to 1-bit, overlay a white pill-shaped title and CTA with a soft shadow, and set the lead text above 30px.
moves: Img. 02 of 44 counter in the caption row

title: Habitats
name: Companion Platform - Habitats
one_line: Page of habitat definitions as a grid of soft rounded cells, with blurred macro photographs mixed in.

look.type: A friendly humanist sans about 15px in dark olive, centred at the top of each cell; no headings.
look.color: Mud-brown ground, sage-green cells, one cream-lime cell for the definition; photos add saturated yellow, pink and blue.
look.layout: Five-column grid of equal squircle cells about 195 by 155px with big corner radii; photos occupy scattered cells.
look.imagery: Out-of-focus macro photos (yellow flower, blue insect, moss, pink bloom) as soft blurred squares inside the grid.

behaviour: Probably hover or click sharpens a blurred photo and opens the entry (unclear). Webflow page now returns 404 Page not found.
signature: A grid of soft habitat cells in which some cells are blurred photographs, as if specimens sit just out of focus.
why: Squircle cells make a taxonomy feel organic rather than tabular, and blurred photo cells hint at hidden content that needs attention to resolve, so looking becomes the interaction.
steal: Lay out a taxonomy as equal rounded cells, drop a few blurred image cells among them, and sharpen them on hover so discovery is the interface.
moves: squircle cells as a taxonomy grid
blurred photo cells among text cells
earth-tone palette of mud, moss and cream

title: I Heard It In A Magazine
name: I Heard It In A Magazine (Hii)
one_line: Sound-culture magazine archive as a wall of flat colour tiles sized by headline length, one hue per category.

look.type: Rounded humanist grotesk about 13px in black: title top-left, grey date top-right, tiny caps category tag bottom-left in every tile.
look.color: Eight flat saturated fills - hot pink, lime, tomato, violet, cyan-blue, yellow, mint, tangerine - one per category; text always black.
look.layout: Justified rows of rectangular tiles whose widths follow title length, each row filling the width; fixed audio player bar at the bottom.
look.imagery: None; the colour tile is the thumbnail.

behaviour: React and Three.js app: tile wall by date, fixed player bar with gradient waveform strip and transport controls, settings and support icons. The live page shows only an empty shell.
signature: A brick wall of flat colour tiles where width follows headline length and hue means category.
why: Colour as category and width as content length make the archive scannable without images; packed rows feel like a brick wall of topics, with date and tag always in the same corners.
steal: Give each category one flat hue, size each tile by its headline length, pack rows edge to edge, and put date and tag in fixed corners.
moves: date top-right and tag bottom-left in every tile

title: untold stories
name: untold stories
one_line: Political design studio portfolio as a sideways row of full-height columns, each project in its own flat colour.

look.type: Times-like serif headlines about 38px centred, Courier New 14px for subtitles and notes, Times 16px body with footnote superscripts.
look.color: Each column a flat ground: sunflower yellow, white with red type, mint, pale grey; text black or red; hot pink (#ff0087) elsewhere.
look.layout: Horizontal row of full-height columns about 258px wide, one project each, scrolling sideways; slim top bar with home, arrows and title.
look.imagery: Press photos, protest posters, a Scrooge McDuck riff on the I amsterdam logo, a hand-drawn graph grid, simple illustrations.

behaviour: Cargo site: sideways scroll with arrow buttons in the top bar; each column holds a full case study with footnotes; 27 articles and about 35k words on one page.
signature: Each political design project is its own full-height coloured column, set like a newspaper column in Times and Courier.
why: One column per project gives each campaign its own palette and voice while the shared type pair holds the set together; reading becomes a horizontal sweep through a print-like page.
steal: Make each project a full-height narrow column with its own flat colour and the same two typefaces, and let the page scroll sideways.
moves: arrow navigation in the top bar

title: Dexter Edwards
name: Dexter Edwards
one_line: A typewriter-set bio listing only collaborations, beside one crude paint-program flower and four soft colour glows.

look.type: Monospaced typewriter face about 13px in dark grey, top-left, no hierarchy; today Times New Roman 20px.
look.color: White ground; soft yellow glows left and right, pale blue above and below; a yellow flower with orange centre and green stem.
look.layout: Small text block pinned top-left; the rest of the screen is one centred flower over four blurred blobs in a cross.
look.imagery: A deliberately crude MS-Paint-style flower, flanked by Gaussian-blurred colour orbs.

behaviour: 2019 capture appears static. Today: Times text, a French-flag gradient text class, and fixed butterfly elements whose wings flap (rotateY keyframes) via butterflies.js.
signature: A bio that lists projects only as X with Y, next to one clumsy hand-drawn flower.
why: Naming work only as project-with-collaborator foregrounds relationships, and Portfolio on Request swaps a gallery for a conversation; the childlike flower makes the restraint feel warm, not withholding.
steal: Replace your portfolio grid with a plain list of projects written X with Y and an email address, and keep one naive drawing as the only image.
moves: projects listed as X with Y
Portfolio on Request instead of a gallery

title: Dandelion Cafe
name: Dandelion Cafe
one_line: Pop-up anti-coffee shop page: a hand-lettered blue-ink poster above a plain how-to for dandelion coffee and solar cookers.

look.type: Times New Roman at browser default (about 13px), bold section heads over 2px rules, default blue underlined links; hand-printed ink lettering in the poster.
look.color: White page, black text, default link blue (#0000ee); one royal-blue ink drawing.
look.layout: One full-width text column with no max-width, so lines run about 1000px; centred poster image on top; ruled headings between sections.
look.imagery: One hand-lettered poster: a dandelion on a zigzag boat, the event name, dates and URL.

behaviour: Static HTML document with links to a zine PDF, assembly instructions, solar-cooker plans and a reading list; the.tk domain no longer resolves.
signature: A blue-ink hand-lettered poster sitting on an unstyled how-to for running your own dandelion-coffee cafe.
why: The unstyled page is honest DIY: the content is instructions for others to copy, so nothing needs to impress, and the single hand-drawn poster supplies all the personality.
steal: If your project is a how-to, publish it as plain HTML with ruled headings and a printable zine link, and put one drawn poster on top.
moves: link list of instructions and readings

title: BAD STUDIO
name: BAD STUDIO (Bráulio Amado)

look.color: Flat mid-grey ground (about #c8c8ca) with black text; today white with orange, green and red flashes.

signature: The whole portfolio is one sentence of text links, with a doodle standing in for the @ sign.
why: Making the bio the interface removes chrome: each underlined phrase is a category link inside running prose, and the doodle @ adds character without leaving the sentence.
steal: Write one sentence about what you make, set it at 40px+, underline each noun that links to a section, and swap one glyph for a doodle.
moves: bio paragraph as the whole nav
doodle glyph replacing @ in the email

title: AAAAN.NET
name: AAAAN.NET
one_line: Curator-researcher's archive: raw checkbox filters above a wall of text cards, each in a randomly chosen font, border and fill.

signature: Raw HTML checkboxes serve as the filter UI above a wall of text cards, each dressed in its own font, border and fill.
why: Exposing the taxonomy as unstyled checkboxes is honest and fast, while randomised card styling gives a sprawling research archive many voices without needing images.
steal: Show your tags as plain checkboxes in a mono face, then give each result card a randomly assigned font, border and fill from a short list.
moves: random per-card font, border and fill
Twitter feed as a grey card

title: Kaitlyn Chai
name: Kaitlyn Chai

signature: Navigation as a matching game: drag the illustrated object into its empty outline to open that section.
why: A matching game gives visitors a reason to explore and makes categories memorable; outline-only silhouettes are clear affordances, and everything else stays flat and legible.
steal: Draw each category as an object plus an empty outline of that object, and make visitors drag the object into its outline to enter.

instruction as a hand-drawn arrow note
flat vector props with black outlines

title: sues-space.herokuapp.com

look.imagery: Casual selfie portraits (tongue out, silver mask) and an upside-down cat, each clipped to a different organic mask.

signature: Faces clipped into wobbly blobs, lit like objects against pure black, with no text at all.
why: The blob mask turns ordinary snapshots into small creatures, and the empty black ground makes each face a lit object; with no text, the page is purely about presence.
steal: Clip every portrait to a different irregular blob and float them on pure black with no text, so the faces read as characters.

title: sue roh
name: sue roh

signature: A retro desktop in mauve: their 3D-scanned face in a window, a smiley face on the Start button.
why: Familiar OS chrome gives instant orientation, and changing the colours, icons and Start glyph keeps it personal; a working tray clock sells the illusion of a running machine.
steal: If you use an OS metaphor, retheme it: change the title-bar colour, draw your own icons, put a face on Start, wire a real clock into the tray.

title: Post-Radical Pedagogy
name: Post-Radical Pedagogy
one_line: Program statement in giant italic serif running across two tilted neon-pastel gradient slabs.

look.type: Times-style italic serif about 40px in dark grey for the statement; a tiny bold mono wordmark (Inconsolata) about 11px at top left.
look.color: Off-white ground; one slab runs lime to pink to mint, another sky blue to orange to pink; text stays dark grey across all of it.
look.layout: Single text column about 750px wide; two rotated rectangles (about 2 degrees) sit behind the text and bleed off the right edge.
look.imagery: No images; the rotated gradient slabs are the pictures.

signature: Giant italic serif text crosses tilted neon-pastel slabs and the white gaps between them without changing colour.
why: Text that ignores colour boundaries makes the colour read as light behind the page; the slight tilt breaks the grid and signals a pedagogy that resists institutional order.
steal: Set your statement at 40px italic serif and put two or three rotated gradient rectangles behind it, ignoring where the paragraphs break.

tiny mono wordmark in the corner
one dark grey text colour across all grounds

title: Touchy Coffee
name: Touchy Coffee

why: Soft, swollen lettering says touch directly; rigid tracked mono caps and pill buttons contrast with it so the wordmark feels even softer, and flat colour fields help tell products apart.
steal: Run your story as a single-line mono-caps ticker along the bottom, and make the logo the only soft, hand-drawn shape on a flat colour page.

pill buttons in the top corners
joke message in place of a phone layout

why: Solid circle markers are easier to see and tap than superscripts and echo the black menu button; setting pull quotes in the mono companion face and hanging them out of the column adds rhythm to long text.
steal: Mark footnotes with small solid black circles holding white numerals, and set pull quotes in the mono companion face, hanging into the margin.

title: Smack dat ass

why: Mixing five lettering styles in one name is a collage of internet-era text effects; the bland cream gradient and pixel-font ENTER keep the joke deadpan.

steal: Run your instruction line as a header marquee (Click anywhere to start) and make the title one glossy rendered object on near-white.

instruction text as a top marquee
near-white sky ground with a faint rainbow

title: Moving Parts

steal: Build your landing page from the product's own UI parts: headline in a chat bubble, signup as a real input, so the page demos itself.

title: La luce alpina

hover a section to unblur its image
