title: Vivien Sansour
name: Vivien Sansour
one_line: Artist and seed-library site: cut-out project photos laid over colossal black letter fragments, with lime-green captions.

look.type: Heavy Roboto-like bold caps about 34px in lime green, right-aligned stacked captions; condensed grotesk caps about 15px for nav; bold condensed wordmark about 22px.
look.color: White ground with solid black letter shapes; lime-green (about #2ab721) captions; photographs add pale blue-green leaves, wood brown, pink sticky notes.
look.layout: Staggered two-column placement of cut-out photos with captions, overlapping giant black glyph shapes that bleed off the viewport; thin nav bar on top.
look.imagery: Cut-out photographs: melon leaves, a mobile wooden kitchen with a cook, seeds and pink post-its, farmers holding wheat.

behaviour: Cargo site; project captions (Traveling Kitchen, Palestine Heirloom Seed Library, Exhibitions Performances Publications) presumably link out. Today it shows This site is private.
signature: Cut-out photos sit on enormous black letter fragments, each captioned in lime-green caps.
why: Gigantic black shapes give weight and structure without a grid; a saturated mid-tone caption colour works over both black and white (weaker on white).
steal: Put giant black type shapes behind cut-out photos as a structural backdrop, and pick one vivid mid-tone label colour; check it against the white ground.
moves: giant black glyph fragments as the backdrop
one lime caption colour across black and white grounds

title: effydigiworld
name: effydigiworld
one_line: Artist site whose project menu is six unlabelled objects in different media on a soft grey gradient.

look.type: Bold humanist sans (Social variable) about 17px for the Hi :P greeting and about link; no headings; tiny icon pairs in the bottom corners.
look.color: Cool grey vertical gradient (about #b9c1c8 to #d3d3d3); objects add pink, cream, blue-green marble, black and soft blue.
look.layout: Two rows of three objects centred in the upper half, empty gradient below, greeting top-left, about top-right, icon pairs in the lower corners.
look.imagery: Illustrated wooden cube, circle-line logo, 3D marble sheet, chunky black glyph, scanned grey crumple with tape, pink dotted card.

behaviour: Cargo site with a custom cursor image; the objects presumably open sketches and other projects (unclear); corner icons for smile, flower, phone and web.
signature: Six wordless objects in six different media stand in for a project menu.
why: Unlabelled objects in different media make the menu a small puzzle and a sample of the practice at once; the quiet gradient lets each object keep its own lighting.
steal: Replace thumbnails with six objects from your practice in six different media, no captions, on a flat gradient; let the objects be the menu.
moves: icon pairs in the bottom corners
greeting used as a nav label

title: Metis Foundry
name: Metis Foundry
one_line: Type foundry home as stacked full-width bands, one typeface per band, each with specimen, three sliders and a price pill.

look.type: Helvetica about 20px for UI; each band's specimen in its own face (contour LXII Display, blocky Geometer, MF Doom); price in a rounded pill button.
look.color: A different ground per band: iridescent pink-lime-mint mesh, flat cobalt blue (about #2072be), olive gold; dark grey type; beige price pills.
look.layout: Full-width bands about 480px tall: name top-left, specimen centred, three slider lines, More information left, Buy Now right.
look.imagery: Specimens only; the first band's backdrop is a blurred gradient mesh of colour shapes.

behaviour: Three horizontal slider lines with dots per band (axes or sample controls, unclear); Swiper and typed effects in the JS; WordPress with styled scrollbars; Buy Now pills with prices.
signature: Each typeface lives in its own colour band with three sliders, so every specimen feels like a small instrument with a price on it.
why: One identical module per typeface (name, specimen, three sliders, info link, price) makes the catalogue skimmable, while per-band colour gives each face a mood without a new layout.
steal: Make one identical specimen band per typeface (name, live sample, three sliders, info link, price pill) and change only the ground colour.
moves: iridescent gradient mesh behind a contour face

title: Transmediale for refusal
name: transmediale - for refusal
one_line: Festival site where blurred forest video sits under neon-mint blob controls with feathered edges.

look.type: Pale-white light sans wordmark about 20px; Menu in black about 14px inside a pill; today system sans at 11-15px.
look.color: Desaturated overcast photo (cream, grey, brown trees) with neon mint-green (about #14f58a) blobs; today cyan #00bbff, orange #ff4f0e and white.
look.layout: Full-bleed blurred video still; feathered Menu pill and a dot top-left, wordmark beside them, one mint blob with a black pictogram bottom-right.
look.imagery: Out-of-focus, motion-smeared footage of bare trees under a flat overcast sky.

behaviour: 2021 for refusal skin: blurred blob controls over a video backdrop (likely interactive, unclear). Today a SvelteKit site with feed, festival, residency, journal and shop, in a cyan-and-orange identity.
signature: Interface controls drawn as blurry neon-mint blobs over an equally blurred forest video.
why: Blurring both picture and controls makes the whole screen feel withheld, matching the refusal theme, while one neon hue keeps the few controls findable.
steal: Apply the same blur to your interface shapes as to your background so they read as part of the picture, and keep one neon hue for controls.
moves: one neon mint accent on a desaturated video

title: mmm
name: mmm
one_line: Free-form page builder whose homepage is itself an editor: drag stickers, GIFs and video around a paper-white sheet.

look.type: Giant bold high-contrast serif mmm about 190px; Courier for tips and credits about 14px; light sans headline about 30px; typewriter hint text.
look.color: White sheet on white ground with pastel blobs (lavender, pink), yellow highlighter, teal paint swipe, beige scribble; stickers supply the saturation.
look.layout: Centred paper column about 620px with hairline edges; stickers and tip text overflow on both sides; floating editor toolbar top-left.
look.imagery: Stickers and GIFs: goggled rat, astronaut, Arthur cartoon, isometric HELLO lettering, a printer photo, a YouTube embed, marker scribbles.

behaviour: The landing page is the editor: elements drag, resize, rotate, undo and delete; sign-in top-right. Heavy SPA (3.8 MB JS); the live page shows only a shell.
signature: The homepage is a live page-builder: a handwritten note says try moving any of these, and every sticker drags.
why: Letting visitors manipulate the landing page proves the product in seconds; stickers on a white sheet set expectations for what users will make, and handwritten prompts lower the barrier to play.
steal: Make the landing page a working demo of the editor, with a handwritten try-moving-any-of-these note beside a few draggable stickers.
moves: landing page is a working editor
floating toolbar with text, video, image, undo

title: Chicago Architecture Biennial
name: Chicago Architecture Biennial
one_line: Biennial homepage: a heavy black four-line title interlocked with hairline outlined tiles on sage green.

look.type: Heavy extended grotesk caps about 170px for the title, tight leading; bold small-caps nav about 12px in a boxed bar; light sans in the footer.
look.color: Sage green (about #85b99b) ground with black type, black hairlines and black sponsor logos; no other colour.
look.layout: Full-viewport poster: boxed nav top-left, four-line title filling the width, date line, footer bar with sponsor row and slide ticker.
look.imagery: Black hairline outlines of overlapping rounded tiles with notched corners, like building plans or brickwork, behind and through the letters.

behaviour: WordPress: footer features ticker with 1/2 arrows, skip-to-content link, reduced-motion rules. Today the same site shows the 2025 SHIFT biennial instead of this 2019 poster.
signature: The title letters interlock with hairline-outlined brick tiles that notch into them.
why: One tile system drawn from the subject (masonry, plans) evokes architecture directly, and overlapping the type makes the title feel constructed rather than placed; two colours make it unmistakable.
steal: Draw an outline tile system from your subject (bricks, plans) and let it overlap and notch your poster title so the type seems built from it.
moves: outlined tile pattern interlocking with the title
boxed nav bar with a logo cell
sponsor logo strip in the footer

title: PACKET
name: PACKET
one_line: Art-magazine site that announces things in yellow hard-shadowed popup windows over huge Helvetica Bold headlines.

look.type: Helvetica Bold with tight negative tracking about 85px for the headline, cropped by the viewport edge; 12-24px Helvetica elsewhere; coloured words in popups.
look.color: White page, black scan frames, hard yellow (about #ffee00) UI, red close dots; popup words in pink, green, orange and blue.
look.layout: Two wide issue spreads on black, a right rail of eight narrow cover thumbnails, floating popups and a subscribe widget overlapping the content.
look.imagery: Scans of printed magazine spreads on black backgrounds; cover thumbnails with hard offset shadows.

behaviour: Tumblr-based theme: yellow popups with red x close buttons, subscribe form (6 issues $24), search, issue and artist filters, Follow and Email pills fixed bottom-right.
signature: Yellow bevelled popups with red close dots float over giant Helvetica headlines, like pop-up ads for an art magazine.
why: The pop-up ad vernacular turns announcements into physical objects with hard shadows, readable over any content; scans on black make the spreads look like lightbox slides.
steal: Make announcements small yellow windows with a hard offset shadow and a red close dot instead of a banner, and crop your headline at the viewport edge.
moves: yellow popup windows with red close dots
headline cropped by the viewport edge

title: Digital Animsim
name: Digital Animism
one_line: SMS-based environmental project explained in a rebus paragraph where small icons replace the nouns.

look.type: Arial/Helvetica-style sans about 38px black for the intro, about 28px for the how-to list; inline icon images set at text height.
look.color: White ground, black text; icons bring a red heart, rainbow arrows, blue globe, orange cone and a green dotted circular badge.
look.layout: One left-aligned text column about 900px wide with generous leading; a rotated circular text badge at top-right overlaps the paragraph.
look.imagery: Flat emoji-like icons (heart, globe, eye, book, sunrise, cone, hazard diamond) inline in sentences; a text-on-circle DIGITAL ANIMISM badge.

behaviour: Static page explaining an SMS service: text the project and receive a daily message about local environments (sidewalks, ozone, blossoms, wind). One icon is a broken image. Domain now dead.
signature: A rebus paragraph: icons replace the nouns (heart, globe, eye, sunrise, traffic cone) inside the project description.
why: Icons at text size slow the eye and make each noun an object to look at; plain sans lets the icons carry the personality, and the SMS instructions sit directly below so understanding leads to action.
steal: Swap the nouns in your intro for small icons at text height, then give the action steps in the same paragraph style right below.
moves: broken image icon left in place

name: PC Music (2020 capture)
one_line: Earlier capture of the PC Music splash: white condensed-serif logotype on pure blue, footer links below.

look.type: Same tall condensed serif wordmark about 250px; here the footer renders in Arial/Helvetica: 9px tracked caps tagline, 17px Catalogue Contact Merch.
look.color: Full-bleed #0000ff blue and white only; the two-colour rule holds from the 2017 splash to today's catalogue page.
look.layout: Centred logotype, with LONDON-BASED RECORD LABEL, three links, five social icons and a 2017 copyright stacked at the bottom centre.
look.imagery: Logotype only: a quaver as the P, a zig-zag ribbon as the last letter.

behaviour: Static splash in this capture; today the page lists about 150 Bandcamp releases with a newsletter dialog (SvelteKit), still blue with white text at 12px.
signature: A label that is one white logotype on one blue field, unchanged in look for years.
why: Holding one colour and one logo constant across years builds recognition faster than any layout change; the tiny footer keeps all utility out of the way of the mark.
steal: Make your homepage one logotype on one flat colour, push every link into a tiny footer cluster, and resist redesigning it.
moves: one logotype on one flat colour
footer cluster as the only navigation

title: Chimeric Worlding
name: Chimeric Worlding
one_line: Thesis essay on graphic design, poetics and world-building, shown as two scrolling panes split by a draggable circle.

look.type: Arial-like sans at 80px with -4px tracking: caps title, italic subtitle, underlined author; Menlo mono in the left pane at 16px.
look.color: Olive (#808000) text and 1.5px rules on gainsboro (#dcdcdc); links flip to pure blue on hover; images multiply into the grey.
look.layout: Two full-height panes split 50/50 by a hairline; a 25px outlined circle at dead centre is the handle; panes scroll separately, scrollbars hidden.
look.imagery: None on first screen; later images use mix-blend-mode multiply so their white backgrounds vanish into the ground.

behaviour: Drag the circle to resize the panes (cursor grab, olive fill on hover); markdown-it renders the essay; Tone.js and RiTa libraries are loaded for sound and text play; 0.25s easing.
signature: A 25px outlined circle on a hairline: the entire interface is one draggable handle between two panes.
why: Placing the only control at the exact centre of a bare screen makes the reader's first action the essay's theme, moving a boundary between two things. Two colours and one rule carry the identity.
steal: Replace the nav with one draggable handle on a 1.5px divider; give hover a single colour flip (olive to blue) and multiply-blend images into the ground colour.
moves: draggable divider circle as the only control
olive on gainsboro, two colours total

title: Rachel Kim
name: Rachel Kim
one_line: Designer's portfolio set inside a glass-egg crystal ball with calligraphic category headings and sparkles; project titles are the menu.

look.type: Monsieur La Doulaise copperplate script at about 50px for numbered category headings, overlapping each other; a neutral 20px sans for project names.
look.color: White ground, grey-glass egg, one electric-violet plasma burst, black four-point sparkles; otherwise monochrome.
look.layout: Egg centred; project lists flank it left and right; headings staggered diagonally, and '3. Animation' collides with '5. Art & craft'.
look.imagery: Photoreal glass egg on a plinth hanging from a ring, purple lightning flare, scattered sparkle glyphs; 85 images behind.

behaviour: Loading screen first; a custom cursor element follows the pointer; swup handles page transitions; project titles open Vimeo or Giphy iframes (27 embeds).
signature: A giant glass egg with a lightning ball inside is the background of a table of contents.
why: One hyper-real object gives the portfolio a world to live in, while plain sans lists keep every project a visible link; the script headings carry the personality so decoration never blocks navigation.
steal: Put one oversized photoreal object behind a text-only contents list, set category headings in a script face, and keep the list items in a neutral 20px sans.
moves: script category headings that overlap on purpose
project titles are the whole nav

title: Shared Space
name: Shared Space
one_line: A browser scene in a thin frame: a WebGL field of false-colour grass you move through by scrolling and clicking.

look.type: 12px monospace only: two tiny captions under the frame, 'movement' bottom-left and 'scroll up/down, click' bottom-right.
look.color: White page, 1px black frame, acid-yellow sky over saturated greens; no interface colour at all.
look.layout: One square frame inset about 50px from the viewport edge, filling the screen; captions sit just below it.
look.imagery: Real-time rendered grass blades in flat high-saturation false colour with a yellow sky fill.

behaviour: Three.js and Pixi WebGL with shaders and Web Audio; scroll and click move you. Firebase and localStorage are present, so shared state between visitors is possible but unclear.
signature: The whole page is a 1px-framed window onto acid-green grass with two lines of instruction.
why: Two corner captions explain the action without any UI, so the scene is the interface; the plain white margin makes the saturated image read as a framed object.
steal: Frame your hero experience as one bordered square on white and put the only controls in two 12px mono captions at its bottom corners.
moves: gallery-wall margin around a live canvas
false-colour grass: yellow sky, green blades

title: Memory Work | Possible futures of women’s labour
name: Memory Work
one_line: Ten-minute audio scenario about women's labour in 2038 Toronto, then a scroll-down illustrated future city.

look.type: Title assembled from several Glyphworld display fonts so every letter differs (pixel stairs, floral, blobby); Authentic Sans body in tiny spaced caps near 10px.
look.color: Full-screen yellow-green to violet to blue mesh gradient with a cream title; ink #140024, lavender #d8d5f1, accent chips #71c6ff #8af38a #f2fc72.
look.layout: Centred stack of title, play button, progress bar and caption; ruled top bar with menu, logo and clock; sections scroll beneath.
look.imagery: Drifting teal specks over the gradient; later sections carry 56 images (5 GIFs) and Lottie animation.

behaviour: Play starts the soundscape; the top-right clock shows today's real day and time but with the year hard-coded to 2038; scrolling after listening reveals the city.
signature: A live clock that shows your actual day and time stamped with the year 2038.
why: The first screen asks for one action (play, eyes closed) and sets the premise with one altered number, so the future feels like somewhere you already are, not a pitch.
steal: Fake the future with one changed field: show the real date and time with a different year, and gate all content behind a single play button.
moves: real-time clock with the year fixed to 2038
title built letter by letter from different glyph fonts

title: Ana Montiel
name: Ana Montiel
one_line: Artist portfolio whose home is a blurred wavy colour field with a few bright rectangles floating on it.

look.type: Garamond-like serif at 20px for name and nav, split by thin vertical bars, 'Thought & Process' in italic; today's CSS names Nitti Grotesk.
look.color: White ground; peach, pink, butter-yellow and slate-blue gradient field; tiny saturated rectangles in magenta, cyan, green and yellow.
look.layout: Name left, four nav items right on one line; the blur form runs full height down the centre, bleeding off top and bottom.
look.imagery: A heavily blurred vertical wave graphic with soft outlines, no caption; five or six hard-edged coloured rectangles as accents.

behaviour: Cargo template. The capture shows an unlabelled artwork as the home; today the home is a plain list of series titles with About, PDF, Exhibitions, Words, Contact.
signature: Navigation floats over an unlabelled blurred artwork: the art is the homepage, not a thumbnail of it.
why: Soft blur against crisp serif type and tiny sharp rectangles creates depth with two image treatments; leaving the work unlabelled lets visitors read it as a mood before any list.
steal: Open on one full-height blurred artwork with a handful of hard-edged rectangle accents and let a single serif nav line sit on top.
moves: one-line serif nav with bar separators

title: CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts
name: CCA Wattis Institute
one_line: Art institute homepage written as one scattered sentence where only punctuation and link underlines show at first.

look.type: Times-style serif near 24px for the white-on-white sentences, Monaco black for punctuation marks, Helvetica caps near 10px for the foot menu; '.+*' logo.
look.color: White page, black ink; words are white-on-white in the capture, so only black punctuation and link underlines show; red (#ff0000, #e60073) is for news.
look.layout: Sentence fragments float in blocks 10-34% wide, alternating left and right with irregular padding; a looping knot GIF sits centre; menu at the foot.
look.imagery: One hand-drawn knot-line GIF and tiny social icons; otherwise no images.

behaviour: animatePunctuation.js animates the punctuation marks (200ms delay); a colour-class toggle can flip text black or white (mechanism unclear); /?random replays the site one sentence at a time in random order.
signature: Only commas, dashes and link underlines show in the capture, so you read the page's rhythm before its words.
why: Showing punctuation alone turns the grammar of the text into a pattern and rewards a second look, while link underlines announce what is clickable; one script gives a serious institution a signature gesture.
steal: Write your homepage as one sentence split into floated blocks of varied width and style its punctuation as separate animated marks, so structure shows before content.
moves: punctuation marks as the visible layer
?random mode reads one sentence at a time
knot GIF as the sole image

title: Decentralise
name: Decentralise (Somerset House)
one_line: Participatory archive toolkit: pick a category and an object from Somerset House's past, then draw with it.

look.type: Extra-condensed black display caps about 120px for the title; tiny all-caps grotesk near 12px for instructions; heavier sans in yellow outlined pills.
look.color: Signal green main field, magenta and orange side panels, cloud-sky photo blurs; yellow pills outlined in black; all type black.
look.layout: 200px left rail of stacked coloured panels (Brush, Inventory, Categories) ruled in black; wide green stage with title, three-step oval diagram and Start.
look.imagery: Blurry-edged sky photographs, scalloped and semicircular category stickers, outlined step ovals, a sound-off icon.

behaviour: Pick a category and an object, draw over it with a brush; sound toggle plays drawing jams; inventory panel collects objects. Domain no longer connects.
signature: A three-oval instruction flow (pick a category, pick an object, draw) floating on flat signal green.
why: Colour blocks double as tool panels, so the interface explains itself before any reading: each panel colour is a mode. Pill labels with black outlines make every control look like a pressable sticker.
steal: Give each tool panel its own flat colour and a pill-shaped outlined label; explain the flow with three ovals and arrows rather than a paragraph.
moves: condensed title overlapping a cloud photo

title: untold stories
name: untold stories
one_line: Numbered series of design stories; each page sets its own ground and ink, here orange on black.

look.type: Huge book serif title near 110px; same serif at 17px for the intro, then Courier Prime paragraphs at 15px; real italics and superscripts.
look.color: Black ground with a single orange ink (#fe7128) for every word and caption; the photographs supply all other colour.
look.layout: Thin white top bar (home, i, arrows, counter, social); centred title block; two columns below, text left, cover and manuscript photos right.
look.imagery: Book cover and fore-edge photographs plus a medieval manuscript spread, captioned in the same orange serif.

behaviour: Top bar pages through stories as 'untold story 6/23' with arrows; each story's header carries data-color-background and data-color-text attributes that set its own pair.
signature: A top-bar counter (untold story 15/27) turns the site into a numbered deck of one-colour pages.
why: One ink on black makes every photograph the only other colour on the page, so mixed content stays coherent; swapping the pair per story adds variety without changing the system.
steal: Store a background and text colour pair on each page, render everything including captions in that one ink, and add 'n/total' paging in a thin top bar.
moves: per-story colour pair via data attributes
serif plus Courier inside one ink
white top bar as the only neutral

title: Reed Enger, history and design
name: Reed Enger
one_line: Designer-writer's homepage: a hairline-ruled grid of seven line-drawn illustrations with no text above the fold.

look.type: None visible in the capture; the CSS names IowanOldSt old-style serif and Public Sans, with sizes pinned to 17-18px.
look.color: White ground with black 1px rules and outlines only; no fills and no accent colour.
look.layout: Irregular ruled grid of seven cells sharing rules, inset about 30px from the viewport edge; each drawing centred in its cell.
look.imagery: Mesoamerican masks, a rainbow serpent, a pictogram figure, figurines and a site plan, all in uniform 1px outline.

behaviour: Three of the six images in today's 6 KB page are GIFs, so some cells likely animate; otherwise static, no JavaScript.
signature: Illustrations drawn in the same 1px line as the grid rules, so images and layout are one drawing.
why: Matching stroke weight between content and container removes the usual frame-versus-picture hierarchy, so the page reads as a catalogue plate. With no colour, the subject matter carries the personality.
steal: Convert images to outlines at the same stroke weight as your grid rules and let cells share borders, so picture and layout are one line drawing.

title: IDS SPRING 2021
name: Cooper Union IDS (Spring 2021)
one_line: Lecture-series site on black: hairline-boxed nav cells, a stripe-to-grid texture, speakers listed by date.

look.type: Wide-set grotesk in ALL CAPS: about 20px for nav and names, 11px for body and dates; one weight plus a bold subtitle.
look.color: Pure black ground with white 1.5px rules and text; no accent here (the Fall edition inverts to warm grey with black lines).
look.layout: Left 415px column of bordered cells (logo, five stacked nav buttons beside a glyph box, description, themes, scroll bar); right column: centred speaker list.
look.imagery: Line-only ID monogram and loop glyph; white rule stripes resolving into a square lattice; no photography.

behaviour: Static in the capture. A SCROLL button with a down arrow cues the page; the loop glyph and rule texture may animate (unclear). The domain no longer resolves.
signature: A 'SCROLL ↓' tab sits above a hairline texture that goes from stripes to a square lattice.
why: Every region is a bordered cell, so the layout reads like an instrument panel; all-caps text needs no hierarchy beyond size. Texture drawn from the same rules ties identity to the grid.
steal: Draw every block as a bordered cell with 1.5px white rules on black, set all text in caps at two sizes, and make decorative texture from the same rules.
moves: nav buttons stacked as a ruled column

title: “a concise biographical sketch depicting a personality by vivid outlining and sharp contrast”
name: umhi.xyz (Seán)
one_line: Personal hub: a dotted box of arrow-links beside a washed-out photo, plus platform names marked active or dusty.

look.type: Small lowercase monospace near 13px throughout; arrows as link markers, tiny kaomoji and superscript glyphs as punctuation; grey for dormant items.
look.color: Near-white ground, charcoal text, mid-grey for dormant links; the faded blue-white photograph is the only colour.
look.layout: Centred 775px block: dotted-border text box left, photo right at equal height, link rows beneath; wide empty margins above and below.
look.imagery: One overexposed film-style photo of a person on a hillside, a hand-drawn scribble sigil over the head.

behaviour: Static in the capture; each arrow item opens a sub-page (life situation, interests, credits, neighbourhood map). The live page timed out, so current status is unclear.
signature: Platform accounts sorted into '(active)' and '(dusty)' rows: a profile that admits abandoned accounts in grey.
why: Honest labelling of what is alive turns a link dump into a small confession; the box states what it contains, so a visitor knows the cost of each click.
steal: Open with a box that says 'this small box contains:' above a plain list of arrows; mark stale links 'dusty' in grey instead of deleting them.
moves: one washed-out photo as the only colour

title: S A L L Y T H U R E R
name: Sally Thurer
one_line: Art director's portfolio: a bio paragraph buried under a drop-shadowed pile of posters and 3D renders, with checkbox nav.

look.type: Geometric sans near 28px for the bio with blue underlined links; nav in 24px caps beside hand-ticked checkbox glyphs in blue ink.
look.color: White ground and link blue; all other colour comes from the artwork: chrome, acid yellow, a red-white-blue flag, lime slime.
look.layout: Four checkbox items across the top; below, the bio column with images piled on it at random offsets, overlapping each other and the text.
look.imagery: 3D chrome hands, magazine covers, posters, a Frenchie in sunglasses, a winged TV; every item with a heavy soft shadow.

behaviour: Checkboxes toggle layers (WORK and ABOUT ticked, SLIME and CONTACT unticked); a winged-TV sprite hovers top left. The domain now shows a DreamHost 'Site not found' page.
signature: The navigation is four real checkboxes: each ticked section is a visible layer in the pile.
why: Checkboxes show the page's state at a glance, so nothing hides behind a click and layers can combine. Large soft shadows let heavy image stacking read as a desk rather than a mess.
steal: Use checkbox-style controls as navigation where each ticked item adds a layer to the same page; give piled images large soft drop shadows.

title: Maxim Leyzerovich
name: Maxim Leyzerovich (round.is)
one_line: Designer's page, once a wall of…'men at work' signs; now three centred paragraphs.

look.type: No text in the capture; today Repro sans at weight 325, 1em, -0.015em tracking, in a 30em column with medium-blue links.
look.color: White ground; yellow-and-black diamond signs on a regular lattice; today black text on white, links mediumblue turning blue on hover.
look.layout: Capture: a 30 by 30 grid of identical icons filling the viewport; today a centred 30em column with a 2em logo above.
look.imagery: One repeated road-sign pictogram (a figure shovelling), pixel-aligned like wallpaper.

behaviour: Static in both versions; today's 4 KB page is a single HTML file with one font file, one logo image and no scripts of its own.
signature: An entire homepage that is one repeated under-construction sign, filling the screen as wallpaper.
why: Repetition turns a tiny icon into texture, and the joke lands without a word: a designer's site is permanently under construction. One icon, one tile, no code.
steal: If the site isn't ready, tile one 'under construction' icon across the whole viewport as wallpaper instead of apologising in text.
moves: single icon tiled as page wallpaper
today: centred 30em column in a light variable sans

title: Garden with Insight
name: Garden with Insight
one_line: Software page for an educational garden simulator, in plain 1990s HTML with captioned screenshot strips.

look.type: Browser-default Times at 16px with bold h3 headings and no CSS; the bitmap screenshots carry all the visual interest.
look.color: Pale yellow body background, grey hr rules, tan table cells behind screenshots, green links; no stylesheet.
look.layout: One full-width column: intro, then three tan tables each holding a row of four captioned thumbnails; small green icon top right; hr between sections.

look.color: White field; colour comes only from the posted photos (forest greens, sky blues) and tiny pixel-art flowers.
look.layout: Free canvas: photos of every size overlap at random positions with soft drop shadows; one instruction card near centre.
look.imagery: Ferns, trees and low-poly landscapes as photos, plus a cluster of tiny pixel-art plant icons.

behaviour: React canvas app with realtime signals; custom move, grabbing and delete cursors let you drag or remove images; one input adds content; localStorage.
signature: A tiny hand-drawn egg creature stands on a shared white field of plant photos beside the card 'Please post images of plants.'
why: One plain request turns a collage tool into a shared ritual; hand-drawn controls, pixel icons and soft shadows make it feel like a collective sketchbook rather than an app.
steal: Give a participatory canvas a single instruction in a rounded white card, hand-draw the zoom controls, and let content overlap with soft shadows on plain white.
moves: drag and delete cursors as tools

title: Future Corp London
name: Future Corp London

signature: The translation is the design: English on white and French on chartreuse, identical lists side by side.
why: Showing both languages at once turns a language toggle into a colour split; one tiny tracked size and one neon make a studio feel precise with zero imagery.
steal: Show two languages in two side-by-side colour fields with identical line breaks; set everything in one small tracked uppercase size and use a single neon against white.

look.layout: Two-row nav on a column grid; the glyph is centred and huge; the essay is set on named CSS grid areas.

behaviour: Gatsby site with swup page transitions and a typed-text effect; driven by 369 CSS custom properties; skip-to-content link.
signature: A giant letter drawn as its Bezier skeleton, white points and handles on flat blue, like a blueprint of the typeface.
why: Showing a letter's construction is the foundry's craft statement; one flat colour, hairline strokes and 11px nav give spec-sheet precision, so the type is the only image.
steal: Draw your hero glyph or logo as its skeleton (outline, anchor points, handles) in white hairlines on one flat saturated blue; keep nav at 11px.

signature: A bordered white card of small light type floats over a loud rainbow poster with a giant black letter behind it.
why: The gradient is the whole identity and stays loud because long copy is lifted onto a white card; light extended type keeps black text calm against the colour.
steal: Put long text on a 1px-bordered white card over a full-bleed gradient; keep the poster loud and crop the logotype behind the card.
moves: white text card over gradient poster

signature: A poem whose caption is its own arithmetic: fifteen words, 23 syllables, 40,320 orderings.
why: A tiny combinatorial rule produces a finite universe a reader can feel; flat colour and one serif leave nothing between the reader and the lines.
steal: Publish a constraint-based piece with its numbers as the subtitle (words, syllables, permutations); one flat colour, one serif, mono labels in two corners.

why: Treating a font as a tile set turns type design into building with blocks; showing every control and shortcut in plain, dense labels signals a serious, scriptable tool.
steal: For a tool, show the whole control surface at once in a dense numbered panel with shortcuts printed in the labels (t / ESC, b, h); skip onboarding.

why: The collective's contributions are literally placed in space, and using Are.na as the CMS lets any student add a blob with no code; the sky ground makes it atmospheric.
steal: Use a feed as your CMS and scatter its blocks across a larger-than-viewport field that pans with cursor: grab; give the field a photographic sky ground.

steal: Write the page as one sentence: set small images and form inputs inline at text height, and reveal full-size images in a hover popover that tracks the cursor.

steal: To make a circular marquee, repeat your phrase on an SVG textPath around a scaling ellipse and animate startOffset; repeat enough text that the tail never shows.

why: The metaphor is the navigation: ghosted next-layer text promises depth, the instruction is written into the first layer, and keyboard plus button make peeling effortless.
steal: Stack responses as layers, show the next one as low-contrast ghost text behind, and advance with one labelled button plus the down-arrow key; explain it in layer one.

why: Setting type vertically and adding glow and blur gives it speed and physical presence; a one-blue, one-white palette says 'sky' with no imagery besides clouds.
steal: Rotate a welcome line 90 degrees, add text-shadow bloom and a directional blur on a sky-blue field, and move the second column at a different speed.
moves: sky and clouds as the ground

title: Blackout Poetry Generator
name: Blackout Poetry Generator
one_line: A generator that shows a public-domain poem with most words blacked out in red bars, leaving found poetry.

look.type: Helvetica/Arial ~15px, all red, letterspaced; bold title and italic author; header in caps ~18px over a hairline rule.
look.color: Bone #f0e9e5 ground; one red (#e00) for text, bars, borders and rules.
look.layout: Centred ~400px column under a full-width ruled header; poem at top, button below; ruled footer 'made by emmad'.
look.imagery: Solid red bars replace words; no images.

behaviour: Loads a poem (The Waning Moon, Shelley), covers most words with bars and leaves a few; 'Another Poem' loads the next. Glitch hosting has ended (410).
signature: The 'Another Poem' button drawn as three stacked offset outlines, a deck of cards you take from.
why: One red does everything, so bars and surviving words feel like the same ink; the button's stacked outlines suggest a pile of poems rather than a generic action.
steal: Use a single ink colour for text, redaction bars, borders and rules, and draw the primary button as three offset outlines to imply a deck.

title: ATV, drone, elbil, elsykkel, rc helikopter, ATV, robot, elatv
name: Arngren.net
one_line: Norwegian gadget and electric-vehicle catalogue crammed edge to edge with 400+ product photos, boxed offers and mixed-colour links.

look.type: Arial in every size from 10 to 36px and every colour: bold green and red headers, blue links, underlines, tiny prices like 'kr. 998,-'.
look.color: White page with navy-bordered boxes, yellow notices, red 'Nyhet!' tags; green, blue and red links code the categories.
look.layout: Nested tables and absolutely positioned boxes tile the page like a classified-ad grid; index column left, offers in bordered cells.
look.imagery: 417 product photos and 244 animated GIFs (go-karts, drones, tanks, robots) plus a cartoon of the owner as logo.

behaviour: Old catalogue: category links, a hit counter (since 07.11.2004), a search box; no viewport tag and no responsive layout.
signature: Density as identity: every pixel sold to a product, with the proprietor's cartoon face and a flying car in the header.
why: It never apologises: trust comes from the clutter (a real shop with real stock) and a price in every cell; boxes and colour make a huge inventory scannable in the mail-order tradition.
steal: If the business is a huge range, show it all: bordered cells with photo, name and price, colour-coded category links, and a face in the logo.
moves: hit counter as proof of age

title: In-Depth Guide to the Best Free Fonts
name: BWT: Guide to the Best Free Fonts
one_line: Curated guide to open-source typefaces where each specimen sets jazz album titles or fashion quotes in the face, on black.

look.type: Light calligraphic italic heading ~48px; heavy italic caps wordmark; specimens in the face itself (Space Grotesk ~56px) with a tiny bold caption.
look.color: Light grey #efefef page, white top bar, black specimen cards; pastel red, sage, slate, ochre and pink blocks behind phrases.
look.layout: Centred heading, then full-width black cards each with a centred specimen and a one-line caption naming face and designer.
look.imagery: No images; coloured text-background blocks are the only decoration.

behaviour: Next.js: tabs for Serif, Sans-Serif, Display, Monospaced and Pairings; every specimen is an h1 in its own face; RSS feed available.
signature: Specimen text is borrowed culture (Sun Ra album titles, a fashion quote about black) instead of pangrams, each phrase on its own colour block.
why: Real sentences show how a face behaves in meaningful copy, and colour chips under phrases show rhythm and line breaks; the curator's taste becomes the product.
steal: Replace lorem ipsum in a specimen with a quote you love, set each phrase on its own flat colour block, and caption with face and designer in 11px bold.

title: Wremena | Typefaces of The Temporary State
name: Typefaces of The Temporary State: Wremena
one_line: Cyrillic-Latin type foundry page showing Wremena at 16, 32, 64 and 128px in four ruled columns.

look.type: A Times-like serif (Wremena Regular) in white at 16, 32, 64 and 128px; captions 10.5px grotesk; control panel in 16px system sans.
look.color: Pure black ground, white type and 1px white column rules; nothing else.
look.layout: Five equal columns split by hairlines: four scale samples, each clipped at its column edge, and a right column holding the menu.
look.imagery: A circular emblem: 'TYPEFACES OF THE TEMPORARY STATE' set around a closed eye with lashes.

behaviour: JS-rendered (Django app, domain since moved to type.tmpstate.net); a select picks the family and weight (Light, Regular, Bold); links to free fonts and a PDF specimen.
signature: One line set at four sizes in four hairline columns, each clipped at its edge, so scale is shown by what no longer fits.
why: Cutting text at the column edge turns the size ladder into a visible comparison of how much fits; with only black, white and hairlines, the typeface is the only thing to judge.
steal: Show a type scale as four equal columns split by 1px rules, the same sample at 16, 32, 64 and 128px, overflow clipped, a 10px label above each.
moves: controls in a quiet side column
circular wordmark with an eye emblem

title: A guide to custom cursors in Webflow | Webflow Blog
name: Webflow Blog: custom cursors guide
one_line: Webflow Blog tutorial on custom cursors, headed by a blue duotone hero with cursor, cart and plus icons.

look.type: Graphik-like grotesk: white ~48px medium title, ~20px subtitle; nav ~16px; the meta line in tiny letterspaced mono caps.
look.color: Duotone navy and teal-blue (#1f2c7a, #234c78) over a beach photo; white type; black CTA button; white page chrome.
look.layout: Header bar, then a bordered hero panel built from overlapping tinted rectangles with the title at lower left; a sticky '#MadeInWebflow' tag bottom-right.
look.imagery: A beach photo (sunglasses on a towel) in one-colour duotone; thin line icons of a cursor, cart and plus.

behaviour: Tutorial on Webflow Interactions plus one line of custom code to follow the mouse. The blog is since redesigned inside Webflow's new platform nav (GSAP, Three.js).
signature: A duotone photo cut into tinted rectangles with line-icon cursors floating on it: the article's topic as a poster.
why: One hue across photo, blocks and icons unifies mismatched stock imagery; the icons stand in for the cursor states being taught, so the hero is the lesson in miniature.
steal: Duotone a stock photo into one blue, overlay darker tinted rectangles, and draw the topic's icons as thin line art on top.

title: ITP Thesis Archive - Thesis showcase of NYU TISCH ITP 2020 Grads
name: ITP Thesis Archive 2020
one_line: NYU ITP 2020 thesis showcase: giant scrambling letters over an outlined '2020', then a scrolling row of project thumbnails.

look.type: Bold Helvetica caps ~180px for the scrambled letters; thin outlined '2020' about 400px tall behind; ~18px bold grey caps titles, light grey caps categories.
look.color: White ground; black letters and thin grey outline numerals; the thumbnails bring the colour (rainbow blob, orange, blue).
look.layout: Headline band fills the top two-thirds; a ruled bar holds 'ITP Thesis Archive 2020' and 'EXPLORE'; below, a row of equal portrait thumbnails.
look.imagery: Student project stills in 1px grey frames: a pixel apple, chrome 3D shapes, a rainbow bear, a bookcase.

behaviour: JS-rendered (p5 canvas, WordPress shell; the live page shows an empty body, and the site moved to itp.nyu.edu). The headline letters look mid-scramble, settling into a word; EXPLORE opens the grid.
signature: Random capitals tumbling over an outlined 2020, so the year is both backdrop and title.
why: Outlined numerals make a giant but quiet backdrop, so bold scrambled type can sit on top at full contrast; the thumbnail row under the fold promises the content immediately.
steal: Set the year as huge outlined numerals in light grey, put bold black headline letters on top, and start the content row right under the fold.
moves: ruled bar with title and EXPLORE

title: The Bureau of Push Notifications
name: The Bureau of Push Notifications
one_line: Satirical public-service page about push notifications: a huge custom-type title, reassuring headlines and curved links.

look.type: Geometric display ('Fugue') ~150px mixing caps and lowercase, with a Z-shaped S; Arial caps ~32px headlines; Arial ~20px body in a narrow column.
look.color: Peach #ffc8aa ground; one orange-red #ff5100 for all type and the footer bar; strictly two tones.
look.layout: Three reassurance headlines across the top, a giant title below overlapping a narrow text column at left, curved links in both upper corners.
look.imagery: None; type only, with arc-set labels 'Click: The Inquiries' and 'Click: The Experience' rotated around the corners.

behaviour: Static GitHub Pages site with CSS rotate and spin keyframes; the corner links ride arcs; the footer reads 'Sponsored by'; body text deliberately collides with the title.
signature: Three soothing all-caps 'notifications' (IT IS OK - YOU ARE DOING GREAT) across the top like banners above a giant stencil-like title.
why: The look copies a public-service pamphlet crossed with a notification badge; one peach and one orange make a single-voice parody, and the collision of text and title shows pressure rather than polish.
steal: Write the page as the thing it mocks: three short reassuring all-caps lines at the top, a giant custom-type title below, in two tones of one hue.
moves: links set on arcs in the corners

title: Feedhack Download
name: FeedHack
one_line: Landing page for a collaborative video-chat tool for VJs and artists, drawn with RGB-split line art on charcoal.

look.type: Fira Mono-style monospace: ~24px white headline, ~14px grey body; thin light sans 'FEEDHACK' logo.
look.color: Charcoal #232329 ground, grey text; cyan and red copies of every line offset like chromatic aberration.
look.layout: Text column at centre-left, a large generative line drawing filling the right, quotes bottom-left, a one-line footer.
look.imagery: Vector line art: ridge-like polylines in cyan, red and blue around a rotated outlined 'FEED HACK' mark.

behaviour: Static landing page (domain gone) for a multiplayer video chat with screenshare, webcam, VJ and music; open source (AGPLv3), source promised 'sometime in May'.
signature: The logo mark and the line drawing are both rendered in two misregistered colour copies, so everything looks like a signal with a glitch.
why: One drawing technique (1px lines with an offset duplicate) serves logo, illustration and quote marks, so the tool's glitchy collaborative nature shows before any copy is read.
steal: Draw illustrations and the logo as 1px lines, duplicate each a few pixels off in cyan and red, and do the same to outlined quotation marks.
moves: misregistered cyan and red line copies
mono text beside generative line art

title: Visual Communication
name: Visual Communication ZHdK
one_line: Zurich University of the Arts design department's project index: ruled headings, year filters and a staggered grid of student work.

look.type: Neue Haas Grotesk at three sizes: 24px menu and project titles, ~48px heading, 16px names; filters in grey.
look.color: White page, black type, thick black rules; grey filter text; images on black or grey backdrops supply the only colour.
look.layout: Three-column masonry with titles hanging under uneven image heights; 2px black rules frame the 'Projekte' heading and the filter row.
look.imagery: Student work shot on plain grey or black backdrops: books, screens, installations, hands at a table.

behaviour: Isotope-style filtering by year or type (2011-2019, BA-Diplom, MA-Diplom) with an x to clear; Leaflet, canvas and GSAP elsewhere on the site; German interface.
signature: Filters live in a ruled strip under the heading (years and degree types in grey), and the grid below never changes its frame style.
why: Neutral type and a grid with uneven rows let very different projects dominate; consistent backdrops and one text style make 400+ items read as one archive.
steal: Between a ruled heading and a masonry grid, put one line of grey filter words; keep titles at 24px medium with names at 16px under each image.
moves: grey filter words with a clear control

title: REKKI
name: REKKI
one_line: Supplier-ordering app homepage built as a bar chart of colour tiles (download, contact, careers) under a huge wordmark.

look.type: Light grotesk (Diatype-like) wordmark ~210px; lowercase ~32px column headings; ~18px tile labels with an arrow at the right.
look.color: Pale grey #f0f0f0 ground; three flat fields: green #00684a, blue #0063e1, amber #ffb300; black wordmark.
look.layout: Three columns of tiles at different heights like bars, anchored to the bottom edge; wordmark top-left, intro text top-right.
look.imagery: A grey circle ('watch our film Lights Out') balanced on a black pictogram table at bottom-left; no photos.

behaviour: Every tile is a link (iPhone, Android, talk to the team, four career areas with open-position counts). Today it is a Framer site on black with an 'office robots' pitch.
signature: Navigation arranged as a bar chart: tiles of different heights stacked from the bottom, labelled with open-position counts.
why: Flat colour tiles with the label bottom-left and an arrow bottom-right make large, obvious targets with no icons; the staggered heights give a skyline that feels like a chart of the company.
steal: Build a CTA grid of flat colour tiles in different heights, bottom-aligned, each labelled bottom-left with an arrow bottom-right and a live count.
moves: tiles arranged as a bar chart

title: Creating an interactive SVG metro map with JointJS - Netvlies
name: Netvlies: SVG metro map with JointJS
one_line: Dutch agency's tutorial on building an interactive SVG metro map with JointJS, headed by a grey-tinted transit map.

look.type: DIN-like grotesk (Circular Std today): ~40px medium title, 18px body, 20px sidebar nav in white on dark.
look.color: Dark brown-black #2b2523 sidebar, white article; grey-tinted map with red, blue, green, purple, orange and yellow lines; magenta badges.
look.layout: Fixed left sidebar nav; hero map image; byline, title and text in a ~650px column; a cookie panel across the top.
look.imagery: An SVG metro map: coloured routes at 45-degree angles, dotted alternates and station ticks.

behaviour: Walks through the build: JointJS paper as the SVG canvas, nodes and links for lines and stations. Cookie wall on top, chat bubble bottom-right; site since rebuilt on Nuxt.
signature: The hero is the output of the tutorial: a real transit-style map drawn in SVG, in subway colours and 45-degree turns.
why: Showing the finished artifact as the header sells the technique before explaining it; transit-map conventions are a visual language readers already know.
steal: Lead a tutorial with the actual output cropped full-width and let the title sit under it; use the real colours of the thing you built.

title: Max Kaplun - Home
name: Max Kaplun
one_line: Designer's portfolio whose opening bio is one big sentence with logos, boxed wordmarks and handwritten asides standing in for words.

look.type: Light high-contrast display serif ~55px for the bio; inline grotesk caps and heavy wordmarks; tiny tilted handwritten notes; 12px nav.
look.color: Black on white only; colour is left to the brand logos and the project images below.
look.layout: One ~800px paragraph at tight leading, a hand-drawn arrow from the 'updated Dec 2019' note, then 'Selected Works' lower down.
look.imagery: Employer and project logos set inline as words: SSENSE, Dynamic/MTL, ONE&ALL, workmode, Young Guns, N10.AS.

behaviour: Readymag page (the live page shows 2 words, so the shot is the evidence): boxed 'Get in touch' button ends the last line; hand-drawn arrows point into the text and down.
signature: A bio paragraph where the logos of the things they run sit in the sentence in place of their names.
why: Sentence flow makes a resume read like prose, and swapping names for logos makes the page visual without breaking the line; tags like '2014-NOW' and '(CANADA)' in handwriting add voice.
steal: Write your bio as one sentence at 50px+ and drop each client or project logo in place of its name, with a tiny handwritten date above it.
moves: boxed button inside the last line

title: Max Kaplun - Home
name: Max Kaplun (second save)
one_line: Duplicate Are.na save of Max Kaplun's Readymag portfolio; the screenshot is identical to #856.

look.type: Same as #856: light display serif ~55px for the bio sentence, with grotesk wordmarks and tilted handwriting.
look.color: Black on white; logos and project images provide the only colour.
look.layout: Same as #856: one paragraph, hand-drawn arrows, Selected Works below with a stencil-serif 'GOODEE' project mark.
look.imagery: Inline logos and wordmarks used as words, plus the first project title in large type.

behaviour: Readymag shell with 2 words from the static page, so motion is unverified; boxed 'Get in touch' button and hand-drawn arrows, as in #856.
signature: Logos in place of names inside one long bio sentence, as in #856.
why: Same idea as #856: prose flow plus logo-as-word makes a resume visual without breaking the line.
steal: Write the bio as a sentence and replace each client name with its logo at text height, adding tiny handwritten dates above.
moves: boxed button inside the last line

title: Tutorial - Creating an Interactive SVG map - Parallax
name: Parallax: interactive SVG map tutorial
one_line: Agency tutorial on drawing an interactive SVG map of the UK, under a violet mono nav and vertical logo.

look.type: Light geometric grotesk (Matter) ~56px centred title; mono ~14px for nav, byline and Contact; vertical wordmark in a squared rounded display face.
look.color: White page, charcoal #2a2a2a title, one violet (#7b4de0) for logo, nav accents, byline, badge and icons.
look.layout: A 90-degree rotated logo on the left edge, an evenly spaced mono nav across the top, centred byline and title, social icons stacked bottom-left.
look.imagery: None above the fold; the article is expected to show an SVG map of the UK below.

behaviour: Static tutorial page; the current nav item (Blog) is underlined in violet and Careers carries a count badge. Since rebuilt on Webflow with a cookie wall.
signature: The wordmark runs vertically up the left edge in violet, with all chrome in mono, leaving the title alone and large.
why: Mono micro-type for chrome and a single hue make navigation recede; the empty space around a light title makes the article feel important.
steal: Put the logo on the left edge rotated 90 degrees, set nav in mono in one accent colour, and let a light 56px title float alone above the fold.
moves: vertical logo at the left edge

title: Carolyn Zhang
name: Carolyn Zhang
one_line: Designer's portfolio on powder blue where…'work' label are tilted images laid over big serif sentences.

look.type: Light Didone-style serif ~48px with tight tracking for the sentences; brush-pen name and 'work' as rotated images; email in small serif.
look.color: Powder blue-grey #d6dce4 ground, black ink, white brush 'work'; grey social icons.
look.layout: Wide left margin; paragraphs in a ~480px column; handwritten labels rotated about -25 degrees overlapping the text's top-left; icons stacked top-right.
look.imagery: Brush-pen lettering PNGs with a faintly visible box edge; the rest is type.

behaviour: Static scroll of first-person paragraphs, each introduced by a handwritten label. Today it is rebuilt on Notion/Super with a new bio.
signature: The handwritten 'CAROLYN ZHANG' signature drops onto the first paragraph, colliding with the printed type.
why: Handwritten labels over refined serif text give a personal voice without clutter; the overlap shows the signature was added by hand, not typeset.
steal: Pair a light high-contrast serif with brush-pen images for section labels; tilt them 20 to 25 degrees and let their tails overlap the first line of text.

title: YOU MIGHT FIND YOURSELF
name: You Might Find Yourself
one_line: A Tumblr of poems, film and book notes (Tarkovsky, mushrooms) in a narrow two-column theme with ruled date headers.

look.type: Arial-style small sans: ~12px body, bold caps post titles, letterspaced bold caps dates, italic commentary, ~9px meta.
look.color: White page, black and grey type; a black crow and a colour photo are the only images; a 3px black rule under each date.
look.layout: Left sidebar (crow, photo, ruled link list) and a ~390px post column; each post opens with a thick black rule over a thin grey one.
look.imagery: A small crow illustration, a Tea People iced-drink photo, an embedded video still of an old mushroom picker.

behaviour: Standard Tumblr theme: relative dates ('1 month ago'), tags, notes count, timestamp and permalink on one tiny meta line. Today the site returns 403.
signature: Dates as small spaced caps over a thick black rule, with a poem set in its original line breaks and a bookish ledger tone.
why: Restraint and small type suit slow reading: the double rule gives each post a clear start, and a quiet long poem feels at home on a printed page.
steal: Begin each post with the date in spaced bold caps over a 3px black rule and a 1px grey rule; set poems in the author's line breaks at 12-13px.
moves: thick plus thin rule date headers
poem in the original line breaks
tags, notes and timestamp on one meta line

title: does this seem more professional?
name: Molly Soda: does this seem more professional?
one_line: Artist Molly Soda's site as a collage of girl-internet ephemera: doll GIFs, webcam grids, YouTube results and overlapping windows.

look.type: No designed type: 11px file names under GIFs, default blue link lists, YouTube and Vimeo UI text, a yellow pixel caption inside a black window.
look.color: White ground overrun by pink, red, yellow and sky-blue web media; a yellow tote bag; a hot-pink banner (#ff00b3) today.
look.layout: Free-placed layers (HotGlue-style) overlapping at all angles: scattered thumbnails, list columns, windows, crawling-ant and cobweb GIFs.
look.imagery: Dozens of dancing-doll GIFs, a Vimeo grid of 40 webcam faces, a Street View frame, pixelated hair, balloon videos.

behaviour: Free placement: layers overlap, animated GIFs run, YouTube and Vimeo embeds play. Today a Next.js page with a hot-pink scrolling marquee ('I take direction well...') plus CV, Blog, YouTube, Vimeo.
signature: Raw file names and platform UI left visible: the site is a heap of the exact media that shaped the artist's persona.
why: Nothing is polished away: showing GIF file names, a stray ad ('Lamp or Woman?') and real YouTube chrome documents a culture on its own terms, and the density reads as honesty, not mess.
steal: Treat found media as the layout: paste thumbnails with their raw file names, overlap windows from other platforms, and let default blue link lists sit among them.
moves: GIF list in default link blue
marquee banner as the CV intro

title: Publish Something Online
name: Publish Something Online
one_line: A 20-item resource library on making web things, split into blue tag chips and a ruled white table.

look.type: Times-like serif ~18px for titles and chips; ~12px mono for header meta, column heads and domains; roman numerals for level.
look.color: Left half pure blue #0000f0 with white outlines and text; right half white with black text and one blue link for the author.
look.layout: 50/50 vertical split: chips centred on blue; right a table with SUBJECT and LEVEL columns, dotted row rules and a solid rule under the heads.
look.imagery: No images; glyph icons (asterisk, list mark, arrow) precede each title and roman numerals mark difficulty.

behaviour: Tag chips filter the library (pills for level, rectangles for topic); rows split into 'subject' and 'external resource' sections. The domain is now a parked page.
signature: Two chip shapes encode two kinds of tag: rounded pills for level, rectangles for topic, on a flat blue field.
why: Shape-coding the filters needs no legend; a saturated blue field beside a white document keeps tool and content distinct, and level as roman numerals avoids more colour.
steal: Split the screen: a saturated field holding filter chips in two shapes, and a white mono-headed table of results with dotted row rules and roman-numeral levels.

title: Mana Records
name: Mana Records
one_line: Record label catalogue as a flowchart: black release boxes joined by thin lines, by year, on grainy cobalt.

look.type: Unica-style grotesk in white caps ~14px inside boxes; ~12px year labels; descriptions ~13px; nothing larger.
look.color: Cobalt blue #2b3bd6 photographic ground with white cloud specks; black boxes and pills with white text; a navy diamond for a side item.
look.layout: Three columns for 2017, 2018 and 2019; boxes stacked and linked with elbow connectors; format pills beside each; footer line at bottom centre.
look.imagery: A blue satellite-like photo of sea and cloud with film grain, fixed behind; a black blob logo top-left.

behaviour: SVG connectors link the releases; a mobile list reveals each long description; Bandcamp-powered audio; a commented-out three.js shader scene hints at a moving background.
signature: A catalogue as a family tree: releases are nodes, lines show the label's lineage, formats are black pills.
why: A node-link diagram says these records belong together and in an order, which a grid of covers cannot; one deep blue plus black UI makes sparse boxes feel like objects on a chart.
steal: Show a discography as a flowchart: black rectangles with catalogue number, artist and title, elbow lines linking related releases, and oval pills for formats.

title: Portfolio Starter
name: Portfolio Starter
one_line: Open-source starter kit for static portfolio sites, demonstrated by a GIF typing the site's own front matter.

look.type: Inter ~16px for nav and intro; the hero GIF is bold monospace ~32px in teal with visible middle dots for spaces and a block caret.
look.color: White page; mint #e8f4f1 hero box with teal #18bfa5 type and dark-green keywords; black and white Muybridge photos.
look.layout: Thin header, name left and links right; ~460px intro; ~620px hero; below, a full-bleed project grid of small, medium and large blocks.
look.imagery: An animated GIF of typed markdown front matter; sample projects use Muybridge horse-motion sequences and similar archival photos.

behaviour: Pure static HTML with zero JavaScript: lazy images, project blocks in three sizes, an RSS feed; the poster GIF performs the typing.
signature: The hero is a GIF of someone typing the page's own front matter, with whitespace shown as pale teal dots.
why: Showing the source that produces the page teaches the tool in five seconds; visible spaces and a caret make code feel like content, and the plain chrome proves the claim of lightweight.
steal: Demonstrate a developer tool with a looping GIF of the source being typed in a pastel box with whitespace made visible, above the real output.
moves: GIF of the source being typed
three block sizes in the grid

title: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
one_line: A museum homepage built from stacked marquee rows of giant headlines with thumbnails set inline like words.

look.type: Union grotesk caps ~85px for headlines; hairline-outlined caps for 'THE COLLECTION'; small red caps lead-ins ~28px; 'Search' and 'Menu' ~22px.
look.color: White rows divided by 4px black rules; one red #d62348 for labels (OPENING ON APRIL 25); art thumbnails supply all other colour.
look.layout: Full-width stripes each with its own text and thumbnails, cropped by the viewport edge; a row of outlined buttons breaks the rhythm.
look.imagery: Small exhibition thumbnails (painted heads, a hanging concrete slab, hay, a performance) at line height inside the sentences.

behaviour: CSS tickers (move-ticker: translate 0 to -50%) slide each row sideways on a loop, with duplicated content so the loop has no jump; skip links and reduced-motion support.
signature: Every headline is a marquee and every image is a word: a ticker of exhibition titles with thumbnails inline.
why: Turning the whole fold into tickers shows everything on at once without carousel clicks; line-height thumbnails read like emoji in a sentence; 4px rules give the motion a rigid frame.
steal: Stack six rows divided by 4px black rules; in each, loop a CSS ticker of giant caps and line-height thumbnails; reserve one red for small labels.

title: 2727.today | Home
name: 2727 California Street
one_line: Berkeley art and residency initiative whose homepage is a ruled butter-yellow dashboard: nav cells, live weather and a month calendar.

look.type: Browser-default Times throughout: ~30px intro, ~20px nav, italic subtitles in colour cells; no web fonts.
look.color: Butter yellow #fdfbd5 with 1px black rules, a saturated yellow #ffdd44 panel, and five muted cells: blue, khaki, green, terracotta, rose.
look.layout: A framed box grid: hand-drawn logo cell, intro cell, nav row, five coloured section cells, then a today panel beside a month calendar.
look.imagery: Hand-drawn crayon '2727' numerals as the logo; hand-drawn social icons; a pale-yellow sun disc beside the weather.

behaviour: Shows today's date and weather ('Clear, 64 F') and a month calendar with…'s events. Since rebuilt on Squarespace.
signature: A homepage that is a table of the day: date, local weather and a calendar on the first screen, ruled like a graph-paper notebook.
why: Showing what is happening today (and the weather) tells a visitor to a physical place whether to come by; browser serif and thin rules make dense information look handwritten and calm.
steal: Open with a live 'Today is...' panel showing date, weather and a month calendar with dots for events; build it in default serif and 1px rules.

title: Adam Ho
name: Adam Ho
one_line: Portfolio of a left text menu and a fan of tilted colour cards; today a 50-level XP showcase that reshuffles.

title: Placevalue Ascii Playground

one_line: Typed formula x*x*y*y is evaluated at every cell and one decimal place of it is printed as asterisks.

look.type: Black monospace asterisks at about 12px fill the entire page; the control panel uses the same mono plus default blue underlined links.
look.color: Pure black asterisks on white; a white controls card with a faint grey rounded edge; default #0000ee links.
look.layout: Edge-to-edge character grid; a small controls modal floats top-left listing keys and six numeric fields.
look.imagery: None: mosaic, letter-like tilings made only of asterisks and gaps.

behaviour: Advances every 100 ms by default; keys c pause, j/k change place value, drag shifts x/y offset, shaking a phone toggles controls. Glitch hosting ended (410).
signature: One typed formula becomes dense, letter-like mosaics out of nothing but asterisks.
why: Maths becomes texture, and each dial (formula, place value, offset, speed) changes the pattern predictably, so exploring feels like turning knobs instead of reading code.
steal: Give a full-screen character grid a formula field and three or four numeric dials; bind keys and drag to them and let people watch it run.
moves: formula field drives a full-page ASCII grid
j/k keys step the place value
drag to offset x and y

steal: Bind one typographic property (letter-spacing, weight, slant) to a real data series, tick it every 100 ms, and let the sentence's meaning justify the motion.

name: Ngaio Parr
one_line: Artist-curator's black-screen hero: a wide bold wordmark with an asterisk, and two corner links, Index and About.

look.type: Dia (wide humanist grotesk), bold near 60px for 'Ngaio* Parr'; 16px bold links in the bottom corners.
look.color: Pure black with off-white (~#f5f5f5) type; today's page adds sienna, lime #d5e351, mauve #7a5c83 and cream sections further down.
look.layout: A single centred line on a full-screen black field; Index bottom-left and About bottom-right.
look.imagery: None on the hero; the page below carries 554 images, 23 gifs and the 'Some Things' newsletter.

behaviour: The asterisk resolves to a footnote, '*You say it Nigh-Oh', further down the page; Webflow build with a newsletter sign-up and an index of work.
signature: The name carries an asterisk that pays off as a pronunciation footnote: '*You say it Nigh-Oh'.
why: A tiny typographic gesture does the work of a bio: it answers the question every visitor has, shows personality, and gives a plain wordmark a hook.
steal: Add an asterisk to the hard-to-pronounce part of your name and put the footnote in plain words lower on the page.

title: Ryan Morrison, Designer
name: ryry.io
one_line: Design manager's one-column page: a pixel-stretched 'ryry' wordmark, an 'Under construction' stamp and three ruled link lists.

look.type: Inter bold near 14px for body and underlined links; an extremely stretched bitmap 'ryry' wordmark about 350px wide; wavy orange 'UNDER CONSTRUCTION' caps.
look.color: White page, black type, one hazard orange-red (~#e8532a) stamp; nothing else.
look.layout: A left-aligned 400px column: stamp, role line, wordmark, bio, then SOCIALS, BRAGS and INTERVIEWS, each a tiny caps label over a 1px rule.
look.imagery: No photos; the stretched pixel wordmark and the doubled, rotated stamp are the graphics.

behaviour: Today the domain serves a Vite and React page titled 'Ryan Miyoshi' with cursor-follow and drag; the screenshot shows the earlier static column.
signature: A stretched pixel 'ryry' logotype under a doubled, tilted 'UNDER CONSTRUCTION' stamp: unfinished on purpose.
why: Declaring the page under construction removes the pressure of polish and becomes the charm; the hierarchy is just three sizes and rules, so it stays instantly usable.
steal: Use three text sizes, tiny caps section labels over 1px rules and one loud stamp; let a deliberately stretched logotype be the only decoration.
moves: caps label plus 1px rule for list sections
brags and interviews as link lists

title: Glenn Ingdahl - Designer / Illustrator
name: Glenn Ingdahl
one_line: Illustrator's near-black homepage: a centred intro and four services flanked by two mirrored, cropped hot-pink line characters.

look.type: Work Sans light near 40px for the intro; extended bold caps near 20px for services; 12px tracked grey caps for corner nav.
look.color: Near-black (~#0a0a0a), white type, one hot pink (~#ff0066) for the line drawings and fills.
look.layout: Nav in four corners and top centre; intro and services stacked on the centre axis; characters cropped by the left and right edges.
look.imagery: A naive line-drawn big-headed figure seated with a raised hand, outlined in pink with a solid pink sleeve, repeated mirrored.

behaviour: A chevron at the bottom signals scroll; Work and Play are separate sections; today the domain returns a Cloudflare DNS error (1001).
signature: The same hand-drawn figure appears twice, flipped, leaning in from both edges as if listening to the headline.
why: Symmetry and one hot colour on near-black make a calm, memorable stage; mirrored cropping suggests a character larger than the screen, and the drawing does the talking.
steal: Draw one character in a single bright line colour, crop it at the viewport edge, and mirror it on the other side of centred text.

name: hyumankind
one_line: Product designer's portfolio: a heavy extended-sans bio sentence with coordinates, then phone-mock case studies.

look.type: Raveo Display-style black extended sans near 55px for the bio; Suisse/Arial near 12px nav with missing-glyph boxes after each word; 32px bold case titles.
look.color: White ground, black type, grey Microsoft link, green bounding box in the phone mock; today a darker build (#080909 and #f4f4ee).
look.layout: Left-aligned statement at a wide left margin; pager dots at the right edge; alternating text and device-mock sections; nav top-right.
look.imagery: An iPhone mock showing a data-labelling camera UI with a green box labelled 'Hand'.

behaviour: Today's page is a Webflow redesign using GSAP ScrollTrigger and Splitting text; the screenshot shows an earlier light build.
signature: The bio sentence at poster weight, with 'Microsoft' greyed and badged by an inline circled arrow so the employer reads as a link.
why: Weight and width carry the personality while the layout stays plain; inline link styling (grey word plus circled arrow) signals interactivity without underline clutter.
steal: Set the bio in an extra-wide black face near 55px and style linked words as a grey word plus a circled-arrow chip.
moves: inline link chip (grey word plus circled arrow)
pager dots on the right edge
